title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
江以西大郡十餘蓋古荆揚
之域云自廬陵南豐諸君子
卓然以古文詞名家而江右
之文遂重天下其後鹿洞鵞
湖之間相與考道講業學士
復靡然趨之一變而爲性命
===
之學流風遺敎至于今未艾
也
明興二百年來通儒碩輔往往出
其間而解士
制額亦較佗藩爲獨盛豈不謂好
學有文斌斌多材賢之國哉
維岳不佞心嘗鄉往之矣乃
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序
江以西大郡十餘，蓋古荆、揚之域云。自廬陵、南豐諸君子卓然以古文詞名家，而江右之文遂重天下。其後鹿洞、鵞湖之間，相與考道講業，學士復靡然趨之，一變而爲性命之學。流風遺敎，至于今未艾也。明興二百年來，通儒碩輔往往出其間，而解士制額亦較佗藩爲獨盛。豈不謂好學有文、斌斌多材賢之國哉？維岳不佞，心嘗鄉往之矣。乃
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

West of the Yangzi River there are more than ten great prefectures, which formed part of the ancient domains of Jing and Yang. Ever since the worthy gentlemen of Luling 廬陵 and Nanfeng 南豐 stood out as renowned masters of ancient-style prose and diction, the literature of Jiangxi (Jiangyou 江右) has been held in high esteem throughout the realm. Thereafter, at the White Deer Grotto (Ludong 鹿洞) and Goose Lake (Ehu 鵞湖), scholars investigated the Way and lectured on their studies together; men of learning once again flocked to follow them, transforming the tradition into the learning of human nature and destiny. Their lingering influence and bequeathed teachings have not abated even to this day. In the two hundred years since the rise of the Ming, comprehensive Confucians and great ministers have frequently emerged from among them, and the imperially established quota for provincial graduates (jieshi 解士) is also uniquely large compared to other provinces. Could one not call this a land fond of learning and possessed of culture, resplendently abundant in men of talent and worth? Unworthy as I, Weiyue 維岳, am, my heart has long yearned toward it. Now…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆丙子秋天下當大比士
巡按江西監察御史張簡走
幣四方徵維岳與敎諭鄭卿
爲考試官李道焞諸嶠陳傑
薄思忠姚一新姚光虞馮季
兆郭應翰曾傳段公衮爲同
考試官以布政司左布政使
===
朱梀右布政使何子壽提調
之按察司副使魏體明李臺
監之他百執事畢受約束已
乃進提學副使莊國禎所簡
士幾三千人入棘三試之而
屬維岳等校焉於是維岳始
獲縱觀夫此邦賢士之文以
punctuated: 萬曆丙子秋，天下當大比士。巡按江西監察御史張簡走幣四方，徵維岳與敎諭鄭卿爲考試官，李道焞、諸嶠、陳傑、薄思忠、姚一新、姚光虞、馮季兆、郭應翰、曾傳、段公衮爲同考試官，以布政司左布政使朱梀、右布政使何子壽提調之，按察司副使魏體明、李臺監之。他百執事畢受約束已，乃進提學副使莊國禎所簡士幾三千人，入棘三試之，而屬維岳等校焉。於是維岳始獲縱觀夫此邦賢士之文，以
translation_en: … In the autumn of the bingzi year of the Wanli reign (1576), the empire was due to hold the triennial examinations to select scholars. The Regional Inspector of Jiangxi and Investigating Censor Zhang Jian 張簡 dispatched ceremonial gifts in all directions, summoning me, Weiyue, and the Instructor Zheng Qing 鄭卿 to serve as Examiners, and Li Daodun 李道焞, Zhu Qiao 諸嶠, Chen Jie 陳傑, Bo Sizhong 薄思忠, Yao Yixin 姚一新, Yao Guangyu 姚光虞, Feng Jizhao 馮季兆, Guo Yinghan 郭應翰, Zeng Chuan 曾傳, and Duan Gonggun 段公衮 to serve as Associate Examiners; while of the Provincial Administration Commission, Left Administration Commissioner Zhu Lai 朱梀 and Right Administration Commissioner He Zishou 何子壽 acted as Proctors, and of the Provincial Surveillance Commission, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Wei Timing 魏體明 and Li Tai 李臺 acted as Monitors. After all the other functionaries had received their instructions and regulations, the nearly three thousand scholars selected by the Education-intendant Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhuang Guozhen 莊國禎 were admitted into the examination compound to be tested in three sessions, and Weiyue and his colleagues were entrusted with grading them. Thereupon I, Weiyue, was first able to read extensively the writings of the worthy scholars of this region, so as to …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
快其所嘗嚮往之志遵故事
拔儁九十五人授御史以
獻是九十五人者業已稱儁無論
已即其他並舉爭驅者大抵
擷藝籍之餘芬究性道之眇
緒殆人人能也夫江右士之
閒於文學固以生諸君子之
後雅化使然而至於今其亦
可謂極盛矣雖然維岳於諸
士竊願有言焉昔者孔子喟
周末之文欲從先進且不輕
以君子與篤論蓋文詞之不
足多也如此方
今承恬襲熙操觚之士盈於宇內
punctuated: 快其所嘗嚮往之志。遵故事，拔儁九十五人，授御史以獻。是九十五人者，業已稱儁無論已，即其他並舉爭驅者，大抵擷藝籍之餘芬，究性道之眇緒，殆人人能也。夫江右士之閒於文學，固以生諸君子之後，雅化使然，而至於今，其亦可謂極盛矣！雖然，維岳於諸士，竊願有言焉。昔者孔子喟周末之文，欲從先進，且不輕以君子與篤論，蓋文詞之不足多也如此。方今承恬襲熙，操觚之士盈於宇內，
translation_en: … gratify the aspiration I had long cherished. In accordance with precedent, we selected ninety-five men of outstanding talent and delivered their names to the Censor for presentation to the throne. Setting aside these ninety-five who have already been acclaimed for their excellence, even among the others who competed alongside them, almost everyone was capable of gathering the lingering fragrance of the literary and canonical texts and probing the subtle threads of human nature and the Way. That the scholars of Jiangxi are so well-versed in literature and learning is surely the result of refined transformation from being born after those great gentlemen of the past; and down to the present day, it may indeed be called the height of flourishing! Even so, I, Weiyue, venture to have a word for the scholars. In antiquity, Confucius sighed over the cultural refinement of the late Zhou and wished to follow the men of former times; moreover, he did not lightly grant the title of gentleman merely on the basis of earnest discourse. Such is the extent to which literary words alone are not worth prizing! At present, inheriting an era of peace and tranquility, scholars who wield the writing tablet fill the realm, …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
琱章綴辭日趨於浮巧而渾
厚悃幅之意顧若少衰憂世
者鰓鰓欲亟輓之然則有司
者敢謂今日之文爲盡足以
得士而諸士亦可自多其文
之舉於有司云爾哉且凡有
司所爲舉士上之毗
===
主匡時次之展采錯事又其下不
失爲廩廩質行之流乃其文
直羔雉爾吾無暇遠引第卽
子鄉往哲論之彼其倡明性
命者豈徒以談辯相雄長要
皆操行修潔晰義利於秋毫
歐陽子號文章家而其歎昔
punctuated: 琱章綴辭，日趨於浮巧，而渾厚悃幅之意顧若少衰，憂世者鰓鰓欲亟輓之。然則有司者敢謂今日之文爲盡足以得士，而諸士亦可自多其文之舉於有司云爾哉？且凡有司所爲舉士，上之毗主匡時，次之展采錯事，又其下不失爲廩廩質行之流，乃其文直羔雉爾。吾無暇遠引，第卽子鄉往哲論之：彼其倡明性命者，豈徒以談辯相雄長？要皆操行修潔，晰義利於秋毫。歐陽子號文章家，而其歎昔
translation_en: … carving out phrases and stringing together words, daily trending toward superficial cleverness, while the spirit of substantial depth and sincere integrity seems on the contrary to have somewhat declined; those who worry for the world are anxiously eager to swiftly reverse this trend. Such being the case, how dare the authorities claim that today's literary compositions are entirely sufficient for selecting worthy scholars, and how can you scholars pride yourselves merely on having your essays recommended by the authorities? Moreover, in all cases where the authorities recommend scholars, the highest aim is that they will assist the ruler and rectify the times; the next is that they will display their talents and manage affairs; and at the very least, that they will not fail to be men of reverent caution and honest conduct—whereas their literary compositions are merely like the ceremonial lamb and pheasant used as gifts of introduction. I have no leisure to cite distant examples, so let us simply discuss the past sages of your own home province: those among them who championed and elucidated human nature and destiny—how could they have vied for supremacy merely through empty talk and disputation? In essence, they were all cultivated and pure in conduct, distinguishing rightness from profit down to the finest autumn hair. Master Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) was renowned as a master of literary prose, yet when he lamented how men of the past…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
人之工文章者至儗之木榮
之飄風鳥音之過耳考其禔
身事主道德勳業咸炳炳可
稱述此所謂有本之言而有
用之文也諸士果能景行前
修潛心實踐異日隨牒而吏
即以其言徇職下則庶幾哉
===
不愧言不辱舉而江右士益
重矣若第操空文游詞以梯
榮媒進旣卽敝帚視之則
國家廣厲博采之謂何無亦偭
先資而負
上意乎夫選士稱掄材尚矣荆揚
之貢寔惟杶栢篠簜登諸職
punctuated: 人之工文章者，至儗之木榮之飄風、鳥音之過耳；考其禔身事主，道德勳業咸炳炳可稱述，此所謂有本之言而有用之文也。諸士果能景行前修，潛心實踐，異日隨牒而吏，即以其言徇職下，則庶幾哉不愧言，不辱舉，而江右士益重矣。若第操空文游詞以梯榮媒進，旣卽敝帚視之，則國家廣厲博采之謂何？無亦偭先資而負上意乎？夫選士稱掄材，尚矣。荆揚之貢，寔惟杶栢篠簜，登諸職
translation_en:
…those in the past who excelled at literary composition, going so far as to liken their works to blossoms on trees scattered by the wind or the calls of birds passing by the ear; yet when one examines how he conducted himself and served his sovereign, his moral integrity and meritorious achievements were all brilliantly worthy of praise. This is what is meant by words with a solid foundation and writing of practical use. If you scholars can truly emulate the worthy men of the past and devote your minds to putting these principles into actual practice, so that in the future, when you receive your commissions and take office, you apply your words to the fulfillment of your duties, then you may well not disgrace your words nor bring shame upon your recommendation, and the scholars of Jiangxi will be held in even greater esteem! If, on the other hand, you merely wield empty prose and floating rhetoric as a ladder to glory and a medium for advancement, only to cast them aside like a worn-out broom once you have succeeded, then what would be the meaning of the state's broad encouragement and wide selection of talent? Would that not be turning your backs on your initial pledge of service and betraying the Emperor's intentions?

Now, referring to the selection of scholars as the choosing of timber is of great antiquity. The tribute from Jing and Yang consisted in fact of chun-cedar, cypress, and small and large bamboos, which were recorded in the Direction…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
方而漢以豫章名其郡蓋材
藪也諸士亦知夫材乎適棟
而棟適桷而桷輻湊竝運以
共
天府乃若曼理竅衷不中繩斧卽
扶疎百尋之木將作氏且不
汗棄之謂無適也然則飾文
===
===
鮮實之士何以異此蓋古之
諸侯貢士于天子任之而任
亦曰適不適則譴訶及焉今
主上明聖方將修
舊典以掄眞材凡我諸士尚懋戒
之其無使有司者抵不適之
咎哉是舉也先巡撫江西右
punctuated:
方，而漢以豫章名其郡，蓋材藪也。諸士亦知夫材乎？適棟而棟，適桷而桷，輻湊竝運，以共天府。乃若曼理竅衷，不中繩斧，卽扶疎百尋之木，將作氏且不汗棄之，謂無適也。然則飾文鮮實之士，何以異此？蓋古之諸侯貢士于天子，任之而任，亦曰適；不適，則譴訶及焉。今主上明聖，方將修舊典以掄眞材。凡我諸士，尚懋戒之，其無使有司者抵不適之咎哉！

是舉也，先巡撫江西右
translation_en:
… [recorded in the] Office of Operations, and the Han dynasty named this commandery Yuzhang ("Camphorwood"), for it is indeed a reservoir of timber. Do you scholars also understand the nature of timber? What is suited to be a ridgepole serves as a ridgepole; what is suited to be a rafter serves as a rafter. They converge like spokes at a hub and are transported together to supply the Imperial Treasury. Yet if the grain is twisted and the core is hollow, so that it does not conform to the marking-line and axe, then even if it is a spreading tree of a hundred fathoms, the Master of Works will cast it aside without breaking a sweat, saying that it is unsuited for use. How, then, do scholars who embellish their prose yet lack substance differ from this? In antiquity, when the feudal lords presented scholars as tribute to the Son of Heaven, those who proved capable upon being entrusted with office were likewise called "suited"; if they were unsuited, reprimand and censure fell upon the presenters. Now our Sovereign is enlightened and sage, and is just about to revive the old canons to select genuine talent. May all of you scholars diligently take warning, so as not to cause the authorities to incur the blame of presenting what is unsuited!

In this examination, the former Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi and Right …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
副都御史今陞工部右侍郎
楊〔成〕今巡撫右副都御史潘
〔季馴〕提督南贛軍務右副都
御史江〔一麟〕先後保釐相與
宣風猷以厲文敎清軍御史
侯〔堯封〕將
指中度士知嚮方若左參政盧
===
〔仲佃〕右參政陶〔幼學〕侯〔于趙〕
左參議沈〔奎〕副使朱〔茹〕馮〔叔〕
〔吉〕僉事王〔徽猷〕霍〔與瑕〕參將
郭〔堅〕署都指揮僉事胡〔忠〕張
〔榜〕則皆協襄于外右參議王
〔闢臣〕副使王〔象坤〕署都指揮
僉事陳〔道〕以入
賀
punctuated: 副都御史今陞工部右侍郎楊〔成〕、今巡撫右副都御史潘〔季馴〕、提督南贛軍務右副都御史江〔一麟〕，先後保釐，相與宣風猷以厲文敎；清軍御史侯〔堯封〕將指中度，士知嚮方；若左參政盧〔仲佃〕、右參政陶〔幼學〕、侯〔于趙〕、左參議沈〔奎〕、副使朱〔茹〕、馮〔叔〕〔吉〕、僉事王〔徽猷〕、霍〔與瑕〕、參將郭〔堅〕、署都指揮僉事胡〔忠〕、張〔榜〕，則皆協襄于外；右參議王〔闢臣〕、副使王〔象坤〕、署都指揮僉事陳〔道〕以入賀
translation_en: …Vice Censor-in-Chief and former Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works, Yang Cheng 楊成; the current Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Pan Jixun 潘季馴; and the Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Superintendent of Military Affairs in Nan'gan, Jiang Yilin 江一麟, have successively safeguarded and governed the region, joining together to propagate moral influence and administrative plans so as to encourage literary education. The Troop-Purifying Censor Hou Yaofeng 侯堯封 has carried out the imperial instructions with due measure, so that the scholars know the proper direction toward which to strive. As for Left Administration Vice Commissioner Lu Zhongdian 盧仲佃, Right Administration Vice Commissioners Tao Youxue 陶幼學 and Hou Yuzhao 侯于趙, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Shen Kui 沈奎, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhu Ru 朱茹 and Feng Shuji 馮叔吉, Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Wang Huiyou 王徽猷 and Huo Yuxia 霍與瑕, Assistant Regional Commander Guo Jian 郭堅, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Hu Zhong 胡忠 and Zhang Bang 張榜, they all assisted and collaborated from outside the examination compound. Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Wang Pichen 王闢臣, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Xiangkun 王象坤, and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Chen Dao 陳道, who [departed] to enter the capital to offer congratulations…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
賀行按察使金立敬右參政張
士佩以遷秩行皆先與有勞
焉刑部郎中史櫃戶部主事
史繼志周嘉謨程沂中書舍
人姚士觀行人楊四知則皆
以使事至而欣覩其盛者於
法得並書
===
湖廣衡州府桂陽州儒學學
正馮維岳謹序
punctuated:
賀行，按察使金立敬、右參政張士佩以遷秩行，皆先與有勞焉。刑部郎中史櫃，戶部主事史繼志、周嘉謨、程沂，中書舍人姚士觀，行人楊四知，則皆以使事至而欣覩其盛者，於法得並書。

湖廣衡州府桂陽州儒學學正馮維岳謹序。
translation_en:
… departed to present congratulations; and Surveillance Commissioner Jin Lijing 金立敬 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhang Shipei 張士佩 departed upon promotion to new posts; all of them had earlier contributed their labors to the affair. Ministry of Justice Bureau Director Shi Gui 史櫃; Ministry of Revenue Bureau Secretaries Shi Jizhi 史繼志, Zhou Jiamo 周嘉謨, and Cheng Yi 程沂; Drafter Yao Shiguan 姚士觀; and Messenger Yang Sizhi 楊四知 all arrived on official missions and gladly witnessed this grand occasion; according to the regulations, their names may also be recorded together here.

Respectfully prefaced by Feng Weiyue 馮維岳, Subprefectural Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Guiyang Subprefecture 桂陽州, Hengzhou Prefecture 衡州府, Huguang 湖廣.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
萬曆四年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史張簡〔易從直隸靜海縣人戊辰進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使柴淶〔季東光祿寺籍浙江鄞縣人丙辰進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司右布政使何子壽〔康伯錦衣衛官籍山西交城縣人己未進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司副使魏體明〔用晦福建侯官縣籍福清縣人乙丑進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司副使李臺〔國佐浙江壽昌縣人壬戌進士〕
===
考試官
湖廣衡州府桂陽州儒學學正馮維岳〔汝瞻湖廣江陵縣人甲子貢士〕
河南南陽府泌陽縣儒學教諭鄭卿〔上卿山西長治縣人甲子貢士〕
同考試官
山東濟南府章丘縣儒學教諭李道焞〔亨甫直隸濬縣人辛酉貢士〕
浙江衢州府西安縣儒學教諭諸鐈〔鼎臣直隸上海縣人戊午貢士〕
湖廣岳州府澧州慈利縣儒學教諭陳傑〔位卿四川成都縣人戊午貢士〕
福建福州府長樂縣儒學教諭薄思忠〔孝乎浙江錢塘縣人乙卯貢士〕
湖廣承天府京山縣儒學教諭姚一新〔文初浙江慈谿縣人辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
萬曆四年江西鄉試。

監臨官：

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
欲罷不能既竭吾才如有所立卓爾
唯天下至誠爲能化
堯以不得舜爲己憂舜以不得禹臯陶爲
己憂夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
爲天下得人者謂之仁
===
易
天地以順動故日月不過而四時不忒聖
人以順動則刑罰清而民服豫之時義
大矣哉
上九鼎玉鉉大吉无不利象曰玉鉉在上
剛柔節也
天地設位而易行乎其中矣
精義入神以致用也利用安身以崇德也
過此以往未之或知也窮神知化德之
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮，欲罷不能。既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾。

唯天下至誠爲能化。

堯以不得舜爲己憂，舜以不得禹、臯陶爲己憂。夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，爲天下得人者謂之仁。

易

天地以順動，故日月不過，而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！

上九，鼎玉鉉，大吉，无不利。象曰：「玉鉉在上，剛柔節也。」

天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。

精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。過此以往，未之或知也；窮神知化，德之
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books (Sishu)

"The Master is orderly and skillful in leading people forward. He broadens me with learning and restrains me with ritual propriety, so that even if I wished to stop, I could not. Having exhausted all my abilities, it seems as though something stands lofty and firm before me." [Analects 9.11]

"Only the one who possesses the utmost sincerity in the world has the ability to transform." [Doctrine of the Mean 23]

"Yao 堯 made it his personal concern not to find a Shun 舜; Shun made it his personal concern not to find a Yu 禹 and a Gao Yao 臯陶. Now, one who makes it his personal concern that his hundred mu of land are not well cultivated is merely a farmer. Sharing one's wealth with others is called generosity; teaching others to be good is called loyalty; finding the right person for the world is called benevolence." [Mencius 3A.4]

The Classic of Changes (Yi)

"Heaven and earth move in accord, and therefore the sun and moon do not err, and the four seasons do not deviate. The sage moves in accord, and thus punishments and penalties are clear and the people submit. Great indeed is the timely significance of Enthusiasm (Yu 豫)!" [Hexagram 16, Commentary on the Decision]

"Top Nine: The cauldron has rings of jade. Great good fortune; nothing that is not advantageous. The Commentary on the Images says: 'The rings of jade at the top signify that the firm and the yielding are in proper measure.'" [Hexagram 50, Ding 鼎]

"Heaven and earth establish their positions, and Change operates within them." [Appended Remarks, Part I, Ch. 6]

"Refining the meaning to enter into the unfathomable spirit is for the sake of utmost practical application; utilizing things profitably to secure one's person is for the sake of exalting virtue. Beyond this, one cannot know how to proceed; exhausting the spirit and understanding transformation is the [culmination] of virtue…" [Appended Remarks, Part II, Ch. 5]

text:
盛也
書
臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作朕
股肱耳目
浮于積石至于龍門西河會于渭汭
極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
三后協心同底于道道洽政治澤潤生民
詩
七月鳴鵙八月載績
===
我黍與與我稷翼翼我倉旣盈我庾維億
有馮有翼有孝有德以引以翼豈弟君子
四方爲則
宣哲維人文武維后燕及皇天克昌厥後
綏我眉壽介以繁祉
春秋
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕公會齊侯宋
公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯于鹹〔僖公〕
punctuated:
盛也。

書：
臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。」
浮于積石，至于龍門、西河，會于渭汭。
極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。
三后協心，同底于道；道洽政治，澤潤生民。

詩：
七月鳴鵙，八月載績。
我黍與與，我稷翼翼。我倉旣盈，我庾維億。
有馮有翼，有孝有德，以引以翼。豈弟君子，四方爲則。
宣哲維人，文武維后。燕及皇天，克昌厥後。綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。

春秋：
夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于鹹。〔僖公〕
translation_en:
…abundance.

Book of Documents (Shu):
"Ministers! Associates! Associates! Ministers!" Yu said, "Yes!" The Emperor said, "My ministers act as my legs and arms, my ears and eyes."
[Tribute] floated from Jishi, reaching Longmen and the Western River, and met at the bend of the Wei River.
The amplification of the Ultimate in speech: take this as instruction and put this into practice, so as to draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven.
The three sovereigns united their hearts and together arrived at the Way; the Way permeated governance and order, and their beneficence moistened the living people.

Book of Odes (Shi):
In the seventh month the shrike cries; in the eighth month they begin to spin hemp.
Our glutinous millet is abundant, our panicled millet is luxuriant; our granaries are already full, our open-air stacks number in the hundreds of thousands.
Looked to for support and giving aid, possessing filial piety and virtue, to lead and to assist—easy and fraternal is the lord, a model for the four quarters!
Comprehensive in wisdom is the man; civil and martial is the ruler. Giving peace even to August Heaven, he is able to make prosperous his descendants. He comforts us with longevity of prominent eyebrows and aids us withmanifold blessings.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
In summer, the Duke met the Grand宰 (Grand Minister) the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the son of the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. [Ninth year of Duke Xi] The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Xian. [Duke Xi, …]

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
十有三年
春王正月公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕
冬公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十有三年〕
公子遂如楚乞師〔僖公二十有六年〕冬
十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十〕
〔有一年〕
五月公及諸侯盟于臯鼬〔定公四年〕
禮記
天子視學大昕鼓徵所以警衆也衆至然
===
後天子至乃命有司行事興秩節祭先
師先聖焉
故禮也者義之實也協諸義而協則禮雖
先王未之有可以義起也義者藝之分
仁之節也協於藝講於仁得之者强仁
者義之本也順之體也得之者尊
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
punctuated:
〔十有三年〕。
春，王正月，公敗齊師于長勺〔莊公十年〕；冬，公會齊侯盟于柯〔莊公十有三年〕。
公子遂如楚乞師〔僖公二十有六年〕；冬，十月，甲午，叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十有一年〕。
五月，公及諸侯盟于臯鼬〔定公四年〕。

《禮記》
天子視學，大昕鼓徵，所以警衆也。衆至，然後天子至，乃命有司行事，興秩節，祭先師先聖焉。
故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。義者，藝之分，仁之節也。協於藝，講於仁，得之者强。仁者，義之本也，順之體也，得之者尊。
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。如此，則四海之內，合敬同
translation_en:
…[thirteenth year of Duke Xi].
In spring, in the King's first month, the Duke defeated the army of Qi at Changshao [tenth year of Duke Zhuang]; in winter, the Duke met with the Marquis of Qi and made a covenant at Ke [thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang].
Prince Sui went to Chu to beg for troops [twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi]; in winter, in the tenth month, on the jiawu day, Shusun Dechen defeated the Di at Xian [eleventh year of Duke Wen].
In the fifth month, the Duke and the feudal lords made a covenant at Gaoyou [fourth year of Duke Ding].

Record of Rites (Liji)
When the Son of Heaven visits the Imperial School, at dawn a drum is beaten to summon the students, by which the multitude is roused to attention. Only after the multitude has arrived does the Son of Heaven arrive; he then commands the authorities to perform the ceremonies, initiating the regular ritual procedures and offering sacrifices to the Former Teachers and Former Sages.
Therefore, ritual is the substance of righteousness. If a practice is measured against righteousness and found to be in accord with it, then even if such a ritual did not exist under the former kings, it may be instituted on the basis of righteousness. Righteousness is the allotment of the arts and the regulation of benevolence. He who conforms to the arts and cultivates benevolence—and attains righteousness—is strong. Benevolence is the root of righteousness and the embodiment of compliance; he who attains it is honored.
Great music shares the same harmony as Heaven and Earth; great ritual shares the same order as Heaven and Earth. Because there is harmony, the hundred things do not lose their nature; because there is order, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the bright realm of the visible there are ritual and music; in the dark realm of the unseen there are ghosts and spirits. When it is like this, then within the four seas all will unite in reverence and join in…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
愛矣
采蘋者樂循法也采蘩者樂不失職也
第貳場
論
文王朢道未見
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令禮官勸學詔〔元朔五年〕
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元〕
〔和十年〕
===
擬輔臣進文武職名
御屏表〔萬曆二年〕
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
人戶以籍爲定
致祭祀典神祇
軍民約會詞訟
修理橋梁道路
第叄場
punctuated:
愛矣。
采蘋者，樂循法也；采蘩者，樂不失職也。

第貳場
論：
文王朢道未見。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢令禮官勸學詔〔元朔五年〕。
擬唐以裴度爲中書侍郎同平章事誥〔元和十年〕。
擬輔臣進文武職名御屏表〔萬曆二年〕。

判語〔五條〕：
官員赴任過限。
人戶以籍爲定。
致祭祀典神祇。
軍民約會詞訟。
修理橋梁道路。

第叄場
translation_en:
… affection.
"Gathering Duckweed" (Caipin) is about rejoicing in following the rules; "Gathering White Southernwood" (Caifan) is about rejoicing in not failing in one's duties.

Second Session
Discourse:
"King Wen looked toward the Way as if he had not yet seen it."

Proclamation, Mandate, and Memorial [examinees are to write on one of these]:
Imitation of a Han-dynasty proclamation ordering the ritual officials to encourage learning [5th year of the Yuanshuo era (124 BCE)].
Imitation of a Tang-dynasty mandate appointing Pei Du 裴度 as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery [10th year of the Yuanhe era (815 CE)].
Imitation of a memorial by the Grand Secretaries presenting the imperial screen inscribed with the names and offices of civil and military officials [2nd year of the Wanli era (1574)].

Legal Judgments [five items]:
Officials exceeding the time limit in proceeding to their posts.
Households and population being determined on the basis of the registers.
Offering sacrifices to the deities in the Sacrificial Canon.
Joint adjudication of lawsuits involving military and civilian personnel.
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
策〔五道〕
問帝王所以保命凝圖而建無疆之治者
莫大於敬
天莫要於勤民典謨訓誥所載尚矣我
太祖高皇帝受
天明命肇造函夏
登極之初首舉
郊禋乃有感而作
存心錄以垂訓萬世又
===
詔有司均節財用蠲除租稅至形之
訓諭者每不一而足
列聖相承益隆繼述如
成祖文皇帝之
聖學心法
世宗肅皇帝之
欽天記頌幷勤恤元元者焜燿日星可得而
指陳之與我
皇上天縱聖神
punctuated:
策〔五道〕

問：帝王所以保命凝圖，而建無疆之治者，莫大於敬天，莫要於勤民。典、謨、訓、誥所載，尚矣。我太祖高皇帝受天明命，肇造函夏，登極之初，首舉郊禋，乃有感而作《存心錄》，以垂訓萬世；又詔有司均節財用，蠲除租稅，至形之訓諭者，每不一而足。列聖相承，益隆繼述，如成祖文皇帝之《聖學心法》，世宗肅皇帝之《欽天記頌》，幷勤恤元元者，焜燿日星，可得而指陳之與？我皇上天縱聖神，
translation_en:
Policy Questions (five items)

Question: In the means by which emperors and kings preserve the Mandate, consolidate their rule, and establish boundless good governance, nothing is greater than revering Heaven, and nothing is more essential than being diligent toward the people. What is recorded in the Canons, Counsels, Instructions, and Announcements of the Book of Documents is already of ancient renown. Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu), received the bright Mandate of Heaven and founded the realm of China. At the very beginning of his reign, he first performed the suburban sacrifice; moved by the occasion, he composed the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu) to hand down instruction for ten thousand generations. He also decreed that the authorities equalize and economize on expenditures and remit taxes, expressing this in his instructions and edicts time and again. Successive sacred emperors inherited the throne, ever more grandly continuing and recounting this legacy—such as the Methods of the Mind in Imperial Learning (Shengxue xinfa) of Ancestor-Realizer, Emperor Wen (Chengzu), and the Record and Odes on Revering Heaven (Qintian jisong) of Generation-Honored, Emperor Su (Shizong), together with their diligence and compassion toward the common people, which shine as brightly as the sun and stars. Can you point these out and set them forth? Our August Emperor is endowed by Heaven with sagely divinity, …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
嗣服以來欽崇
天道子惠困窮者至矣乃於去歲躬舉
南郊之典
聖敬昭格且
嘉納輔臣所進
郊禮圖冊邇
戒有司之虛飾憫小民之失所
聖諭復惓惓焉一念
敬天勤民足以光紹
===
二祖而匹休
世宗矣爾諸士涵濡
聖化有年其悉心揚厲以效忠悃于萬一將藉
以轉聞于
上
問聖人法天立政必備一代之典制以昭
示臣民唐虞而上無論已周公夾輔成
王始作周禮經綸精悉後世稱君臣明
聖者必歸焉下此掌故之設會要之編
punctuated:
嗣服以來，欽崇天道、子惠困窮者至矣。乃於去歲躬舉南郊之典，聖敬昭格，且嘉納輔臣所進《郊禮圖冊》；邇戒有司之虛飾，憫小民之失所，聖諭復惓惓焉。一念敬天勤民，足以光紹二祖而匹休世宗矣。爾諸士涵濡聖化有年，其悉心揚厲，以效忠悃于萬一，將藉以轉聞于上。
問：聖人法天立政，必備一代之典制，以昭示臣民。唐虞而上，無論已。周公夾輔成王，始作《周禮》，經綸精悉，後世稱君臣明聖者必歸焉。下此，掌故之設、《會要》之編，
translation_en:
… Since inheriting the throne, his reverent veneration of the Way of Heaven and paternal kindness toward the distressed and impoverished have reached the utmost degree. Moreover, last year he personally performed the ceremony of the Southern Suburb; his sagely reverence brightly reached Heaven, and he graciously accepted the Illustrated Album of the Suburban Sacrificial Rites (Jiaoli tuce) presented by the Grand Secretaries. Recently, he has admonished the authorities against empty pretension and pitied the common people for losing their livelihoods, his sagely edicts repeatedly expressing earnest concern. With this single-minded reverence for Heaven and diligence toward the people, he is fully able to gloriously continue the legacy of the Two Ancestors and match the splendid achievements of Emperor Shizong. You scholars have been steeped in the sagely transformative influence for years; devote your whole hearts to extolling and expounding these matters, so as to offer up a ten-thousandth part of your loyal sincerity, which we shall rely upon to transmit to the scrutiny of His Majesty above.

Question: When the sages modeled themselves on Heaven to establish governance, they invariably prepared the institutional codes of an entire era to clearly instruct their officials and people. Of the eras of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] and earlier, we need not speak. When the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, he first composed the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli); its statecraft was refined and comprehensive, so that when later generations praised enlightened and sagely rulers and ministers, they invariably looked back to them. After this, the establishment of institutional precedents (zhanggu) and the compilation of Essential Documents (Huiyao)…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
代有作者然治化未光自難垂範於後
也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝
神聖御天貽謀深遠
創製諸司職掌一書
列聖世守海内治平嗣我
孝宗敬皇帝熈明撫運加志經制編摩
大明會典傳布中外不知二書意義亦有相孚
合者與抑各有所倣與其中宏綱細目
===
===
可得而聞與修輯
頒行歷更歲時可得而殫述與
世宗肅皇帝纘承先志兩議增續然止及會典
而不及職掌何與玆者
皇上聰睿天授明哲作輔媲美成周此其會也
乃於
朝講之暇宣賁
綸音重修會典然
繼述之中寓化裁之道不知因革損益何者
punctuated: 代有作者，然治化未光，自難垂範於後也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，神聖御天，貽謀深遠，創製《諸司職掌》一書，列聖世守，海内治平。嗣我孝宗敬皇帝，熈明撫運，加志經制，編摩《大明會典》，傳布中外。不知二書意義，亦有相孚合者與？抑各有所倣與？其中宏綱細目，可得而聞與？修輯頒行，歷更歲時，可得而殫述與？世宗肅皇帝纘承先志，兩議增續，然止及《會典》而不及《職掌》，何與？玆者皇上聰睿天授，明哲作輔，媲美成周，此其會也。乃於朝講之暇，宣賁綸音，重修《會典》。然繼述之中，寓化裁之道，不知因革損益，何者
translation_en:
…in every dynasty there were authors who produced them, yet because their governance and moral transformation lacked brilliance, it was naturally difficult for them to hand down a model for posterity.

Thinking grandly of our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, r. 1368–1398): divinely sage, he ruled as Heaven's representative, leaving behind plans of deep and far-reaching foresight. He initiated and compiled the book Statutes for the Charges of the Various Offices (Zhusi zhizhang). Successive sacred emperors observed it from generation to generation, and all within the seas enjoyed peaceful governance. Subsequently, our Emperor Jing, the Filial Ancestor (Xiaozong, r. 1487–1505), governing the dynastic destiny with radiant intelligence, devoted special attention to the regular institutions and compiled the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian), promulgating it inside and outside the court. One wonders whether the purport and principles of these two books correspond with one another, or whether each had its own separate model? Can their overarching framework and detailed entries be heard about? Can the history of their compilation, editing, and promulgation over the course of years and seasons be recounted in full? Emperor Su, the Epochal Ancestor (Shizong, r. 1521–1567), carrying forward the aspirations of his predecessors, twice deliberated on expanding and continuing the work; yet why did this extend only to the Collected Statutes and not to the Statutes for the Charges?

Now, His Majesty the Emperor is endowed by Heaven with perspicacity and wisdom, and brilliant and wise ministers serve as his辅 (assistants); this is the very juncture that rivals the perfection of the flourishing Zhou! Thus, in the leisure from court audiences and classical lectures, he has proclaimed his silken imperial words to order the revision of the Collected Statutes. Yet within the act of inheriting and recounting resides the Way of transforming and tailoring. Regarding what to retain or abolish, and what to diminish or augment, one wonders which matters…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
爲最要與我
皇上之注意此書者其亦有所本與願詳敷陳
以鳴
國家之盛
問天下元元之命係於守令蓋所使承流
宣化者也任顧不重與守令稱良惟漢
世爲盛然稽前史所載僅僅數人可指
而言之與夫吏以良稱宜有奇政可紀
而考其所敘述惟曰謹身率先廉平不
===
苛好爲民興利若斯而已至於投巫鄴
水筩筩發奸三異徵奇五袴詠德者顧
不得與循吏並傳何與豈當時所稱者
專於敦本務實而奇踔非所尚與我
國家重守令之選嚴六事之責法至詳矣
隆卓異之賞厲不職之罰意至勤矣宜乎循
良之風比迹兩漢然猶澤不下究民或
愁嘆而治效罔臻焉豈吏未盡良而設
施之間多飾虛聲與夫悃愊者難知粉
punctuated:
爲最要與？我皇上之注意此書者，其亦有所本與？願詳敷陳，以鳴國家之盛。

問：天下元元之命係於守令，蓋所使承流宣化者也，任顧不重與？守令稱良，惟漢世爲盛，然稽前史所載，僅僅數人，可指而言之與？夫吏以良稱，宜有奇政可紀；而考其所敘述，惟曰「謹身率先」、「廉平不苛」、「好爲民興利」，若斯而已。至於投巫鄴水、筩筩發奸、三異徵奇、五袴詠德者，顧不得與循吏並傳，何與？豈當時所稱者，專於敦本務實，而奇踔非所尚與？我國家重守令之選，嚴六事之責，法至詳矣；隆卓異之賞，厲不職之罰，意至勤矣。宜乎循良之風，比迹兩漢，然猶澤不下究，民或愁嘆，而治效罔臻焉。豈吏未盡良，而設施之間，多飾虛聲與？夫悃愊者難知，粉
translation_en:
… is most essential? And in directing His attention to this compilation, upon what basis does Our Sovereign proceed? We wish you to set forth your views in detail, so as to proclaim the flourishing glory of the State.

Question: The lives of the common people throughout the realm depend upon the Prefects and Magistrates, for they are the ones commissioned to receive the sovereign's grace and propagate his transforming influence—is their responsibility not weighty indeed? For Prefects and Magistrates praised as upright and good, only the Han era is considered the most flourishing; yet when one examines what is recorded in the former histories, there are merely a handful of men—can you point to them and discuss them? Now, when officials are praised as good, one would expect them to have extraordinary administrations worthy of record; yet when we examine what is narrated of them, it says only that they "cultivated their persons and led by example," were "incorruptible, fair, and not harsh," or "delighted in promoting what was beneficial for the people"—nothing more than this. As for those who cast the shamans into the waters of Ye, exposed villainy by means of bamboo ballot-tubes [reading 筩筩 for 筩筒], verified wonders through the "Three Marvels," or had their virtue celebrated in the song of the "Five Pairs of Trousers"—why were they instead not included in the collective biographies of the "Upright Officials" (Xunli)? Could it be that what was praised at the time lay exclusively in attending to fundamentals and striving for practical substance, whereas extraordinary and flamboyant feats were not what was valued? Our State attaches great weight to the selection of Prefects and Magistrates and strictly enforces their responsibility for the Six Duties—the regulations are most detailed; it bestows generous rewards for outstanding merit and applies stern punishments for dereliction of duty—its intention is most earnest. It ought to be that the ethos of upright and good governance would match the footsteps of the Western and Eastern Han; yet blessings still do not penetrate to the bottom, the people at times sigh in distress, and the efficacy of good rule is not achieved. Could it be that the officials are not all good, and that in their administrative measures they mostly cultivate empty reputations? Now, the sincere and unpretentious are hard to recognize, while those who…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
飾者易售兹欲崇實政而黜虛文似又
不專在有司也所以精其藻鑑握其權
衡者伊誰之責與諸士將出而膺是寄
者願悉陳所見以觀用世之學
問利莫大於裕國阜民錢法之興昔人謂
先王以守財物以御人事而平天下乃
美利之自然也自莊山寶開九府軌立
繼是作者紛紛而議者亦人人殊焉有
欲弛盜鑄之禁者有獨專私鑄之利者
===
有下更鑄之令者有罷鑄錢之官者有
聽民鑄大錢者有縱民日銷錢者可得
而言其槩與抑孰得而孰失與夫私鑄
與大錢不便固也變而爲半兩榆莢再
變而爲當千鵞眼等類將以何者爲適
中與七福四美惜銅愛工之說似爲謀
議之當可舉而行之與夫錢以泉稱必
其流通不滯稽古司市外府泉府之掌
出入皆自官導之而民爭趨利厥後皮
punctuated:
飾者易售。兹欲崇實政而黜虛文，似又不專在有司也。所以精其藻鑑、握其權衡者，伊誰之責與？諸士將出而膺是寄者，願悉陳所見，以觀用世之學。

問：利莫大於裕國阜民。錢法之興，昔人謂先王以守財物，以御人事，而平天下，乃美利之自然也。自莊山寶開，九府軌立，繼是作者紛紛，而議者亦人人殊焉。有欲弛盜鑄之禁者，有獨專私鑄之利者，有下更鑄之令者，有罷鑄錢之官者，有聽民鑄大錢者，有縱民日銷錢者，可得而言其槩與？抑孰得而孰失與？夫私鑄與大錢不便，固也；變而爲半兩、榆莢，再變而爲當千、鵞眼等類，將以何者爲適中與？七福、四美、惜銅愛工之說，似爲謀議之當，可舉而行之與？夫錢以泉稱，必其流通不滯。稽古司市、外府、泉府之掌，出入皆自官導之，而民爭趨利。厥後皮
translation_en:
… [while those who] apply superficial window-dressing easily sell themselves. Now, if we wish to exalt substantive governance and dismiss empty formalities, it would seem not to depend solely on the local authorities. On whom, then, rests the responsibility for refining the discernment of talent and holding the scales of judgment? You scholars who are about to go forth and assume these charges: please set forth your views in full, so that we may observe your learning for practical statecraft.

Question: There is no benefit greater than enriching the state and making the people prosperous. Regarding the rise of monetary administration, people of the past said that the former kings used it to safeguard wealth and goods, to regulate human affairs, and to bring peace to the world—it was thus a natural form of admirable benefit. Ever since the treasures of Mount Zhuang were opened and the regulations of the Nine Treasuries were established, those who came after initiated measures in great profusion, and those who debated the matter also differed from one person to the next. Some wished to relax the prohibition against illicit minting; some monopolized the profits of private minting for themselves; some issued orders to remint coins; some abolished the officials in charge of minting; some permitted the people to mint large coins; and some allowed the people to melt down coins daily. Can you give a general account of these? Moreover, which of these succeeded and which failed? Now, that private minting and large coins are inconvenient is certainly true; yet when things changed to "half-tael" (banliang) and "elm-pod" (yujia) coins, and changed again to "worth-a-thousand" (dangqian), "goose-eye" (eyan), and the like, which of these should be taken as hitting the proper mean? The doctrines of the "seven blessings," the "four merits," and "sparing copper and begrudging labor" seem to be sound counsels—can they be taken up and put into practice? Now, coin (qian) is called "spring" (quan) because it must circulate without stagnation. Examining antiquity, under the management of the Director of Markets (sishi), the Outer Treasury (waifu), and the Treasury of Currency (quanfu), both disbursement and receipt were guided by the authorities, and the people eagerly pursued the benefit. Thereafter, with hide…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
幣飛錢天下病焉錢之行阻果在上而
不在下與方
今下鼓鑄之令以貽萬世之利古錢當以何
代爲準
制錢當以何式爲則必如何而後可竝行不悖
與幸詳言之勿讓勿略
問江西距山匯湖當吳楚閩粵之交古重
地也
國家二百年餘其間經略制置爲地方計治
===
安者良旣密矣但桑土之徹亦不可不
講也試與諸生籌之寧新之間重岡複
嶺夙稱盜藪矣邇建議蒐獮分憲臣以
彈壓之誠足以杜竊發也然嘯聚之徒
每乘間焉絕其萌蘖何以處之黃鄉之
洞盤據巢穴久逞桀驁矣邇計處葉酋
設縣治以控制之誠足以綏黨與也然
反側之輩或生心焉圖其善後何以施
之鄱湖匯合三江延袤廣矣而波濤瀰
punctuated:
幣、飛錢，天下病焉。錢之行阻，果在上而不在下與？方今下鼓鑄之令，以貽萬世之利。古錢當以何代爲準？制錢當以何式爲則？必如何而後可竝行不悖與？幸詳言之，勿讓勿略。

問：江西距山匯湖，當吳、楚、閩、粵之交，古重地也。國家二百年餘，其間經略制置，爲地方計治安者，良旣密矣。但桑土之徹，亦不可不講也，試與諸生籌之。寧、新之間，重岡複嶺，夙稱盜藪矣。邇建議蒐獮，分憲臣以彈壓之，誠足以杜竊發也；然嘯聚之徒每乘間焉，絕其萌蘖，何以處之？黃鄉之洞，盤據巢穴，久逞桀驁矣。邇計處葉酋，設縣治以控制之，誠足以綏黨與也；然反側之輩或生心焉，圖其善後，何以施之？鄱湖匯合三江，延袤廣矣；而波濤瀰…
translation_en:
…[white deer-skin] currency and "flying cash" (feiqian), the whole empire suffered from them. Does the circulation or obstruction of coins truly depend on those above rather than those below? Just now, an order to cast coins has been issued so as to bequeath a benefit for ten thousand generations. The coins of which dynasty should be taken as the standard for ancient coins? What model should be taken as the rule for official standard coins (zhiqian)? How must it be done so that both may circulate side by side without conflict? Please speak of this in detail, neither yielding out of modesty nor being cursory.

Question: Jiangxi is bordered by mountains and gathers waters into its lake, standing at the junction of Wu, Chu, Min, and Yue; since antiquity it has been a place of strategic importance. For the more than two hundred years of our Dynasty, the strategic planning and institutional arrangements made during that time to secure peace and order for the region have indeed been thorough. Yet the precaution of "gathering mulberry root-bark [before it rains]" is something that cannot go unexamined; let us deliberate on this with you students. Between Ningzhou and Xinchang, where ridge upon ridge of mountains overlap, it has long been known as a lair of bandits. Recently, proposals were made to hunt them down and extirpate them, assigning a provincial surveillance official to suppress them, which is truly sufficient to prevent covert outbreaks; yet gangs that whistle to gather their fellows still seize every opportunity. To cut off their sprouting buds, how should one deal with this? In the valleys of Huangxiang, bandits have been entrenched in their lairs, long indulging in unruly defiance. Recently, through calculated action against the chieftain Ye, a county seat was established to hold the area under control, which is truly sufficient to pacify his partisans; yet vacillating and rebellious elements may still harbor ulterior thoughts. To plan for post-pacification rehabilitation, what measures should be applied? Lake Poyang receives the confluence of three rivers and stretches over a vast expanse; amid its boundless waves…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
漫匿奸者能逆其不掠商航乎詰其盜
階以肅湖防其策安在九江雄據上游
連接遙矣而舸艦出沒操舟者能保其
悉為良民乎發其隱伏以靖江臯其術
安施夫三營並列衛所隸分將領非不
備也聯以追胥募以精常戎兵非不足
也卒然有警果足恃與說者以為盜之
未弭由於保甲之未嚴然與否與或者
猶欲專責之守令其說然與諸生抱董
===
賈之策將志於匡時矧桑梓邦乎願明
言之無隱
punctuated: 漫，匿奸者能逆其不掠商航乎？詰其盜階以肅湖防，其策安在？九江雄據上游，連接遙矣，而舸艦出沒，操舟者能保其悉為良民乎？發其隱伏以靖江臯，其術安施？夫三營並列，衛所隸分，將領非不備也；聯以追胥，募以精常，戎兵非不足也。卒然有警，果足恃與？說者以為盜之未弭，由於保甲之未嚴，然與否與？或者猶欲專責之守令，其說然與？諸生抱董、賈之策，將志於匡時，矧桑梓邦乎？願明言之，無隱。
translation_en: …are vast and boundless; can one anticipate that hidden malefactors will not plunder merchant vessels? Where does the strategy lie for rooting out the sources of banditry so as to tighten the defenses of the lake? Jiujiang commands a strategic position upstream, with far-flung connections; yet as large boats and warships come and go, can one guarantee that those who crew the vessels are all law-abiding subjects? How should methods be applied to uncover those hiding in ambush so as to pacify the riverbanks? Now, with the three divisions ranged side by side and the Guard and Battalion units divided under their respective jurisdictions, commanders are certainly not lacking in preparedness; linked together by local pursuers and constables, and reinforced by recruited elite regulars, the military forces are certainly not insufficient. Yet if an alarm should suddenly arise, can they truly be relied upon? Commentators hold that the failure to eradicate banditry stems from the lax enforcement of the mutual-responsibility system (baojia)—is this so or not? Others would still place the responsibility solely upon the prefects and magistrates—is their view correct? You students cherish the statecraft strategies of Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 and Jia Yi 賈誼 and aspire to rectify the times—how much more so when it concerns your own native land! Pray state your views clearly and hold nothing back.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
夫子循循然善誘人博我以文約我以禮
欲罷不能既竭吾才如有所立卓爾
王命爵
同考試官教諭姚批此作不浮不俗理致悠然
得顏子歸功聖人之意宜錄以式
同考試官教諭溥批場中作此辭多纏繞唯此
篇刋去陳言直說心髓別於騁浮蔓者矣
===
考試官教諭鄭批思深語到
考試官學正馮批精緻典雅取之
大賢領聖教之善而因以見聖道焉夫博文約
禮顏子所由以見乎道者也此聖人善誘之功
所以為大歟想顏子學既有得而歸功于夫子
也若曰方吾仰鑽瞻忽之時將謂于夫子之道
終無所見矣然不可企而及者道之妙也而其
可循而入者教之善也文有不博或失則陋矣
夫子則先博我以文焉凡所以廓吾聞見之□
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

「夫子循循然善誘人，博我以文，約我以禮，欲罷不能。既竭吾才，如有所立卓爾。」

王命爵
同考試官教諭姚批：此作不浮不俗，理致悠然，得顏子歸功聖人之意，宜錄以式。
同考試官教諭溥批：場中作此，辭多纏繞，唯此篇刋去陳言，直說心髓，別於騁浮蔓者矣。
考試官教諭鄭批：思深語到。
考試官學正馮批：精緻典雅，取之。

大賢領聖教之善，而因以見聖道焉。夫博文約禮，顏子所由以見乎道者也，此聖人善誘之功所以為大歟！想顏子學既有得，而歸功于夫子也，若曰：方吾仰鑽瞻忽之時，將謂于夫子之道終無所見矣。然不可企而及者，道之妙也；而其可循而入者，教之善也。文有不博，或失則陋矣。夫子則先博我以文焉，凡所以廓吾聞見之□
translation_en:
First Session
The Four Books

"The Master, by orderly method, skillfully leads men on. He broadened me with culture and restrained me with ritual. Even if I wished to stop, I could not. Having exhausted all my ability, it is as if something stands right before me, lofty and erect."

Wang Mingjue 
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Yao comments: This composition is neither superficial nor vulgar, and its reasoning flows with leisurely grace. It captures Yanzi's intention in attributing credit to the Sage, and ought to be recorded as a model.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Pu comments: In the examination compound, those writing on this topic mostly produced tangled verbiage. Only this essay trims away hackneyed expressions and speaks directly to the heart and marrow of the matter, setting it apart from those that indulge in superficial and sprawling rhetoric.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng comments: Deep in thought and apt in expression.
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng comments: Refined and classically elegant; select it.

The great worthy appreciates the goodness of the Sage's teaching, and thereby perceives the Sage's Way. Now, broadening through culture and restraining through ritual were the means by which Yanzi came to perceive the Way. Is this not why the Sage's achievement in skillfully leading men on is so great? Imagine Yanzi, having attained understanding in his learning, attributing the credit to the Master, as if to say: When I was first looking up at it, boring into it, gazing before and suddenly seeing it behind, I might have thought that I would ultimately see nothing of the Master's Way. Yet what cannot be reached by straining on tiptoe is the subtlety of the Way, whereas what can be entered into step by step is the goodness of his teaching. If culture is not broad, one may err on the side of narrowness. Thus the Master first broadened me with culture; whatever might expand the [?] of my hearing and seeing…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者何不用也禮有不約或失則泛矣夫子則復
約我以禮焉凡所以養吾德性之能者何不用
也自博以之約而先後不紊由文以之禮而知
行不偏夫子所以誘我者循循然矣夫理本悅
心而復有得于夫子之教其機能自已乎回雖
不敏而苟可以竭請事之力其功庸敢惰乎由
是真積既久則躍如之妙自昭向之彌高彌堅
者恍乎其有定象焉顧諟既專則參前之機自
著向之在前在後者儼然其有定體焉茲固回
===
之竊以自幸者使非夫子誘我焉安能至是哉
觀此而夫子之善教顏子之善學兩見之矣抑
博約之教即虞書惟精惟一之旨此夫子所以
得統于堯舜而授之顏子者也今之學者無見
于知行之相須而强一之乃至混博約之序而
廢格物之條得無以顏子之學如莊周之所謂
墮體黜聰心齋坐忘者耶又烏在其為博文約
禮耶
唯天下至誠為能化
punctuated:
者，何不用也？禮有不約，或失則泛矣；夫子則復約我以禮焉，凡所以養吾德性之能者，何不用也？自博以之約，而先後不紊；由文以之禮，而知行不偏，夫子所以誘我者循循然矣。夫理本悅心，而復有得于夫子之教，其機能自已乎？回雖不敏，而苟可以竭請事之力，其功庸敢惰乎？由是真積既久，則躍如之妙自昭，向之彌高彌堅者，恍乎其有定象焉；顧諟既專，則參前之機自著，向之在前在後者，儼然其有定體焉。茲固回之竊以自幸者，使非夫子誘我焉，安能至是哉？」觀此，而夫子之善教、顏子之善學，兩見之矣。抑博約之教，即《虞書》惟精惟一之旨，此夫子所以得統于堯、舜而授之顏子者也。今之學者，無見于知行之相須，而强一之，乃至混博約之序，而廢格物之條，得無以顏子之學，如莊周之所謂「墮體黜聰、心齋坐忘」者耶？又烏在其為博文約禮耶？
「唯天下至誠為能化。」
translation_en:
… is left unused? If ritual propriety is not restraining, one may err on the side of diffuseness; the Master then further restrains me with ritual propriety, so that among all the means of nourishing the capacities of my moral nature, what is left unused? Moving from breadth to restraint, the sequence of first and last is not confused; proceeding from cultural refinement to ritual propriety, knowledge and action are not one-sided—thus the Master leads me on step by step. Now, principle inherently delights the mind, and when one further gains from the Master's teaching, how could itsvital impulse cease of itself? Although I, Hui, am not clever, so long as I can exhaust my strength in applying myself to this task, how could I dare beremiss in my effort? Through this, once genuine accumulation has continued for a long time, the subtlety that seems to leap forth before my eyes naturally becomes manifest, and what formerly seemed ever higher and ever firmer indistinctly takes on a definite image; once my mindful regard has become focused, the presence that stands before me naturally becomes evident, and what formerly seemed now in front and now behind majestically takes on a definite substance. This is indeed what I, Hui, privately count as my good fortune; had the Master not led me on, how could I have reached this point?" Looking at this, the Master's excellence in teaching and Master Yan's (顏子) excellence in learning are both seen here. Moreover, the teaching of breadth and restraint is none other than the purport of "being refined and being single-minded" in the Book of Yu (Yu shu 虞書); this is the succession of the Way that the Master received from Yao (堯) and Shun (舜) and transmitted to Master Yan. Scholars of today fail to see that knowledge and action depend upon each other and forcibly merge them into one, going so far as to confuse the sequence of breadth and restraint and abandon the item of investigating things. Does this not treat Master Yan's learning as being like what Zhuang Zhou (莊周) called "casting off limb and trunk, driving out perception and intellect, the fasting of the mind, and sitting in forgetfulness"? And where, then, would its "broadening with cultural refinement and restraining with ritual propriety" be?

"Only the one of utmost sincerity in the world is able to transform."

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江楫
同考試官教諭馮批中庸義最難發揮此作體
貼明透而詞更端莊宜錄以式
同考試官教諭姚批理精詞雅體正調高錄式
多士
考試官教諭鄭批博大精詳
考試官學正馮批善發題旨
中庸舉思誠之極功而屬之至誠見其同歸也
甚矣化非至誠不能爲也致曲者而至于化不
===
與至誠同歸哉中庸言人道也若謂誠之在人
所入之途雖異所至之域則同致曲者積而至
于能化矣是化也可以易能哉唯天下之至誠
也天德之備于已者不貳不息既有以端化理
之原斯王道之成于外者不識不知自足以致
無爲之治人心之同然者自吾得之則以吾之
心通天下之心而丕應傒志者熈如焉至誠不
期于物之動而天下亦莫知其所以動矣天命
之本然者自我全之則以我之天觸在人之天
punctuated:
江楫
同考試官教諭馮批：「《中庸》義最難發揮，此作體貼明透，而詞更端莊，宜錄以式。」
同考試官教諭姚批：「理精詞雅，體正調高，錄式多士。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「博大精詳。」
考試官學正馮批：「善發題旨。」
《中庸》舉思誠之極功而屬之至誠，見其同歸也。甚矣，化非至誠不能爲也！致曲者而至于化，不與至誠同歸哉？《中庸》言人道也，若謂：誠之在人，所入之途雖異，所至之域則同。致曲者積而至于能化矣，是化也，可以易能哉？唯天下之至誠也。天德之備于已者不貳不息，既有以端化理之原；斯王道之成于外者不識不知，自足以致無爲之治。人心之同然者自吾得之，則以吾之心通天下之心，而丕應傒志者熈如焉；至誠不期于物之動，而天下亦莫知其所以動矣。天命之本然者自我全之，則以我之天觸在人之天，
translation_en:
Jiang Ji (江楫)

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Feng commented: "The meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) is most difficult to expound. This essay grasps it with clear penetration, and its diction is moreover dignified; it is fitting to record it as a model."
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Yao commented: "Refined in principle and elegant in diction, upright in form and lofty in tone; recorded as a model for the many scholars."
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng commented: "Broad, great, precise, and detailed."
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng commented: "Skillfully brings out the purport of the theme."

The Doctrine of the Mean cites the ultimate achievement of striving for sincerity and attributes it to supreme sincerity, showing that they arrive at the same end. Indeed, transformation is something that none but the supremely sincere can accomplish! When one who cultivates particular shoots of goodness reaches the point of transformation, does he not arrive at the same end as one of supreme sincerity? Speaking of the Way of Man, the Doctrine of the Mean seems to say: As for sincerity in man, although the paths by which one enters differ, the realm that one reaches is the same. One who cultivates particular shoots of goodness accumulates effort until he is able to transform. This transformation—can it be easily achieved? Only by one of supreme sincerity in the world! When the heavenly virtue complete within oneself is without duality and without cease, one already has the means to rectify the source of transformative principle; thus, the kingly way accomplished on the outside, without conscious knowledge or deliberate action, is naturally sufficient to bring about governance through non-action. What is common to human minds is attained by me; thus, through my own mind I communicate with the minds of all under heaven, and those who grandly respond and await my will are harmonious and joyful. One of supreme sincerity does not刻意 expect things to be moved, and the world likewise does not know how it is moved. The original nature of the Mandate of Heaven is kept whole by me; thus, through the Heaven within me I touch the Heaven within others…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
而於變時雍者翕如焉至誠不期于物之變而
天下亦不知其所以變矣一性盡而人物之性
兼成非强也誠精而應妙機固然也一誠立而
天地之功幽賛非勉也誠感而神應道固然也
非天下至誠其孰能與于斯夫唯至誠而始足
以語化致曲者而至于化則亦不異於至誠矣
孰謂天人不相及哉易曰聖人久于其道而天
下化成信斯言也非天下至誠不能化至誠非
久道亦豈易以化哉聖如堯舜豈不謂天下至
===
誠而時雍從欲之治成于在位七十載之餘紹
堯之後則信乎化之必以漸也中庸語天地聖
人之功用而終之以悠久有以也夫
堯以不得舜爲己憂舜以不得禹臯陶爲
己憂夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者農夫
也分人以財謂之惠教人以善謂之忠
爲天下得人者謂之仁
傅一元
同考試官教諭叚批體製高古詞理渾融時義
punctuated:
而於變時雍者翕如焉。至誠不期于物之變，而天下亦不知其所以變矣。一性盡而人物之性兼成，非强也，誠精而應妙，機固然也；一誠立而天地之功幽賛，非勉也，誠感而神應，道固然也。非天下至誠，其孰能與于斯？夫唯至誠而始足以語化，致曲者而至于化，則亦不異於至誠矣，孰謂天人不相及哉？《易》曰：「聖人久于其道，而天下化成。」信斯言也！非天下至誠不能化，至誠非久道，亦豈易以化哉？聖如堯、舜，豈不謂天下至誠？而時雍、從欲之治，成于在位七十載之餘、紹堯之後，則信乎化之必以漸也。《中庸》語天地聖人之功用，而終之以悠久，有以也夫！

堯以不得舜爲己憂，舜以不得禹、臯陶爲己憂。夫以百畝之不易爲己憂者，農夫也。分人以財謂之惠，教人以善謂之忠，爲天下得人者謂之仁。

傅一元

同考試官教諭叚批：體製高古，詞理渾融，時義…
translation_en:
…and thus all are harmoniously transformed and brought to concord. The Possessor of Utmost Sincerity does not consciously aim at the transformation of things, and the world likewise does not know how it has been transformed. Once one's own nature is fully realized, the natures of other men and things are simultaneously fulfilled—this is not by forced effort; rather, when sincerity is pure, the response is wondrous, for such is the natural mechanism. Once utmost sincerity is established, the work of Heaven and Earth is silently assisted—this is not by strained exertion; rather, when sincerity moves, the spirit responds, for such is the natural Way. Apart from the Possessor of Utmost Sincerity in the world, who could participate in this? Now, only with utmost sincerity is one worthy of speaking of transformation; yet when one who pushes partial goodness to the utmost reaches the point of transformation, he too is no different from one who possesses utmost sincerity. Who then can say that the endowment of Heaven and human effort cannot reach the same end? The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "The sage perseveres long in his Way, and all under Heaven is transformed and perfected." True indeed are these words! Without being the Possessor of Utmost Sincerity in the world, one cannot transform; and even with utmost sincerity, without persevering long in the Way, how could transformation be easily achieved? Sages such as Yao and Shun—could they not be called Possessors of Utmost Sincerity in the world? Yet their governance of harmonious concord and of the people following their desires was only accomplished after more than seventy years on the throne, or after succeeding Yao; thus it is truly evident that transformation must proceed gradually. When the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) speaks of the functions and achievements of Heaven, Earth, and the sage, and concludes with endurance and permanence, there is indeed a reason for it!

"Yao made failure to find Shun his own personal sorrow; Shun made failure to find Yu and Gao Yao his own personal sorrow. Now, he who makes the failure to till his hundred mu of land his own personal sorrow is a farmer. Sharing wealth with others is called beneficence; teaching others to be good is called loyalty; finding the right man for all under Heaven is called benevolence."

Fu Yiyuan

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Duan: The style and structure are lofty and antique, the diction and reasoning are seamlessly blended; among contemporary expositions on the Classics, it is…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之絕佳者
同考試官教諭李批說二帝得人以仁天下意
親切有味宜錄以式多士
考試官教諭鄭批理明辭暢可取
考試官學正馮批文思純末
大賢言二帝急於得人而因著其所及之大焉
夫得人以仁天下其所及大矣此堯舜所以以
不得人為憂歟且自古語治道之隆者莫如堯
舜而語憂民之至者亦莫如堯舜推其仁天下
===
之心宜若事事而憂之矣而堯之所以為已憂
者惟以不得舜焉自舜之外非無可憂也舜得
而堯之憂皆舜為之任其責矣堯何憂焉舜之
所以為已憂者惟以不得禹臯陶焉自禹臯陶
之外非無可憂也禹臯陶得而舜之憂皆禹臯
陶為之代其終矣舜何憂焉若夫百畝之不易
此特農夫之憂耳豈堯與舜之所憂哉然是堯
舜之憂也乃所以為堯舜之仁也何也分人以
財惠焉而已惠則有時而窮也非仁也教人以
punctuated:
之絕佳者。
同考試官教諭李批：說二帝得人以仁天下，意親切有味，宜錄以式多士。
考試官教諭鄭批：理明辭暢，可取。
考試官學正馮批：文思純末。
大賢言二帝急於得人，而因著其所及之大焉。夫得人以仁天下，其所及大矣，此堯、舜所以以不得人為憂歟？且自古語治道之隆者，莫如堯、舜；而語憂民之至者，亦莫如堯、舜。推其仁天下之心，宜若事事而憂之矣。而堯之所以為已憂者，惟以不得舜焉。自舜之外，非無可憂也；舜得，而堯之憂皆舜為之任其責矣，堯何憂焉？舜之所以為已憂者，惟以不得禹、臯陶焉。自禹、臯陶之外，非無可憂也；禹、臯陶得，而舜之憂皆禹、臯陶為之代其終矣，舜何憂焉？若夫百畝之不易，此特農夫之憂耳，豈堯與舜之所憂哉？然是堯、舜之憂也，乃所以為堯、舜之仁也。何也？分人以財，惠焉而已，惠則有時而窮也，非仁也；教人以
translation_en:
…an utterly superb example of a contemporary-style explication.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Li comments: Its explanation of how the Two Emperors found worthy men so as to extend benevolence to all under Heaven is earnest, pertinent, and full of savor; it ought to be recorded as a model for the many scholars.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng comments: Its reasoning is clear and its phrasing fluent; it is worthy of selection.
Examiner and Department Director of Studies Feng comments: Its literary thought is pure and [?末].
The Great Worthy [Mencius] speaks of how urgent the Two Emperors were in finding worthy men, and thereby brings to light the greatness of what that reached. Now, finding worthy men so as to extend benevolence to all under Heaven reaches far indeed—is this not why Yao and Shun made failing to find worthy men their concern? Moreover, since antiquity, in speaking of the flourishing of the way of governance, none compare to Yao and Shun; and in speaking of the utmost concern for the people, none compare to Yao and Shun either. Extending their hearts that desired to be benevolent to all under Heaven, it would seem they ought to have worried over every single matter. Yet what Yao took as his own concern was solely failing to find Shun. Outside of Shun, it was not that there was nothing to worry about; rather, once Shun was found, all of Yao's concerns had Shun to shoulder the responsibility for them—what then had Yao to worry about? What Shun took as his own concern was solely failing to find Yu and Gao Yao. Outside of Yu and Gao Yao, it was not that there was nothing to worry about; rather, once Yu and Gao Yao were found, all of Shun's concerns had Yu and Gao Yao to carry them through to completion in his stead—what then had Shun to worry about? As for a hundred mu of land not being properly tilled, this is merely the concern of a farmer; how could it be what Yao and Shun worried about? Yet this concern of Yao and Shun was precisely what constituted the benevolence of Yao and Shun. Why is this? Sharing wealth with others is merely kindness, and kindness at times comes to an end; it is not benevolence. Teaching others…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
善忠焉而已忠亦有所難徧也非仁也惟堯爲
天下而得舜焉舜爲天下而得禹皐陶焉則厚
生之政有人以敷之而容保自極於無疆正德
之化有人以任之而敎思自及於無窮此堯舜
萬世所以稱仁也所憂不亦大哉彼並耕者流
特憂農夫之憂者耳且不得以語忠惠矣況于
仁耶噫堯舜之仁也亦堯舜之所以垂衣而天
下治也古之帝王未嘗不勞于求賢而逸于得
人其有憂者乃所以成其無憂也故曰天不言
===
而歲功成品物亨者四時之吏五行之佐宣其
氣矣此天道也亦君道也
易
天地以順動故日月不過而四時不忒聖
人以順動則刑罰清而民服豫之時義
大矣哉
王命爵
同考試官敎諭曾 批 辭不費而豫之義瞭然是
深於易旨
punctuated:
善，忠焉而已，忠亦有所難徧也，非仁也。惟堯爲天下而得舜焉，舜爲天下而得禹、皐陶焉，則厚生之政有人以敷之，而容保自極於無疆；正德之化有人以任之，而敎思自及於無窮。此堯、舜萬世所以稱仁也，所憂不亦大哉！彼並耕者流，特憂農夫之憂者耳，且不得以語忠惠矣，況于仁耶！噫！堯、舜之仁也，亦堯、舜之所以垂衣而天下治也。古之帝王，未嘗不勞于求賢而逸于得人，其有憂者，乃所以成其無憂也。故曰：天不言而歲功成、品物亨者，四時之吏、五行之佐宣其氣矣。此天道也，亦君道也。

易

天地以順動，故日月不過，而四時不忒；聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。豫之時義大矣哉！

王命爵

同考試官敎諭曾批：辭不費而豫之義瞭然，是深於《易》旨。
translation_en:
… what is good is merely loyalty; and loyalty is also difficult to extend universally, so it is not benevolence. Only when Yao obtained Shun for the sake of all under Heaven, and Shun obtained Yu and Gao Yao for the sake of all under Heaven, were there men to spread the policies that enrich livelihoods, so that tolerant protection naturally reached boundlessness; and there were men to shoulder the transformations that rectify virtue, so that educational care naturally extended to infinity. This is why Yao and Shun have been praised for their benevolence for ten thousand generations—was not their concern great indeed! Those of the school who advocate ruler and subject plowing side by side merely worry about the worries of a farmer; they cannot even be spoken of in terms of loyalty and kindness, how much less of benevolence! Alas! The benevolence of Yao and Shun was also the means by which Yao and Shun let their robes hang down and all under Heaven was governed. The emperors and kings of antiquity never failed to toil in seeking worthies and enjoy ease in obtaining the right men; their having worries was precisely how they achieved their freedom from worry. Therefore it is said: Heaven does not speak, yet the work of the year is accomplished and the myriad things flourish, because the officials of the four seasons and the assistants of the Five Phases propagate its vital force. This is the Way of Heaven, and it is also the Way of the Ruler.

Book of Changes (Yi)

"Heaven and earth move in accord, and therefore the sun and moon do not err, and the four seasons do not deviate; the sage moves in accord, and thus punishments and penalties are clear and the people submit. Great indeed is the timely significance of Yu (Enthusiasm)!"

Wang Mingjue 王命爵

Associate Examiner and Instructor Zeng 曾 comments: The words are not wasted and the meaning of Yu is crystal clear; this is one who is profound in the purport of the Changes.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭姚批易旨融徹文義精緻結處
尤有深意取之
同考試官教諭薄批理旣真切詞復簡當宜冠
多士
考試官教諭鄭批詞不繁而義足佳士也
考試官學正馮批純正典雅
觀於天地聖人之豫而可以見其道之大矣夫
順動者豫之道也極之而天地聖人不能外焉
其道之大何如哉彖傳廣豫之蘊若曰豫之順
===
動豈特建侯行師之利已耶推而言之固天地
之道也聖人之道也彼天地之與日月四時以
氣相屬者也天地順二氣以施生一太極自然
之運而已故日月繫之以著明而不過也四時
順之以成序而不忒也造化調于上而太和之
氣在兩間矣斯其爲天地之豫乎聖人之于萬
民以心相感者也聖人因民心以出治一皇極
大中之道而已故刑不必齊而自若于訓也罰
不必施而自孚于化也民心服于下而太和之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭姚批：易旨融徹，文義精緻，結處尤有深意，取之。
同考試官教諭薄批：理旣真切，詞復簡當，宜冠多士。
考試官教諭鄭批：詞不繁而義足，佳士也。
考試官學正馮批：純正典雅。
觀於天地聖人之豫，而可以見其道之大矣。夫順動者，豫之道也。極之而天地聖人不能外焉，其道之大何如哉！《彖傳》廣豫之蘊，若曰：豫之順動，豈特建侯行師之利已耶？推而言之，固天地之道也，聖人之道也。彼天地之與日月四時，以氣相屬者也。天地順二氣以施生，一太極自然之運而已。故日月繫之以著明而不過也，四時順之以成序而不忒也。造化調于上，而太和之氣在兩間矣，斯其爲天地之豫乎！聖人之于萬民，以心相感者也。聖人因民心以出治，一皇極大中之道而已。故刑不必齊而自若于訓也，罰不必施而自孚于化也。民心服于下，而太和之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yao 姚 comments: "The import of the Book of Changes (Yi) is thoroughly understood and the literary expression and meaning are refined. The conclusion holds particularly deep meaning; select him."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Bo 薄 comments: "The reasoning is genuine and earnest, and the phrasing is concise and apt. He deserves to stand at the head of the many scholars."
Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: "The phrasing is not verbose yet the meaning is complete; a fine scholar."
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Feng 馮 comments: "Pure, orthodox, and classically elegant."

When we observe the "enthusiasm" (Yu 豫) of Heaven and Earth and of the Sage, we can see the greatness of its Way. Moving with compliant accord is the Way of Yu. When carried to its ultimate reach, neither Heaven and Earth nor the Sage can stand outside it—how great indeed is its Way! The Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan 彖傳) expands upon the deeper implications of the hexagram Yu, as if to say: Is the compliant movement of Yu merely advantageous for establishing feudal lords and marching armies? Extended further, it is truly the Way of Heaven and Earth, and the Way of the Sage.

Now, Heaven and Earth are connected with the sun, moon, and four seasons through vital force (qi 氣). Heaven and Earth accord with the two vital forces (yin and yang) to bestow life, which is nothing other than the natural operation of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji 太極). Therefore, the sun and moon are bound to it to shine brightly without excess or default, and the four seasons follow it to complete their sequence without error. The creative transformation is harmonized above, and the vital force of Great Harmony fills the space between Heaven and Earth—is this not the Yu of Heaven and Earth?

The Sage is connected with the myriad people through mutual resonance of the mind. The Sage brings forth governance by following the minds of the people, which is nothing other than the Way of the Supreme Standard (Huangji 皇極) and Great Centrality. Therefore, corporal punishments need not be uniformly enforced for the people naturally to conform to instruction, and fines need not be imposed for them naturally to be inspired with trust in moral transformation. The minds of the people submit below, and the [governance] of Great Harmony …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
治在宇内矣斯其爲聖人之豫乎夫莫大于天
地而不能外之以成化則所以體天地之撰者
此豫也此順動也莫大于聖人而不能外之以
成治則所以成聖人之能者此豫也此順動也
豫之時義不其大哉吁豫道之大如此觀豫者
可以通于三極之道矣甞謂時至于豫可樂也
亦可憂也常人之情每溺于宴安而聖人爲戒
必于方盛之日是以泰豐旣濟之卦聖人屢致
意焉而于豫復叮嚀於順動之義噫聖人之爲
===
世道慮深哉
精義入神以致用也利用安身以崇德也
過此以往未之或知也窮神知化德之
盛也
劉士翹
同考試官教諭曾批發得心學甚透而文更典
實取之
同考試官教諭姚批題本易作而聯絡貫穿毫
髮不遺則子獨得之尚荐允宜
punctuated:
治在宇内矣，斯其爲聖人之豫乎！夫莫大于天地，而不能外之以成化，則所以體天地之撰者，此豫也，此順動也；莫大于聖人，而不能外之以成治，則所以成聖人之能者，此豫也，此順動也。豫之時義，不其大哉！吁！豫道之大如此，觀《豫》者可以通于三極之道矣。甞謂時至于豫，可樂也，亦可憂也。常人之情每溺于宴安，而聖人爲戒必于方盛之日。是以《泰》、《豐》、《旣濟》之卦，聖人屢致意焉，而于《豫》復叮嚀於順動之義。噫！聖人之爲世道慮深哉！

「精義入神，以致用也；利用安身，以崇德也。過此以往，未之或知也；窮神知化，德之盛也。」
劉士翹
同考試官教諭曾批：發得心學甚透，而文更典實，取之。
同考試官教諭姚批：題本易作，而聯絡貫穿，毫髮不遺，則子獨得之，尚荐允宜。
translation_en:
… governance prevails throughout the realm. Is this not the joy and harmony (Yu) of the sage? Now, nothing is greater than Heaven and Earth, yet they cannot depart from this to accomplish their transformations; thus, that by which the manifestations of Heaven and Earth are embodied is this joy and harmony, this movement in顺 (accordance). Nothing is greater than the sage, yet he cannot depart from this to accomplish his governance; thus, that by which the capabilities of the sage are fulfilled is this joy and harmony, this movement in accordance. The timeliness and significance of the Yu hexagram—are they not great indeed! Ah! Since the Way of Yu is as great as this, one who contemplates the Yu hexagram may comprehend the Way of the Three Ultimates (Heaven, Earth, and Man). It has been said that when the time reaches a state of joy and harmony, it is cause for rejoicing, yet also cause for concern. The disposition of ordinary people is to constantly sink into ease and comfort, whereas the sage siempre issues warnings at the very moment of flourishing. Therefore, in the hexagrams Tai (Peace), Feng (Abundance), and Jiji (After Completion), the sage repeatedly directed his attention to this, and in the Yu hexagram he again earnestly enjoined the principle of moving in accordance. Alas! How profound was the sage's concern for the Way of the world!

"Refining righteousness to enter the marvelous is the means to advance practical application; benefiting application to secure the person is the means to exalt virtue. Going beyond this, no one knows how it happens; exhausting the marvelous and knowing transformation is the height of virtue." [Book of Changes, Xici II.5]

Liu Shiqiao 劉士翹

Associate Examiner, Instructor Zeng 曾 comments: It brings out the learning of the mind-and-heart (xinxue) very thoroughly, and the writing is furthermore classical and substantial. Accepted.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Yao 姚 comments: The topic is inherently easy to write on, yet to link and thread it together without leaving out a single hair's breadth—this you alone have achieved. To recommend it highly is truly fitting.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭溥批〔體裁端莊詞意精到是善〕
〔言聖學者宜錄〕
考試官教諭鄭批〔潔淨精微〕
考試官學正馮批〔思致筆力俱不凡〕
大傳舉聖學之全一自然之妙而已夫由下學
而上達聖學之全也然一出於自然焉人亦何
以思慮爲哉嘗謂天下有自然之理聖學有無
心之妙何則天下之事有義存焉而神即義之
微者也君子精義而妙入於神非以求利乎外
===
也然析義之既精者自時措之不匱所以出而
致用者不本於是乎身之所措有用存焉而用
固關乎身者也君子利用而身隨以安非以求
預乎內也然躬行之既裕者自心得之益深所
以入而崇德者不資於是乎以此利用吾知精
吾義也過此則義無可精不得而知也以此崇
德吾知利吾用也過此則用無可利不得而知
也進而至於窮天地之神與合一不測者有默
契焉進而至於知天地之化與推行有漸者若
punctuated:
同考試官教諭溥批：〔體裁端莊，詞意精到，是善言聖學者，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭鄭批：〔潔淨精微。〕
考試官學正馮批：〔思致筆力俱不凡。〕

大傳舉聖學之全，一自然之妙而已。夫由下學而上達，聖學之全也。然一出於自然焉，人亦何以思慮爲哉？嘗謂天下有自然之理，聖學有無心之妙。何則？天下之事有義存焉，而神即義之微者也。君子精義而妙入於神，非以求利乎外也。然析義之既精者，自時措之不匱，所以出而致用者，不本於是乎？身之所措有用存焉，而用固關乎身者也。君子利用而身隨以安，非以求預乎內也。然躬行之既裕者，自心得之益深，所以入而崇德者，不資於是乎？以此利用，吾知精吾義也；過此則義無可精，不得而知也。以此崇德，吾知利吾用也；過此則用無可利，不得而知也。進而至於窮天地之神，與合一不測者有默契焉；進而至於知天地之化，與推行有漸者若
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Pu 溥 comments: [The form and style are dignified, and the diction and ideas are precise and thorough. This is someone skilled at expounding the learning of the sages; it is fitting to select it.]
Examiner and Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: [Pure and subtly profound.]
Examiner and Director of Studies Feng 馮 comments: [Both the train of thought and the vigor of the brush are extraordinary.]

When the Great Commentary (Dazhuan) sets forth the entirety of sagely learning, it is simply a matter of the subtlety of what is natural and spontaneous. Now, proceeding from lower studies to higher penetration is the entirety of sagely learning. Yet since it all issues from what is natural, what need does a person have for anxious deliberation? I have held that in the world there is natural principle, and in sagely learning there is the subtlety of non-deliberation. Why is this so? In the affairs of the world, rightness (yi 義) is present, and the numinous (shen 神) is simply the subtle aspect of rightness. When the gentleman refines his grasp of rightness until its subtlety enters the numinous, it is not in order to seek advantage externally. Yet once the analysis of rightness has become refined, its timely application is naturally inexhaustible; is not this the basis from which one goes forth to achieve practical application? In the actions of one's person, practical application (yong 用) is present, and application inherently pertains to one's person. When the gentleman makes his application advantageous and his person thereby becomes secure, it is not in order to seek prior enrichment internally. Yet once personal practice has become abundant, what is gained in the mind naturally grows ever deeper; is not this the resource upon which one enters within to exalt virtue? Taking this to make application advantageous, I know only to refine my grasp of rightness; beyond this, there is nothing further in rightness that can be refined, and it is beyond what can be deliberately known. Taking this to exalt virtue, I know only to make my application advantageous; beyond this, there is nothing further in application that can be made advantageous, and it is beyond what can be deliberately known. Advancing to the point of exhausting the numinous of heaven and earth, one has a tacit accord with that which is unified and unfathomable; advancing to the point of knowing the transformations of heaven and earth, it is as if with that which moves forward gradually one…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
竝運焉此則精義之極而德之盛於內者一神
之無方夫是以同天地之神也利用之極而德
之盛於外者一化之無體夫是以合天地之化
也使非盛德而可以強致之耶吁卽聖學觀之
而屈伸感應自然之理明矣抑論天下無二理
聖人無二心精義利用非迹也窮神知化非虛
也善學者能自得之而下學上達一以貫之矣
噫以此爲訓猶有本末異見有無論道者
書
===
臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉禹曰俞帝曰臣作朕
股肱耳目
傅一元
同考試官教諭段批發明君臣一體意甚切似
於虞廷親見之者
同考試官教諭李批深得大舜命禹本意而文
又整肅可式
考試官教諭鄭批整潔冠諸士
考試官學正馮批明雅
punctuated:
竝運焉。此則精義之極，而德之盛於內者，一神之無方，夫是以同天地之神也；利用之極，而德之盛於外者，一化之無體，夫是以合天地之化也。使非盛德，而可以強致之耶？吁！卽聖學觀之，而屈伸感應自然之理明矣。抑論天下無二理，聖人無二心。精義利用，非迹也；窮神知化，非虛也。善學者能自得之，而下學上達，一以貫之矣。噫！以此爲訓，猶有本末異見、有無論道者。

《書》：「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」禹曰：「俞。」帝曰：「臣作朕股肱耳目。」
傅一元
同考試官教諭段批：發明君臣一體意甚切，似於虞廷親見之者。
同考試官教諭李批：深得大舜命禹本意，而文又整肅可式。
考試官教諭鄭批：整潔，冠諸士。
考試官學正馮批：明雅。
translation_en:
… operate in unison with it. This, then, is the ultimate point of refining righteousness, where virtue flourishes within and is wholly one with the boundlessness of the spirit; therefore, it is identical with the spirit of Heaven and Earth. It is the ultimate point of making use profitable, where virtue flourishes without and is wholly one with the formlessness of transformation; therefore, it accords with the transformation of Heaven and Earth. If it were not the flourishing of virtue, how could one force oneself to achieve it? Ah! Observing this from the perspective of sage learning, the natural principle of contraction, expansion, stimulus, and response becomes clear. Moreover, if we discuss it further, there are not two principles in the world, and the sage does not have two minds. Refining righteousness and making use profitable are not mere outward traces; exhausting the spirit and knowing transformation are not empty abstractions. Those who are good at learning are able to grasp this for themselves, learning below and penetrating above, binding it all together with a single thread. Alas! Even with this as an instruction, there are still those who hold divergent views on root and branch, or who discuss the Way in terms of being and non-being.

Book of Documents (Shu):
"Ministers! Associates! Associates! Ministers!" Yu said, "Yes!" The Emperor said, "Ministers act as my legs and arms, ears and eyes."
By Fu Yiyuan 傅一元.
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Duan 段: He elucidates the meaning of ruler and minister forming a single body very aptly, as if he had witnessed it in person at the court of Yu [Shun].
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李: He deeply grasps the original intent of Great Shun's charge to Yu, and the writing is also orderly, solemn, and worthy of serving as a model.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭: Neat and pure; it ranks first among all the scholars.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng) Feng 馮: Clear and elegant.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖君嘆臣職之重因著其義之切也甚矣臣之
有關於君也觀諸一體之義而其職之重可見
矣且夫人君必明於臣職而後可以責臣人臣
必自明其職而後可以事君帝固以弼直責其
臣者遂嘆之曰臣哉鄰哉鄰哉臣哉蓋深見乎
臣有鄰之道位不得而虛也鄰即臣之實職不
得而曠也此其弼豈容以不直耶禹固以弼直
事其君者遂應之曰俞蓋深信乎位不可虛臣
必思以善其鄰也職不可曠鄰必思以稱其臣
===
也此其直豈能以自諉耶於是帝復推其義以
示之曰汝知臣之為鄰矣抑知所以為鄰乎彼
人非股肱無以運動朕之有臣以憑以翼運動
資焉非作股肱者乎人非耳目無以聞見朕之
有臣以明以達聞見寄焉非作耳目者乎四體
備而後成人良臣輔而後成治茲其為鄰之義
而弼之必期於直也有臣鄰之責者尚無負於
一體之託哉雖然臣鄰之責禹不容辭矣然亦
不能以獨為也蓋人君之職在論相而相又統
punctuated: 聖君嘆臣職之重，因著其義之切也。甚矣，臣之有關於君也！觀諸一體之義，而其職之重可見矣。且夫人君必明於臣職，而後可以責臣；人臣必自明其職，而後可以事君。帝固以弼直責其臣者，遂嘆之曰：「臣哉鄰哉！鄰哉臣哉！」蓋深見乎臣有鄰之道，位不得而虛也；鄰即臣之實，職不得而曠也。此其弼豈容以不直耶？禹固以弼直事其君者，遂應之曰：「俞。」蓋深信乎位不可虛，臣必思以善其鄰也；職不可曠，鄰必思以稱其臣也。此其直豈能以自諉耶？於是帝復推其義以示之曰：「汝知臣之為鄰矣，抑知所以為鄰乎？彼人非股肱無以運動，朕之有臣，以憑以翼，運動資焉，非作股肱者乎？人非耳目無以聞見，朕之有臣，以明以達，聞見寄焉，非作耳目者乎？」四體備而後成人，良臣輔而後成治，茲其為鄰之義，而弼之必期於直也。有臣鄰之責者，尚無負於一體之託哉！雖然，臣鄰之責，禹不容辭矣，然亦不能以獨為也。蓋人君之職在論相，而相又統
translation_en:
The sage ruler sighed over the weight of a minister's duties, and consequently set forth the intimacy of their meaning. Profound indeed is the importance of the minister to the ruler! If one examines the principle of their being a single body, the weight of his duties becomes evident.

Moreover, a ruler must first understand the duties of a minister before he can hold his ministers accountable; a minister must first understand his own duties before he can serve his ruler. The Emperor [Shun], who held his ministers accountable for assisting him with uprightness, thus sighed and said: "Ministers! Associates! Associates! Ministers!" For he saw deeply that a minister possesses the Way of a close associate, so his position must not be held in vain; and that being a close associate is the true substance of a minister, so his office must not be neglected. How, then, could his assistance be anything less than upright? Yu, who served his ruler by assisting him with uprightness, accordingly replied: "Yes!" For he deeply believed that since the position must not be held in vain, a minister must ponder how to excel as an associate; and since the office must not be neglected, an associate must ponder how to live up to being a minister. How, then, could he shirk this uprightness?

Thereupon, the Emperor further extended this meaning to instruct him, saying: "You know that a minister is an associate, but do you know by what means he acts as an associate? Without limbs, a man has no means to move or act; in having ministers, We rely upon them and are supported by them, drawing upon them for movement and action—do they not act as Our limbs? Without ears and eyes, a man has no means to hear or see; in having ministers, We gain clarity and reach through them, entrusting to them Our hearing and seeing—do they not act as Our ears and eyes?" Only when the four limbs are complete is a person formed; only when worthy ministers assist is good governance achieved. Such is the meaning of being an associate, and the reason why their assistance must aim at uprightness. May those who bear the responsibility of being ministers and associates not fail the trust of forming a single body with the sovereign!

Even so, while Yu could not decline the responsibility of a minister and associate, neither could he carry it out alone. For the duty of a ruler lies in selecting a chief minister, and the chief minister in turn leads…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
百官以致治者也故君元首也相股肱耳目也
百官毛髮形骸也効力於衆收功於獨明於一
身之義而天下之治成矣
極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
朱益隆
同考試官教諭段批說敷言之能動民言簡意
足
同考試官教諭李批以心身發近天子之光處
有斟酌
===
考試官教諭鄭批平實光潤
考試官學正馮批雅健
斯民於敷言而由之以幾君德焉夫君德之光
未易及也庶民由敷言以幾之不可以觀其所
感之深哉箕子之意蓋曰皇極之理通君民而
一之者也兹惟以是而敷之言焉將見凡此庶
民以敷言也者天子所以使之歌咏而興起者
也于是乎訓之反覆致思而王猷之榆揚焉亦
所以使之進修而實踐者也于是乎行之敦行
punctuated:
百官以致治者也。故君，元首也；相，股肱耳目也；百官，毛髮形骸也。効力於衆，收功於獨，明於一身之義，而天下之治成矣。

極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。
朱益隆
同考試官教諭段批：說敷言之能動民，言簡意足。
同考試官教諭李批：以心身發「近天子之光」處，有斟酌。
考試官教諭鄭批：平實光潤。
考試官學正馮批：雅健。

斯民於敷言而由之，以幾君德焉。夫君德之光，未易及也；庶民由敷言以幾之，不可以觀其所感之深哉？箕子之意，蓋曰：皇極之理，通君民而一之者也，兹惟以是而敷之言焉。將見凡此庶民，以敷言也者，天子所以使之歌咏而興起者也，于是乎訓之，反覆致思，而王猷之榆揚焉；亦所以使之進修而實踐者也，于是乎行之，敦行
translation_en:
… all the officials so as to bring about good governance. Therefore, the ruler is the head; the chief minister is the limbs, ears, and eyes; and all the officials are the hair and physical frame. Exerting effort through the many and reaping success in the one—when the principle of being a single body is understood, the governance of the world is accomplished.

"This amplification of the royal perfection, by studying it and practicing it, so as to draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven." [Book of Documents, "Hongfan"]
Zhu Yilong 朱益隆
Associate Examiner Instructor Duan comments: In explaining how the amplified words are able to move the people, the language is concise and the meaning complete.
Associate Examiner Instructor Li comments: Where he elaborates on "drawing near to the glory of the Son of Heaven" in terms of mind and person, it is well-weighed.
Examiner Instructor Zheng comments: Plain, solid, lustrous, and smooth.
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng comments: Refined and vigorous.

When this people follow the amplified words, they thereby approach the ruler's virtue. Now, the glory of the ruler's virtue is not easily reached; when the common people follow the amplified words so as to approach it, can one not see from this how deeply they have been moved? The meaning of Jizi 箕子 is to say: The principle of the Supreme Standard (huangji) connects ruler and people and unites them as one; here, he simply takes this and amplifies it in words. We shall see that all these common people, taking the amplified words to be that whereby the Son of Heaven causes them to sing praises and be inspired, thereupon study them as instructions, pondering them repeatedly and extolling [榆揚 for 揄揚] the royal plans; and taking them also to be that whereby he causes them to advance in cultivation and put them into actual practice, they thereupon carry them out, practicing them earnestly…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不怠而帝則之率履焉夫天子之建極於上也
德音昭矣而民之訓之自有以挹聖謨之英華
德輝動矣而民之行之自有以希帝範之精彩
以由乎極之體天子心法之彰雖未能卽與之
協而必非偏黨反側以自異者矣錫保之盛殆
煥然於邦國之間乎以由乎極之用天子身法
之顯雖未能卽與之齊而必非偏陂好惡以自
悖者矣會歸之化殆燦然於海宇之內乎是則
訓行以合德固庶民感孚之神貞教以淑人尤
===
王者鼓動之善孰謂敷言其可已耶雖然身教
者從敷言何以能感人也蓋皇極之建已先天
下而端其本而言特以鼓之耳是以其入之易
也不然文帝之詔宜其動民之深而貞觀之所
以諭民敦俗者何不臻太和之治哉
詩
有馮有翼有孝有德以引以翼豈弟君子
四方爲則
江楫
punctuated:
不怠，而帝則之率履焉。夫天子之建極於上也，德音昭矣，而民之訓之，自有以挹聖謨之英華；德輝動矣，而民之行之，自有以希帝範之精彩。以由乎極之體，天子心法之彰，雖未能卽與之協，而必非偏黨反側以自異者矣，錫保之盛，殆煥然於邦國之間乎！以由乎極之用，天子身法之顯，雖未能卽與之齊，而必非偏陂好惡以自悖者矣，會歸之化，殆燦然於海宇之內乎！是則訓行以合德，固庶民感孚之神；貞教以淑人，尤王者鼓動之善。孰謂敷言其可已耶？雖然，身教者從，敷言何以能感人也？蓋皇極之建，已先天下而端其本，而言特以鼓之耳，是以其入之易也。不然，文帝之詔，宜其動民之深，而貞觀之所以諭民敦俗者，何不臻太和之治哉？
詩
有馮有翼，有孝有德，以引以翼。豈弟君子，四方爲則。
江楫
translation_en:
…without slackening, and thus follow and tread in the sovereign's norms. Now, when the Son of Heaven establishes the Supreme Ultimate on high, his virtuous voice shines forth; as the people take it as their instruction, they naturally have the means to draw upon the finest essence of the sacred counsels. His virtuous radiance moves them; as the people put it into practice, they naturally have the means to emulate the splendid brilliance of the imperial model. In following the substance of the Ultimate—the manifestation of the Son of Heaven's method of the mind—even if they cannot immediately harmonize with it, they will certainly not set themselves apart through partiality, factionalism, or perversity. How resplendently does the flourishing of his bestowing and preserving shine forth among the states and domains! In following the function of the Ultimate—the display of the Son of Heaven's personal example—even if they cannot immediately equal it, they will certainly not contravene it through biased likes and dislikes. How brightly does the transformation of their converging and returning shine within the realm! Thus, taking it as instruction and putting it into practice so as to conform to his virtue is indeed the marvelous responsiveness of the common people's being moved and inspired; while upholding upright teaching to improve men is especially the excellence of the true king's rousing and motivating them. Who would say that setting forth his words extensively is something that can be dispensed with? Even so, people follow example in action—how is it that setting forth words can move men? It is because the establishment of theAugust Ultimate has already rectified the fundamental basis ahead of the whole world, and words merely serve to rouse them; therefore, they enter into men's hearts easily. Otherwise, the edicts of Emperor Wen of Han ought to have moved the people deeply, and the means by which the Zhenguan reign of Tang instructed the people and fostered pure customs—why did they not attain the governance of Great Harmony?

Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
"You have those on whom to rely, you have those to give you wings, men of filial piety and of virtue, to lead you on and to support you; O easy and fraternal lord, the model for the four quarters of the realm."

Jiang Ji 江楫

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭郭批君德克修皆由得賢所致
此作甚得召公進規之義
同考試官教諭馮批詞義醇深寫出召公矢歌
忠愛意藹然
同考試官教諭姚批理旣真切詞復簡明文之
古調者宜録以式
考試官教諭鄭批溫厚含蓄
考試官學正馮批老臣愛君之意是如此
人君得賢以自輔而爲法于天下也蓋君德成
===
于多助也賢才輔而德脩矣有不爲天下法乎
此召公納誨于成王也若曰人君斂福之本在
德而脩德之資在賢吾王亦於賢而加之意耳
蓋惟我周也道化煕隆而英賢輩出有馮而可
爲依者有翼而可爲輔者均之可以待用也有
順親而謂之孝者有體道而謂之德者均之足
以致主也誠以之爲引焉疑承于後先者罔非
正人則涵養之深而進脩日底于高明矣以之
爲翼焉弼輔乎左右者悉皆端士則啓沃之乆
punctuated:
同考試官教諭郭批：君德克修，皆由得賢所致。此作甚得召公進規之義。
同考試官教諭馮批：詞義醇深，寫出召公矢歌忠愛意藹然。
同考試官教諭姚批：理旣真切，詞復簡明，文之古調者，宜録以式。
考試官教諭鄭批：溫厚含蓄。
考試官學正馮批：老臣愛君之意是如此。
人君得賢以自輔，而爲法于天下也。蓋君德成于多助也，賢才輔而德脩矣，有不爲天下法乎？此召公納誨于成王也，若曰：人君斂福之本在德，而脩德之資在賢，吾王亦於賢而加之意耳。蓋惟我周也，道化煕隆，而英賢輩出。有馮而可爲依者，有翼而可爲輔者，均之可以待用也；有順親而謂之孝者，有體道而謂之德者，均之足以致主也。誠以之爲引焉，疑承于後先者罔非正人，則涵養之深，而進脩日底于高明矣；以之爲翼焉，弼輔乎左右者悉皆端士，則啓沃之乆，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Guo: "That the ruler's virtue can be cultivated is entirely brought about by obtaining worthy men. This composition thoroughly grasps the meaning of the Duke of Shao's presentation of admonition."

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Feng: "The diction and meaning are pure and profound, depicting with gentle warmth the loyal and affectionate intent of the Duke of Shao in offering his song."

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Yao: "The reasoning is genuine and earnest, and the phrasing is furthermore concise and clear. As a composition of ancient style, it ought to be recorded as a model."

Comment by Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng: "Warm, generous, and rich in implication."

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng: "Such is the affection of a veteran minister for his lord."

When a ruler obtains worthy men to assist himself, he becomes a model for the world. For a ruler's virtue is brought to completion through abundant assistance; when men of worth and talent assist him and his virtue is cultivated, how could he not become a model for the world? Such was the counsel presented by the Duke of Shao to King Cheng, as if to say: The foundation for a ruler's gathering of blessings lies in virtue, and the resource for cultivating virtue lies in worthy men; may my King simply pay greater heed to worthy men! For in our Zhou dynasty, the transforming influence of the Way flourishes brightly, and outstanding worthies emerge in succession. There are those who offer support and can be relied upon, and those who act as wings and can serve as aides—all alike are ready to be employed.
