There are those who obey their parents and are called filial, and those who embody the Way and are called virtuous—all alike suffice to bring their lord to perfection. Truly, if one takes them as guides to lead the way, so that those who attend to doubts and provide support before and behind are none other than upright men, then through deep nurturing, one's moral advancement and cultivation will daily attain to lofty brilliance; if one takes them as wings to flank the side, so that those who assist on the left and right are all men of rectitude, then through prolonged enlightenment and counsel, …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
而所造日遊于廣大矣豈弟君子不爲四方則
耶吾知元良旣端則表正之體以立皇極旣建
則物軌之機自章近而百官其訓行以近天子
之光者翕如也蓋吾王本合衆賢之善以爲善
而四方有不環向取則者乎遠而萬民其會歸
而徧爲爾德者熈如也蓋吾王本合天下之德
以爲德而羣黎有不則君自治者乎至是則文
之作孚武之是式於今再覩要之得賢之助爲
可誣也王盍亦急親賢之爲務乎大抵憂治世
===
而危明主老臣謀國之心然也觀虞廷極盛之
時臯陶賡歌以股肱良哉爲咏而召公矢音亦
惓惓於孝德意固相發耳噫後世繼同遊之盛
而賡卷阿之什者尚有在也蓋不能不深致其
望云
宣哲維人文武維后燕及皇天克昌厥後
綏我眉壽介以繁祉
甯遵
同考試官教諭郭批〔文王格天裕後本於道德〕
punctuated:
而所造日遊于廣大矣。豈弟君子，不爲四方則耶？吾知元良旣端，則表正之體以立；皇極旣建，則物軌之機自章。近而百官，其訓行以近天子之光者，翕如也。蓋吾王本合衆賢之善以爲善，而四方有不環向取則者乎？遠而萬民，其會歸而徧爲爾德者，熈如也。蓋吾王本合天下之德以爲德，而羣黎有不則君自治者乎？至是，則文之作孚、武之是式，於今再覩，要之得賢之助，爲可誣也？王盍亦急親賢之爲務乎？大抵憂治世而危明主，老臣謀國之心然也。觀虞廷極盛之時，臯陶賡歌，以「股肱良哉」爲咏，而召公矢音，亦惓惓於孝德，意固相發耳。噫！後世繼同遊之盛，而賡《卷阿》之什者，尚有在也，蓋不能不深致其望云。

宣哲維人，文武維后。燕及皇天，克昌厥後。綏我眉壽，介以繁祉。
甯遵
同考試官教諭郭批：〔文王格天裕後，本於道德，〕
translation_en:
… and his attainments will daily roam in vastness and greatness. Will the愷悌 (easy and pleasant) lord not become the model for the four quarters? I know that once the supreme goodness of the sovereign is rectified, the substance of setting a righteous standard is established; once the August Ultimate is set up, the mechanism by which all things follow the norm naturally becomes manifest. Near at hand, the hundred officials, who follow his teachings to draw near the radiance of the Son of Heaven, are in harmonious accord. For our King fundamentally combines the goodness of the many worthies to make his own goodness—how could the four quarters not turn toward him from all around to take him as their model? Far away, the myriad people, who converge and return to him so that universally they practice your virtue, are in prosperous peace. For our King fundamentally combines the virtue of all under heaven to make his own virtue—how could the multitude of commoners not model themselves on the ruler to govern themselves? When it comes to this, King Wen's inspiring of trust and King Wu's serving as the standard are witnessed once again today. In sum, how could the assistance of obtaining worthies be denied [reading 爲 as 焉/豈]? Why does the King not also make it his urgent task to draw close to the worthy? Generally speaking, to worry in an age of order and to warn an enlightened ruler—such is the heart of a veteran minister taking counsel for the state. Looking at the court of Yu at the height of its flourishing, Gao Yao continued the song, chanting "The legs and arms are good indeed!", while the Duke of Shao in offering his verses was likewise earnestly devoted to the filial and the virtuous; their intentions truly illuminate one another. Alas! In later ages, for those who would continue the splendour of roaming together with the sovereign and carry on the ode of "Juan'e" (Curving Slope), the responsibility still remains; one cannot but express the deepest hopes for it.

"Perceptive and wise as a man, civil and martial as a ruler; he gave peace even unto August Heaven, and was able to make prosperous his descendants. He comforts us with longevity of prominent eyebrows, and aids us with manifold blessings." [Book of Odes, "Yong"]

Ning Zun

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Guo: [That King Wen reached Heaven and enriched his posterity was rooted in the Way and virtue; …]

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
作者徒騁浮詞未發旨趣子能悉其蘊矣
同考試官教諭馮批武王對揚文王之意發揮
殆盡詩義之準繩也
同考試官教諭姚批莊重典雅且過下處渾無
痕迹其善說詩者
考試官教諭鄭批簡潔精邃
考試官學正馮批格高詞爽
詩人頌先王道德之全而推其裕後之實也蓋
福壽兼隆文王昌後之慶也然非道德之克全
===
其何以致之此武王祭文王也其詩曰奉祭以
得人爲孝而先王以裕後爲仁予固得以萃萬
國以肆祀矣然孰非皇考之所詒耶彼盡人之
道曰宣與哲皇考則宣以通微哲以察則人道
其克盡矣備君之德曰文與武皇考則文以經
邦武以戡亂君德其全備矣以之怙冒萬民則
輯寧之化適慰其求莫之心安乎民者因以安
乎天也以之垂裕後昆則監觀之表益隆其眷
顧之休福文王者遂以福其後也昌後者貴其
punctuated:
作者徒騁浮詞，未發旨趣，子能悉其蘊矣。
同考試官教諭馮批：武王對揚文王之意，發揮殆盡，詩義之準繩也。
同考試官教諭姚批：莊重典雅，且過下處渾無痕迹，其善說詩者。
考試官教諭鄭批：簡潔精邃。
考試官學正馮批：格高詞爽。
詩人頌先王道德之全，而推其裕後之實也。蓋福壽兼隆，文王昌後之慶也，然非道德之克全，其何以致之？此武王祭文王也。其詩曰：奉祭以得人爲孝，而先王以裕後爲仁，予固得以萃萬國以肆祀矣，然孰非皇考之所詒耶？彼盡人之道曰宣與哲，皇考則宣以通微、哲以察則，人道其克盡矣；備君之德曰文與武，皇考則文以經邦、武以戡亂，君德其全備矣。以之怙冒萬民，則輯寧之化，適慰其求莫之心，安乎民者，因以安乎天也；以之垂裕後昆，則監觀之表，益隆其眷顧之休，福文王者，遂以福其後也。昌後者貴其
translation_en:
… [Ordinary] writers merely indulge in superficial rhetoric without bringing out the essential purport, whereas you have been able to fully grasp its profound meaning.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Feng: King Wu's intention in extolling and responding to King Wen is expounded almost exhaustively; this is a standard model for interpreting the Classic of Poetry (Shijing).
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Yao: Solemn and refined in style, and its transitions to the following sections leave no trace of artifice; truly one who excels at explaining the Odes.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: Concise, pure, and deeply perceptive.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Feng: Elevated in structure and brisk in diction.

The poet praises the completeness of the former king's moral virtue and traces the reality of how he enriched his descendants. Indeed, the twin abundance of blessings and longevity is the good fortune by which King Wen made his posterity prosper; yet without the perfection of his moral virtue, how could this have been brought about? This ode is King Wu's sacrifice to King Wen. The poem says, in effect: In offering sacrifice, to secure worthy men is filial piety, while for the former king, to enrich his descendants was benevolence. I have indeed been able to gather the myriad states to perform this grand sacrifice, yet what part of this is not bequeathed by my August Deceased Father? To fulfill the Way of man is called comprehensive understanding and wisdom; my August Deceased Father was comprehensive in penetrating the subtle and wise in discerning principles, thus fulfilling the Way of man to the utmost. To possess the complete virtue of a ruler is called civil and martial accomplishment; my August Deceased Father used civil德 to order the state and martial prowess to quell rebellion, thus possessing the virtue of a ruler in full. When with these virtues he sheltered and covered the myriad people, his harmonizing and pacifying transformation precisely satisfied Heaven's desire for the people's tranquil settlement; by bringing peace to the people, he thereby brought peace to Heaven. When with these virtues he handed down abundance to later generations, Heaven, looking down from on high, further increased the grace of its loving regard; having blessed King Wen, it consequently blessed his descendants as well. Since making posterity prosper values…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
壽則綏我以眉壽焉所以膺歷年之多而撫靈
長之運者殆有惠我無疆矣而肇稱之禮不藉
是以盡耶昌後者尚其福則介我以繁祉焉所
以篤思皇之祜而集未成之統者殆有永錫爾
極矣而不匱之孝不賴斯而展耶夫眉壽繁祉
莫非昌後之洪休而本其垂慶要皆道德之所
致然則今日得人以相祀其敢忘所自耶噫此
武王之作求乎世德也乃文王之心惟知朢道
未見遹求厥寧而已六州之獻厚下之防所以
===
終守臣節者如是耳他無所冀也迨夫燮伐之
舉亦時之既至武王不能却其來者故孔子賛
文王為至德而武王以達孝稱之其旨深矣
春秋
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕公會齊侯宋
公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯于鹹〔僖公十有三年〕
毛志尹
punctuated:
壽，則綏我以眉壽焉。所以膺歷年之多，而撫靈長之運者，殆有惠我無疆矣，而肇稱之禮，不藉是以盡耶？昌後者尚其福，則介我以繁祉焉。所以篤思皇之祜，而集未成之統者，殆有永錫爾極矣，而不匱之孝，不賴斯而展耶？夫眉壽繁祉，莫非昌後之洪休，而本其垂慶，要皆道德之所致。然則今日得人以相祀，其敢忘所自耶？噫！此武王之作求乎世德也。乃文王之心，惟知朢道未見，遹求厥寧而已。六州之獻，厚下之防，所以終守臣節者如是耳，他無所冀也。迨夫燮伐之舉，亦時之既至，武王不能却其來者。故孔子賛文王為至德，而武王以達孝稱之，其旨深矣。

春秋
「夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。」〔僖公九年〕「公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于鹹。」〔僖公十有三年〕
毛志尹
translation_en:
…longevity, he then comforts me with venerable longevity. That by which I receive a multitude of years and preside over a long-lasting destiny is truly through his bestowing boundless grace upon me; and are not the newly instituted rites fulfilled by relying upon this? In making prosperous his descendants, one esteems fortune, and so he increases my abundant blessings. That by which I consolidate our august house's favor and bring together the unfinished dynastic line is truly through his eternally granting perfection; and is not unfailing filial piety extended by depending upon this? Now, venerable longevity and abundant blessings are none other than the great favor of making prosperous his descendants, yet tracing the root of the blessings he handed down, in summary they were all brought about by his moral virtue. This being so, when today I obtain worthy men to assist in the sacrifice, how could I dare forget whence it came? Ah! This was how King Wu strove to match the hereditary virtue. Yet the mind of King Wen knew only of gazing toward the Way as if not yet having seen it, and following the quest for peace and tranquility—nothing more. The presentation of the six provinces and the bulwark of generosity to those below—that by which he maintained the integrity of a subject to the very end was simply like this; he had no other ambitions. When it came to the enterprise of the punitive expedition in harmony with Heaven, it was also because the time had arrived, and King Wu could not turn away what came to him. Therefore Confucius praised King Wen as possessing supreme virtue, and acclaimed King Wu for far-reaching filial piety; the meaning of this is profound indeed!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In summer, the Duke met the Grand宰 (Zai), the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu." [Ninth year of Duke Xi] "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Xian." [Thirteenth year of Duke Xi]

By Mao Zhiyin 毛志尹

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批稱公原繫周制人皆以聖
人作經發明殆非本旨此篇獨得尊王之義宜錄以式
考試官教諭鄭批得春秋謹嚴體
考試官學正馮批認傳明措詞雅
春秋序人之爵皆王制所當尊者焉蓋公乃人
爵之尊也春秋特於宰孔宋襄稱之其有深意
乎且夫人君列爵以馭貴論德而詔爵上公之
稱固不輕以假人者葵丘之會宰孔書公何耶
曰天子三公稱公王制也蓋體乾御極惟天王
爲至尊論道經邦惟宰臣爲至貴上兼師保作
一人之股肱焉下總端揆爲羣工之表率焉宰
孔以之其視禹周相君雖曰德有隆替然位躋
崇階同一調元之任也下而卿大夫士其孰能
擬之春秋仍其爵而書曰宰周公義蓋如此于
醎之會宋襄書公何耶曰王者之後稱公王制
也蓋曆數相循天命雖改夫殷祚子孫永保恩
禮特隆于周封尹玆東夏則曰建爾上公焉作
賓王家則曰以備三恪焉宋襄以之其視虞胡=]
===
爲至尊論道經邦惟宰臣爲至貴上兼師保作
一人之股肱焉下總端揆爲羣工之表率焉宰
孔以之其視禹周相君雖曰德有隆替然位躋
崇階同一調元之任也下而卿大夫士其孰能
擬之春秋仍其爵而書曰宰周公義蓋如此于
醎之會宋襄書公何耶曰王者之後稱公王制
也蓋曆數相循天命雖改夫殷祚子孫永保恩
禮特隆于周封尹玆東夏則曰建爾上公焉作
賓王家則曰以備三恪焉宋襄以之其視虞胡
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：「稱公原繫周制，人皆以聖人作經發明，殆非本旨。此篇獨得尊王之義，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「得《春秋》謹嚴體。」
考試官學正馮批：「認傳明，措詞雅。」

《春秋》序人之爵，皆王制所當尊者焉。蓋公乃人爵之尊也，《春秋》特於宰孔、宋襄稱之，其有深意乎？且夫人君列爵以馭貴，論德而詔爵，上公之稱，固不輕以假人者。葵丘之會，宰孔書「公」，何耶？曰：天子三公稱公，王制也。蓋體乾御極，惟天王爲至尊；論道經邦，惟宰臣爲至貴。上兼師保，作一人之股肱焉；下總端揆，爲羣工之表率焉，宰孔以之。其視禹、周相君，雖曰德有隆替，然位躋崇階，同一調元之任也。下而卿、大夫、士，其孰能擬之？《春秋》仍其爵而書曰「宰周公」，義蓋如此。于醎之會，宋襄書「公」，何耶？曰：王者之後稱公，王制也。蓋曆數相循，天命雖改夫殷祚；子孫永保，恩禮特隆于周封。尹玆東夏，則曰「建爾上公」焉；作賓王家，則曰「以備三恪」焉，宋襄以之。其視虞胡=]
爲至尊；論道經邦，惟宰臣爲至貴。上兼師保，作一人之股肱焉；下總端揆，爲羣工之表率焉，宰孔以之。其視禹、周相君，雖曰德有隆替，然位躋崇階，同一調元之任也。下而卿、大夫、士，其孰能擬之？《春秋》仍其爵而書曰「宰周公」，義蓋如此。于醎之會，宋襄書「公」，何耶？曰：王者之後稱公，王制也。蓋曆數相循，天命雖改夫殷祚；子孫永保，恩禮特隆于周封。尹玆東夏，則曰「建爾上公」焉；作賓王家，則曰「以備三恪」焉，宋襄以之。其視虞胡
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Chen: "Calling them 'Duke' originally pertained to the institutions of Zhou. Everyone takes it as an elucidation made by the Sage in composing the Classic, which is probably not the original intent. This essay alone grasps the principle of honoring the King; it should be recorded to serve as a model."
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng: "It grasps the rigorous and strict style of the Spring and Autumn Annals."
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Feng: "Its understanding of the commentaries is clear, and its phrasing is elegant."

When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) sets forth men's titles of nobility, they are all those who ought to be honored under the King's institutions. For "Duke" (gong) is the most exalted of human titles of nobility; Does the Spring and Autumn Annals have a profound meaning in specially applying this title to Prime Minister Kong (Zai Kong) and Xiang of Song (Song Xiang)? Moreover, when a ruler of men ranks titles of nobility to govern the noble, and assesses virtue to confer titles, the designation of Upper Duke (shanggong) is surely not lightly lent to others. At the covenant of Kuiqiu, why is Prime Minister Kong recorded as "Duke"? It is said: That the Son of Heaven's Three Dukes (sangong) are called "Duke" is the King's institution. For in embodying Heaven (Qian) and ruling from the supreme throne, only the Heavenly King is supremely honored; in discoursing on the Way and ordering the state, only the prime minister is supremely noble. Above, he concurrently serves as Mentor and Guardian, acting as the legs and arms of the One Man; below, he exercises general control as chief minister, serving as the model and leader for all officials—Prime Minister Kong occupied this position. Compared to Yu and the Duke of Zhou assisting their rulers, although it may be said that their virtue had its rise and decline, in ascending to this lofty rank, it was the very same responsibility of harmonizing the primordial vitalities. Below him, among the Ministers, Grand Masters, and Servicemen, who could be compared to him? That the Spring and Autumn Annals follows his title of nobility and records "Prime Minister the Duke of Zhou" (Zai Zhougong) has its principle in this. At the covenant of Xian, why is Xiang of Song recorded as "Duke"? It is said: That the descendants of former kings are called "Duke" is the King's institution. For as the destiny of Heaven's calendar succeeded in turn, although the Mandate of Heaven changed the dynastic fortune of Yin, its descendants were perpetually preserved, and grace and ritual were made especially generous in the enfeoffments of Zhou. In governing these eastern Xia lands, it was said, "We establish you as Upper Duke"; in acting as guests of the Royal House, it was said, "to complete the Three Revered Lineages (sanke)"—Xiang of Song occupied this position. Compared to Hu of Yu [Duke Hu of Chen]…
[The second half-leaf duplicates the preceding nine columns of text, from "…is supremely honored; in discoursing on the Way…" through "…Compared to Hu of Yu…"]…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
錫命雖日時有後先然世膺殊典同一天潢之
胄也下而侯伯子男可若是班乎春秋仍其爵
而書曰宋公義蓋如此若如曹州寔固今之諸
侯而昔之三公也安得不稱公以明均勞之義
耶抑論位重者其體隆賜胙細務也乃宰臣將
命得無失居尊之體乎蓋翼戴王室桓實義舉
則殊禮相加較夫河陽下勞者不侔矣如宋襄
協謀勤王覇圖肇起幾于却楚而尊周其亦無
忝先德哉
===
公子遂如楚乞師〔僖公二十有六年〕冬
十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十有一年〕
王德新
同考試官教諭陳批聖經重使將之微意正欲
人君慎其選也此作得之矣
考試官教諭鄭批詞嚴意正可錄
考試官學正馮批發重使將意明盡
春秋紀使將必立常體以重其任焉夫任之重
punctuated:
錫命，雖日時有後先，然世膺殊典，同一天潢之胄也。下而侯伯子男，可若是班乎？《春秋》仍其爵而書曰「宋公」，義蓋如此。若如曹州寔，固今之諸侯，而昔之三公也，安得不稱公以明均勞之義耶？抑論位重者其體隆，賜胙細務也，乃宰臣將命，得無失居尊之體乎？蓋翼戴王室，桓實義舉，則殊禮相加，較夫河陽下勞者不侔矣。如宋襄協謀勤王，覇圖肇起，幾于却楚而尊周，其亦無忝先德哉！

公子遂如楚乞師〔僖公二十有六年〕、冬十月甲午叔孫得臣敗狄于鹹〔文公十有一年〕
王德新
同考試官教諭陳批：聖經重使將之微意，正欲人君慎其選也。此作得之矣。
考試官教諭鄭批：詞嚴意正，可錄。
考試官學正馮批：發重使將意，明盡。

《春秋》紀使將，必立常體以重其任焉。夫任之重
translation_en:
… receiving their investiture, although the times were earlier or later, yet for generations they enjoyed special rites and were alike scions of the heavenly lineage. Below them, could marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons be ranked on a par with them? That the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) retains his title and writes "the Duke of Song" has its meaning in this. As for Shi of Cao [Zhougong Shi], he was indeed a feudal lord of the present day, yet one of the Three Dukes (Sangong) of former times; how could he not be styled "Duke" in order to make clear the principle of sharing the toil? Or if one argues that for someone of weighty position his dignity should be exalted, and that bestowing sacrificial meat is a minor affair, then in having a prime minister convey the command, did it not lose the dignity of occupying an exalted position? In truth, in supporting and upholding the royal house, Duke Huan of Qi's act was genuinely righteous; thus the special courtesy bestowed upon him was not comparable to going down to comfort the feudal lords at Heyang. And as for Duke Xiang of Song joining in counsel to serve the king's cause, when his hegemonic ambitions first arose he came close to repelling Chu and honoring Zhou—surely he too did not disgrace the virtue of his ancestors!

"Gongzi Sui went to Chu to beg for troops" [Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi]; "In winter, in the tenth month, on the day jiawu, Shusun Dechen defeated the Di at Xian" [Eleventh year of Duke Wen].
By Wang Dexin 王德新.
Associate Examiner Instructor Chen comments: The subtle intent of the sagely Classic in attaching importance to the chief envoy and the commander is precisely to desire that the ruler be cautious in selecting them. This composition has grasped it.
Examiner Instructor Zheng comments: The diction is rigorous and the meaning upright; it is worthy of being recorded.
Examiner Director of Studies Feng comments: It brings out the meaning of attaching importance to the chief envoy and the commander clearly and exhaustively.

When the Spring and Autumn Annals records envoys and commanders, it invariably establishes a constant form in order to give weight to their charge. Now, when the charge is weighty…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者責斯重矣春秋特紀使將而略介副謂非立
文之常體哉北鄙見伐魯乞楚師以禦齊于時
奉命行者公子遂臧孫辰也春秋獨舉遂何耶
蓋上客有專對四方之責君命賴以不辱也如
楚之役授節請師襄仲繫一國之重輕介紹不
得而匹焉雖曰子玉之道文仲亦與有力矣然
人君遣使之常體士介於大夫大夫介於卿詞
命有特受孰得而侵其職耶經故舉遂而略辰
也其詩重皇華之義與鄋瞞侵陵魯因興師以
===
敗狄于時董兵行者叔孫得臣侯叔夏也春秋
獨稱得臣何耶蓋元帥有專制閫外之任國家
藉以即安也于鹹之役仗鉞臨戎得臣爲三軍
之司命偏裨不得而竝焉雖曰僑如之獲侯叔
亦嘗有功矣然人君任將之常體不間以親信
不參以羣小法令有專主孰得而分其權耶經
故稱得臣而略夏也其易重丈人之義與觀此
則使將各重其任而體統正矣其有介副竝書
者則變例存焉安可以泥之抑是二役也齊始
punctuated: 者，責斯重矣。《春秋》特紀使將而略介副，謂非立文之常體哉？北鄙見伐，魯乞楚師以禦齊。于時奉命行者，公子遂、臧孫辰也。《春秋》獨舉遂，何耶？蓋上客有專對四方之責，君命賴以不辱也。如楚之役，授節請師，襄仲繫一國之重輕，介紹不得而匹焉。雖曰子玉之道，文仲亦與有力矣；然人君遣使之常體，士介於大夫，大夫介於卿，詞命有特受，孰得而侵其職耶？經故舉遂而略辰也，其《詩》重《皇華》之義與！鄋瞞侵陵，魯因興師以敗狄。于時董兵行者，叔孫得臣、侯叔夏也。《春秋》獨稱得臣，何耶？蓋元帥有專制閫外之任，國家藉以即安也。于鹹之役，仗鉞臨戎，得臣爲三軍之司命，偏裨不得而竝焉。雖曰僑如之獲，侯叔亦嘗有功矣；然人君任將之常體，不間以親信，不參以羣小，法令有專主，孰得而分其權耶？經故稱得臣而略夏也，其《易》重「丈人」之義與！觀此，則使將各重其任，而體統正矣。其有介副竝書者，則變例存焉，安可以泥之？抑是二役也，齊始
translation_en:
… where the office is weighty, the responsibility is weighty as well. When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) specifically records the chief envoy and the commander-in-chief while omitting the deputy envoy and the subordinate general, how could one say that this is not the regular rule of literary composition?

When its northern border was attacked, Lu begged troops from Chu in order to resist Qi. At that time, those who received the ruler's command and went were Prince Sui (Gongzi Sui 公子遂) and Zangsun Chen 臧孫辰. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals mention only Sui? It is because the chief guest bears the responsibility of responding independently across the four quarters, and the ruler's mandate relies on him not to be disgraced. In the mission to Chu, entrusted with the tally to request troops, Xiangzhong (Prince Sui) held the weight of the entire state upon himself, and the deputy could not be placed on a par with him. Even though it is said that in guiding Ziyu 子玉, Wenzhong (Zangsun Chen) also contributed his efforts, nevertheless, according to the regular rule by which a ruler dispatches envoys—where a serviceman acts as deputy to a grand master, and a grand master acts as deputy to a minister—diplomatic messages are specially received by one person; who may encroach upon his office? Therefore the Classic mentions Sui and omits Chen; is this not the same meaning as the Book of Odes (Shi) attaching weight to the ode "Glorious Are the Flowers" (Huanghua)?

When the Souman 鄋瞞 encroached and harassed, Lu consequently raised an army to defeat the Di 狄. At that time, those who directed the troops and marched were Shusun Dechen 叔孫得臣 and Hou Shuxia 侯叔夏. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals name only Dechen? It is because the supreme commander holds the charge of exercising sole authority outside the palace gates, and the state depends on him to attain security. In the campaign at Xian 鹹, wielding the battle-axe and facing the enemy, Dechen was the arbiter of fate for the Three Armies, and subordinate generals could not stand alongside him. Even though it is said that in the capture of Qiaoru 僑如, Houshu (Hou Shuxia) also achieved merit, nevertheless, according to the regular rule by which a ruler appoints a general—not estranging him through personal favorites, nor interfering with him through petty men—military laws and orders have a single master; who may divide his authority? Therefore the Classic names Dechen and omits Xia; is this not the same meaning as the Book of Changes (Yi) attaching weight to the "experienced leader" (zhangren)?

Viewed in this light, the envoy and the general each had the weight of their charges emphasized, and the hierarchical system was rectified. As for those instances where deputies and subordinates are also recorded together, those represent exceptional precedents; how could one be rigidly bound by them? Yet regarding these two campaigns, when Qi first…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
伐我僖則資武于楚狄繼侵齊文乃奮威于狄
不思楚亦狄也狄亦楚也齊可讎也匪可親也
二君何倒行逆施如是若後之辭獻納而富甲
兵者其明使將之義者哉
禮記
故禮也者義之實也協諸義而協則禮雖
先王未之有可以義起也義者藝之分
仁之節也協於藝講於仁得之者强仁
者義之本也順之體也得之者尊
===
同考試官教諭諸批仁義禮相須治情必由之
是作渾融邃雅蓋深于禮者
考試官教諭鄭批詞理精到一洗浮華
考試官學正馮批發揮明透
聖王治情之道皆妙於相須者焉夫禮義仁所
以治情也其道固相須者而可偏廢哉且人情
不齊聖王備道以防範之故嘗修禮以耕之矣
禮非强世也本圓神以定制緣時措以作儀禮
banxin: 鄉試錄 四十四 陳良材
punctuated:
伐我，僖則資武于楚；狄繼侵齊，文乃奮威于狄。不思楚亦狄也，狄亦楚也，齊可讎也，匪可親也。二君何倒行逆施如是？若後之辭獻納而富甲兵者，其明使將之義者哉！

《禮記》

「故禮也者，義之實也。協諸義而協，則禮雖先王未之有，可以義起也。義者，藝之分、仁之節也。協於藝，講於仁，得之者强。仁者，義之本也、順之體也，得之者尊。」

同考試官教諭諸批：仁、義、禮相須，治情必由之。是作渾融邃雅，蓋深于《禮》者。
考試官教諭鄭批：詞理精到，一洗浮華。
考試官學正馮批：發揮明透。

聖王治情之道，皆妙於相須者焉。夫禮、義、仁，所以治情也；其道固相須者，而可偏廢哉？且人情不齊，聖王備道以防範之，故嘗修禮以耕之矣。禮非强世也，本圓神以定制，緣時措以作儀，禮
translation_en:
… attacked us, Duke Xi relied on the military might of Chu; when the Di subsequently invaded Qi, Duke Wen then exerted his martial authority over the Di. They failed to consider that Chu is no different from the Di, and the Di are no different from Chu; while Qi might be treated as a rival, those others must never be befriended. Why did the two rulers act in such a perverse and retrograde manner? As for the later ruler who declined the presentation of captives and spoils and instead enriched his state with armor and weaponry, how well he understood the righteous principle of commissioning generals!

Book of Rites (Liji)

"Therefore, ritual is the substantive embodiment of righteousness. If a practice is measured against righteousness and found to be in harmony with it, then even if it is a ritual that the former kings never had, it may be instituted on the basis of righteousness. Righteousness is the proper apportionment of practical skills and the modulation of benevolence. He who harmonizes with practical skills and cultivates benevolence, and thereby attains righteousness, becomes strong. Benevolence is the root of righteousness and the embodiment of順 [accordance/harmony]; he who attains it becomes honored."

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu: Benevolence, righteousness, and ritual depend upon one another, and governing human feelings must proceed through them. This essay is seamlessly integrated, profound, and elegant—surely the work of one deeply versed in the Rites.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: The diction and reasoning are precise and thorough, completely washing away superficiality and ostentation.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Feng: The exposition is clear and penetrating.

The Ways by which the sage kings governed human feelings all achieved their subtlety through mutual dependence. Now, ritual, righteousness, and benevolence are the means by which human feelings are governed; since their ways inherently depend upon one another, how could any one of them be neglected in favor of the others? Moreover, because human feelings are uneven, the sage kings prepared the Way in its completeness to regulate and bound them; thus they once cultivated ritual as if plowing the field. Ritual does not forcibly constrain the world; grounded in encompassing spirit to establish regulations, and adapting to timely application to create ceremonies, ritual …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
乃義之實焉而先王制禮之精意惟有得於義
耳夫苟因時制宜適協乎天理之公則稱情立
文自可爲人事之則雖不必創於先王而禮自
我出矣禮非可以義起者乎亦甞陳義以種之
矣義果何如者耶以立萬事之閑以節因心之
愛夫固藝之分而仁之節也協藝講仁而於義
有得焉則好義足以服民固天下之所望而震
焉者矣何强如之又甞本仁以聚之矣仁果何
如者耶以立化裁之基以裕達順之原夫固義
===
之本而順之體也精義達順而於仁有得焉則
體仁足以長人固天下之所仰而慕焉者矣何
尊如之是其爲道不同而交錯互用無非管攝
身心之要爲德不一而渾融妙合要皆綱紀人
道之原此先王以之治情也而豈徒哉抑先王
治情之道甞耨之以學安之以樂矣而此獨遺
焉何哉蓋禮義仁足以成德而學也者講明乎
此也樂也者和樂乎此也要在會通之焉耳噫
以此防民民猶有溺於情者
punctuated: 乃義之實焉，而先王制禮之精意，惟有得於義耳。夫苟因時制宜，適協乎天理之公，則稱情立文，自可爲人事之則；雖不必創於先王，而禮自我出矣。禮非可以義起者乎？亦甞陳義以種之矣，義果何如者耶？以立萬事之閑，以節因心之愛，夫固藝之分而仁之節也。協藝講仁，而於義有得焉，則好義足以服民，固天下之所望而震焉者矣，何强如之！又甞本仁以聚之矣，仁果何如者耶？以立化裁之基，以裕達順之原，夫固義之本而順之體也。精義達順，而於仁有得焉，則體仁足以長人，固天下之所仰而慕焉者矣，何尊如之！是其爲道不同，而交錯互用，無非管攝身心之要；爲德不一，而渾融妙合，要皆綱紀人道之原。此先王以之治情也，而豈徒哉？抑先王治情之道，甞耨之以學、安之以樂矣，而此獨遺焉，何哉？蓋禮、義、仁足以成德，而學也者，講明乎此也；樂也者，和樂乎此也，要在會通之焉耳。噫！以此防民，民猶有溺於情者。
translation_en:
… is in fact the substance of righteousness (yi), and the subtle intent of the former kings in instituting ritual (li) lay solely in what was attained through righteousness. Indeed, if one adapts to the times to determine what is appropriate, fittingly harmonizing with the impartiality of heavenly principle, then establishing cultural forms in accordance with human feelings can naturally serve as the standard for human affairs; even if they had not been originated by the former kings, ritual would still issue forth from ourselves. May ritual not be initiated on the basis of righteousness?

They also set forth righteousness so as to plant them [human feelings]. What, then, is righteousness really like? Serving to establish the bounds for the myriad affairs and to regulate the love that arises from the heart, it is indeed the measure of practical capability (yi 藝) and the moderator of benevolence (ren). When one harmonizes capabilities and cultivates benevolence, and thereby attains righteousness, then loving righteousness is sufficient to win the submission of the people; he is naturally someone upon whom the whole world looks with awe—what strength could compare to getting this!

They also rooted them in benevolence so as to gather them together. What, then, is benevolence really like? Serving to establish the foundation for transformation and regulation, and to enrich the source of pervasive compliance (shun), it is indeed the root of righteousness and the substance of compliance. When one refines righteousness and achieves compliance, and thereby attains benevolence, then embodying benevolence is sufficient to be a leader of men; he is naturally someone to whom the whole world looks up in admiration—what honor could compare to getting this!

Thus their ways are different, yet through their interplay and mutual application, they are nothing less than the essentials for governing body and mind; their virtues are not uniform, yet in their seamless and subtle integration, they are in sum the source for ordering the way of humanity. It was by these means that the former kings governed human feelings—and could it have been in vain?

Yet in the former kings' way of governing human feelings, they also weeded them with learning and settled them with music; why are those alone omitted here? It is because ritual, righteousness, and benevolence are sufficient to bring virtue to completion, while learning is the elucidation of these, and music is finding joyful harmony in these; the key lies simply in comprehending them as an integrated whole. Alas! Even when using these as a dike for the people, there are still people who drown in their feelings.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
大樂與天地同和大禮與天地同節和故
百物不失節故祀天祭地明則有禮樂
幽則有鬼神如此則四海之內合敬同
愛矣
譚一召
同考試官教諭諸批禮樂和序貫徹造化人心
子獨究本旨而詞能達意知禮樂之情者
考試官教諭鄭批體裁嚴整說亦有味
考試官學正馮批明潔雅鬯
===
禮樂之成功合造化而感人心也蓋禮樂不外
乎和序也和序旣至造化且不違也而况於人
乎樂記之意謂夫天人有一致之理制作極感
通之妙彼大樂人知由天作也而不知與天地
同和焉蓋天地本有自然之和而樂則敦和以
率神殆有與之相焉融液者矣大禮人知由地
制也而不知與天地同節焉蓋天地本有自然
之節而禮則別宜以居鬼殆有與之相焉脗合
者矣惟和則以和召和而百物由之不失焉竝
punctuated:
大樂與天地同和，大禮與天地同節。和故百物不失，節故祀天祭地。明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神。如此，則四海之內合敬同愛矣。
譚一召
同考試官教諭諸批：禮樂和序，貫徹造化人心。子獨究本旨，而詞能達意，知禮樂之情者。
考試官教諭鄭批：體裁嚴整，說亦有味。
考試官學正馮批：明潔雅鬯。
禮樂之成功，合造化而感人心也。蓋禮樂不外乎和、序也。和、序旣至，造化且不違也，而况於人乎？《樂記》之意，謂夫天人有一致之理，制作極感通之妙。彼大樂，人知由天作也，而不知與天地同和焉。蓋天地本有自然之和，而樂則敦和以率神，殆有與之相焉融液者矣。大禮，人知由地制也，而不知與天地同節焉。蓋天地本有自然之節，而禮則別宜以居鬼，殆有與之相焉脗合者矣。惟和，則以和召和，而百物由之不失焉，竝
translation_en:
"Great music shares the same harmony as Heaven and Earth; great rites share the same order as Heaven and Earth. Because of this harmony, the hundred things do not lose their proper nature; because of this order, sacrifices are offered to Heaven and Earth. In the visible realm there are rites and music, and in the unseen realm there are ghosts and spirits. When it is thus, all within the Four Seas will unite in reverence and join in affection."

Tan Yizhao 譚一召

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu 諸: The harmony and order of rites and music penetrate both the creative transformations of nature and the human mind. You alone have probed the fundamental purport, and your words effectively convey the meaning—truly one who understands the essence of rites and music.

Comment by Examiner and County Instructor Zheng 鄭: The structure is rigorous and well-ordered, and the exposition also has depth and flavor.

Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Feng 馮: Clear, concise, elegant, and fluent.

The perfected achievement of rites and music unites with the creative transformations of nature and moves the human mind. For rites and music are nothing other than harmony and order. Once harmony and order reach their utmost, even the creative forces of nature do not go against them—how much less so human beings! The purport of the Record of Music (Yueji) is that Heaven and humanity share a single unified principle, and the institution of rites and music achieves the utmost subtlety of sympathetic resonance. As for great music, people know that it is created in accordance with Heaven, yet they do not know that it shares the same harmony as Heaven and Earth. For Heaven and Earth originally possess a natural harmony, and music cultivates harmony so as to lead the spirits, thereby almost melting and blending together with them [?]. As for great rites, people know that they are instituted in accordance with Earth, yet they do not know that they share the same order as Heaven and Earth. For Heaven and Earth originally possess a natural order, and rites distinguish what is fitting so as to settle the ghosts, thereby almost matching and tallying seamlessly with them [?]. Because there is harmony, harmony summons harmony, and through it the hundred things do not lose their proper nature; together…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
育於化醇之中者熈如也惟節則以序召序而
天地可以祭祀焉黙享於精禋之表者秩如也
是可見禮樂鬼神循其名固有幽明之别究其
理初無彼此之殊禮樂之合乎造化如此四海
之内有不感孚者哉吾見分之所在而敬同焉
燦然有文以相接其至禮不讓而天下治者與
情之所在而愛同焉驩然有恩以相洽其至樂
無聲而天下和者與夫同和同節是能贊乎化
育矣合敬同愛是能管乎人情矣聖人禮樂之
===
盛何如哉抑論聖人建中和之極而天地幽明
舉會於一心故形諸制作而感通之妙自有莫
知其所以然者使本之則無則禮樂且不爲之
用矣况於人乎况於天地乎於此可以觀制作
之本
第貳場
論
文王朢道未見
王命爵
punctuated:
育於化醇之中者，熈如也。惟節則以序召序，而天地可以祭祀焉，黙享於精禋之表者，秩如也。是可見禮樂鬼神，循其名固有幽明之别，究其理初無彼此之殊。禮樂之合乎造化如此，四海之内有不感孚者哉？吾見分之所在而敬同焉，燦然有文以相接，其至禮不讓而天下治者與！情之所在而愛同焉，驩然有恩以相洽，其至樂無聲而天下和者與！夫同和同節，是能贊乎化育矣；合敬同愛，是能管乎人情矣。聖人禮樂之盛，何如哉！抑論聖人建中和之極，而天地幽明舉會於一心，故形諸制作，而感通之妙自有莫知其所以然者。使本之則無，則禮樂且不爲之用矣，况於人乎？况於天地乎？於此可以觀制作之本。

第貳場
論
《文王朢道未見》
王命爵
translation_en:
…nurtured together amidst the generative vitalities, flourishing in joyful harmony. Because there is due measure, order summons forth order, so that Heaven and Earth may receive sacrifices, silently partaking beyond the pure offerings in regular array. From this it can be seen that as for rites, music, ghosts, and spirits, if one follows their names there is indeed a distinction between the unseen and the manifest, yet if one investigates their principles there was never any difference between the one and the other. When rites and music accord with the creative transformations in such a way, could anyone within the Four Seas fail to be moved and inspired with trust? I see that wherever distinctions of status exist, reverence is shared: resplendently they interact through refined pattern—is this not supreme ritual, whereby the world is well governed even without yielding? Wherever human feelings exist, affection is shared: joyously they blend through kindness—is this not supreme music, whereby the world is brought to harmony even without sound? Now, sharing the harmony and sharing the measure of Heaven and Earth means being able to assist in the transforming and nourishing processes of nature; uniting reverence and sharing affection means being able to govern human sentiments. How magnificent are the rites and music of the sages! Yet if we consider how the sage establishes the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony, so that Heaven and Earth, the unseen and the manifest, all converge within a single mind—therefore, when this is given form in institutions and creations, the marvel of its resonance and penetration naturally operates without anyone knowing how it does so. If the fundamental root is absent, then even rites and music will not serve their purpose—how much less so with human beings, and how much less so with Heaven and Earth! From this one may observe the foundation of the sage's creations.

Second Session
Discourse
"King Wen Looked Toward the Way as Though He Had Not Yet Seen It"
Wang Mingjue 王命爵

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭姚批望道未見乃聖不自聖之
心也此作能發明之而詞更古雅宜錄以式
同考試官教諭薄批就本題發揮而聖人道統
之傳宛然在目非淺學可到
考試官教諭鄭批調高詞古
考試官學正馮批善言聖人之心者取之
聖人之會道也以心是故其心常運而於道常
見其無窮夫心者道之管也道不可窮而以有
窮之心視之則將自限於其所至而一息少間
===
忽不自知其去道之遠矣聖人之心與道爲一
道無窮聖人之心亦無窮雖精神之所孚契固
以獨得其真猶不敢以所至者自信而恒以未
至者自疑蓋有終其身望之亦終其身茫乎若
未之見者嗚呼此聖人之所以爲純其心而天
下之道所以會於聖人歟今夫道之大原出於
天天之爲道無思焉爾矣無爲焉爾矣然闔闢
則不窮其變往來則不窮其通生長收藏則不
窮其化動盪環轉常若有所推乎其内而不容
punctuated:
同考試官教諭姚批：「『望道未見』，乃聖不自聖之心也。此作能發明之，而詞更古雅，宜錄以式。」
同考試官教諭薄批：「就本題發揮，而聖人道統之傳宛然在目，非淺學可到。」
考試官教諭鄭批：「調高詞古。」
考試官學正馮批：「善言聖人之心者，取之。」

聖人之會道也以心，是故其心常運，而於道常見其無窮。夫心者，道之管也。道不可窮，而以有窮之心視之，則將自限於其所至，而一息少間，忽不自知其去道之遠矣。聖人之心與道爲一，道無窮，聖人之心亦無窮。雖精神之所孚契，固以獨得其真，猶不敢以所至者自信，而恒以未至者自疑；蓋有終其身望之，亦終其身茫乎若未之見者。嗚呼！此聖人之所以爲純其心，而天下之道所以會於聖人歟！

今夫道之大原出於天。天之爲道，無思焉爾矣，無爲焉爾矣。然闔闢則不窮其變，往來則不窮其通，生長收藏則不窮其化，動盪環轉，常若有所推乎其内，而不容
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yao [comments]: "'Looking toward the Way as if he had not yet seen it' is the mind of a sage who does not regard himself as a sage. This composition is able to elucidate this, and its diction is moreover antique and elegant; it should be recorded as a model."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Bo [comments]: "It elaborates closely upon the theme itself, and the transmission of the sages' orthodoxy of the Way stands vividly before one's eyes—something shallow learning could not attain."
Examiner and Instructor Zheng [comments]: "Lofty in tone and antique in diction."
Examiner and Director of Studies Feng [comments]: "One who speaks well of the mind of the sage; select it."

The sage comprehends the Way through his mind; therefore his mind is constantly in motion, and in the Way he constantly sees its inexhaustibility. Now the mind is the pivot of the Way. The Way cannot be exhausted, and if one views it with an exhaustible mind, one will limit oneself to what one has already attained; with the slightest pause of a single breath, one will suddenly be unaware how far removed one has become from the Way. The mind of the sage is one with the Way; the Way is inexhaustible, and the mind of the sage is likewise inexhaustible. Although in the spiritual communion of his mind he has indeed uniquely grasped its truth, he still does not dare to be self-assured in what he has attained, and constantly doubts himself over what he has not yet attained. Thus throughout his entire life he looks toward it, and throughout his entire life he remains as though vast and uncertain, as if he had not yet seen it. Alas! Is this not how the sage keeps his mind pure, and why the Way of all under heaven converges in the sage?

Now the great source of the Way comes from Heaven. As for Heaven's being the Way, it has no deliberate thought, and it has no deliberate action. Yet in its closing and opening it is inexhaustible in its transformations; in its going and coming it is inexhaustible in its penetration; in its generating, nourishing, harvesting, and storing it is inexhaustible in its transmutations. Stirring and revolving in cycles, it is constantly as though something were propelling it from within, not allowing…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
有頃刻之停無思而無乎不思無爲而無乎不
爲天之所以運乎道者其心固如此也天心常
運故貞觀于上而天下之道盡於天聖心常運
故貞一於下而天下之道盡於聖聖人之道何
道也顯之於散殊則爲物秩之於經常則爲倫
蘊之於所性則爲仁義粹而無所雜則謂之善
時措而無所偏倚則謂之中人得此以靈於物
而同異之分間不容髮則謂之幾希名殊而致
一者也前乎此而聖者非此無以開其先後乎
===
此而聖者非此無以紹其緒由禹湯而降斯道
之統之傳文王身之矣其所以朢而至之期而
趨之者又烏能以自已乎夫其朢之也固欲如
舜之明之察之也而以明且察自足焉則將有
擇焉而不精者矣其朢之也固欲如舜之由之
也而以旣由自足焉則將有由焉而未至者矣
其朢之也固欲如禹之好之湯之執之也而以
好且執自足焉則將有好焉而或遷執焉而未
固者矣何也心一也不操則必舍不斂則必逸
punctuated: 有頃刻之停。無思而無乎不思，無爲而無乎不爲，天之所以運乎道者，其心固如此也。天心常運，故貞觀于上，而天下之道盡於天；聖心常運，故貞一於下，而天下之道盡於聖。聖人之道，何道也？顯之於散殊則爲物，秩之於經常則爲倫，蘊之於所性則爲仁義，粹而無所雜則謂之善，時措而無所偏倚則謂之中，人得此以靈於物，而同異之分間不容髮則謂之幾希，名殊而致一者也。前乎此而聖者，非此無以開其先；後乎此而聖者，非此無以紹其緒。由禹、湯而降，斯道之統之傳，文王身之矣。其所以朢而至之、期而趨之者，又烏能以自已乎？夫其朢之也，固欲如舜之明之、察之也，而以明且察自足焉，則將有擇焉而不精者矣；其朢之也，固欲如舜之由之也，而以旣由自足焉，則將有由焉而未至者矣；其朢之也，固欲如禹之好之、湯之執之也，而以好且執自足焉，則將有好焉而或遷、執焉而未固者矣。何也？心一也，不操則必舍，不斂則必逸，
translation_en: … have even a moment's pause. Having no deliberate thought and yet leaving nothing unthought, taking no deliberate action and yet leaving nothing undone—such indeed is the mind by which Heaven revolves the Way. Because the mind of Heaven is ever revolving, it displays constant correctness above, and the Way of all under heaven is exhausted in Heaven; because the mind of the sage is ever revolving, it maintains constant unity below, and the Way of all under heaven is exhausted in the sage. What Way is this Way of the sage? Manifested in diverse particulars, it is things; ordered in constant norms, it is human relationships; treasured within one's endowed nature, it is benevolence and righteousness; pure and unadulterated, it is called goodness; timely in its application and without inclination or partiality, it is called the Mean; obtained by human beings so as to be more spiritual than myriad creatures—where the distinction of similarity and difference does not admit even a hair's breadth—it is called that "slightest fraction." Though their names differ, they arrive at the same unity. Those who were sages before this had nothing else by which to open the path ahead; those who were sages after this had nothing else by which to continue the line of transmission. Coming down from Yu and Tang, the succession and transmission of this Way was embodied in King Wen. In gazing toward it to reach it, and in setting his expectation upon it to hasten toward it, how could he possibly stop himself? Now, in gazing toward it, he certainly wished, like Shun, to clearly understand it and closely examine it; yet if one is self-satisfied with having understood and examined it, there will be something imprecise in one's choosing. In gazing toward it, he certainly wished, like Shun, to follow it; yet if one is self-satisfied with having already followed it, there will be something unattained in one's following. In gazing toward it, he certainly wished, like Yu, to love it and, like Tang, to hold fast to it; yet if one is self-satisfied with loving and holding fast to it, there will be times when one's love shifts and one's grasp is not firm. Why is this? The mind is one: if it is not held fast, it will surely be let go; if it is not gathered in, it will surely stray; …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不聚則必散無二用也道一也不明則必蔽不
合則必離不融則必乖無二機也以彼文王之
聖亦奚有夫未見之道哉顧其所見者道也其
所未見者心也以未見之心視旣見之道故其
見愈真而其所以求見者愈切凝神於亦臨亦
保之中而泯其畔援歆羨之迹聚精於日旦曰
明之表而忘其聲色知識之私廓然至虛無所
不備而朢之猶若有所遺也炳然至靈無所不
照而朢之猶若有所眩也純亦不已無始無終
===
而朢之猶若有所間也惟其心若有所遺而後
至虛者常涵道之溥博而無外者由此而體其
撰矣惟其心若有所眩而後至靈者常瑩道之
變化而不測者由此而會其神矣惟其心若有
所間而後純亦不已者常存道之流行而無止
息者由此而立其極矣是故人見文王之聖在
帝左右而不知其心則亹亹也人見文王之聖
緝熈敬止而不知其心則穆穆也人見文王之
聖先登于岸而不知其心則翼翼也以此而紹
punctuated: 不聚則必散，無二用也。道一也，不明則必蔽，不合則必離，不融則必乖，無二機也。以彼文王之聖，亦奚有夫未見之道哉？顧其所見者，道也；其所未見者，心也。以未見之心，視旣見之道，故其見愈真，而其所以求見者愈切。凝神於「亦臨亦保」之中，而泯其「畔援歆羨」之迹；聚精於「日旦曰明」之表，而忘其「聲色知識」之私。廓然至虛，無所不備，而朢之猶若有所遺也；炳然至靈，無所不照，而朢之猶若有所眩也；純亦不已，無始無終，而朢之猶若有所間也。惟其心若有所遺，而後至虛者常涵，道之溥博而無外者，由此而體其撰矣；惟其心若有所眩，而後至靈者常瑩，道之變化而不測者，由此而會其神矣；惟其心若有所間，而後純亦不已者常存，道之流行而無止息者，由此而立其極矣。是故人見文王之聖「在帝左右」，而不知其心則「亹亹」也；人見文王之聖「緝熈敬止」，而不知其心則「穆穆」也；人見文王之聖「先登于岸」，而不知其心則「翼翼」也。以此而紹
translation_en: … if not gathered, it will inevitably disperse—it cannot function in two ways at once. The Way is one: if not illuminated, it will inevitably be obscured; if not united, it will inevitably be separated; if not harmonized, it will inevitably be at odds—it has no dual mechanism. Given such sageliness as that of King Wen (Wen Wang 文王), how could there actually be any part of the Way that he had not yet seen? Yet what he had seen was the Way, whereas what considered it not yet seen was his mind. Because he viewed the Way he had already seen with a mind that felt it had not yet seen it, his vision became all the truer, and his quest to see it all the more earnest. He concentrated his spirit amidst "acting as if approached, as if preserved," obliterating any trace of "factiousness or covetousness"; he gathered his essence beyond "the dawn and the light of day," forgetting the private biases of "sound, appearance, and conscious knowledge." Vast and supremely empty, lacking nothing, yet when he looked toward it, it was as though something were still left out; radiant and supremely numinous, illuminating everything, yet when he looked toward it, it was as though his eyes were still dazzled; pure and unceasing, without beginning or end, yet when he looked toward it, it was as though there were still interruptions. Precisely because his mind felt as though something were left out, the supremely empty was constantly nurtured within, and through this he embodied the substance of the Way in its all-encompassing vastness without exterior. Precisely because his mind felt as though it were dazzled, the supremely numinous remained constantly pellucid, and through this he comprehended the unfathomable transformations of the Way in their spirit. Precisely because his mind felt as though there were interruptions, what is pure and unceasing was constantly preserved, and through this he established the ultimate standard of the Way in its ceaseless flow. Therefore, people saw King Wen's sageliness as "being at the left and right of the Lord on High," without knowing that his mind was "unwearying"; people saw King Wen's sageliness as "continuing in bright and reverent rest," without knowing that his mind was "profoundly solemn"; people saw King Wen's sageliness as "ascending first to the high shore," without knowing that his mind was "cautious and reverent." By means of this, he carried on from …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
舜則爲明物爲察倫爲由仁義而舜之所以見
道者此心而已矣以此而紹禹湯則爲好善爲
執中而禹湯之所以見道者此心而已矣何也
道本若是其無窮也以有窮視道者狃於其所
見而不知易見之非道也以無窮視道者疑於
其所未見而不知未見之爲眞見也故於未見
而可以識文王之心於其心而可以識文王之
見於穆不足以盡天於穆而不已則說天者莫
辨乎此矣不顯不足以盡文王不顯而純則論
===
文王者莫辨乎此矣武王之不泄不忘也朢道
於遠近而未見之心合遠近而一之也周公之
夜以繼日也朢道於四事而未見之心合四事
而一之也此武周之所以得統於文也非直此
耳孔子天縱之聖也而曰吾有知乎哉無知也
夫無不知而視之爲無知亦猶文王之無不見
而視之爲無見也萬古一道千聖一心學者欲
得其心法之傳以紹斯道之統則將何始乎亦
曰有若無而已實若虛而已學顏子之學則能
punctuated: 舜，則爲明物、爲察倫、爲由仁義，而舜之所以見道者，此心而已矣；以此而紹禹、湯，則爲好善、爲執中，而禹、湯之所以見道者，此心而已矣。何也？道本若是其無窮也。以有窮視道者，狃於其所見，而不知易見之非道也；以無窮視道者，疑於其所未見，而不知未見之爲眞見也。故於未見而可以識文王之心，於其心而可以識文王之見。「於穆」不足以盡天，「於穆」而「不已」，則說天者莫辨乎此矣；「不顯」不足以盡文王，「不顯」而「純」，則論文王者莫辨乎此矣。武王之不泄不忘也，朢道於遠近，而未見之心合遠近而一之也；周公之夜以繼日也，朢道於四事，而未見之心合四事而一之也。此武、周之所以得統於文也。非直此耳，孔子天縱之聖也，而曰：「吾有知乎哉？無知也。」夫無不知而視之爲無知，亦猶文王之無不見而視之爲無見也。萬古一道，千聖一心，學者欲得其心法之傳，以紹斯道之統，則將何始乎？亦曰「有若無」而已，「實若虛」而已。學顏子之學，則能
translation_en: … Shun, it was his clarity about all things, his keen discernment of human relationships, and his acting out of benevolence and righteousness—and that by which Shun perceived the Way was nothing other than this mind. Succeeding Yu and Tang with this, it was Yu's fondness for good words and Tang's holding fast to the Mean—and that by which Yu and Tang perceived the Way was nothing other than this mind. Why is this? Because the Way is inherently thus boundless. Those who view the Way as finite grow complacent in what they have already seen, not realizing that what is easily seen is not the Way; those who view the Way as boundless remain tentative toward what they have not yet seen, not realizing that looking toward the unseen is true perception. Therefore, from his looking as though he had not yet seen it, one can recognize the mind of King Wen; and from his mind, one can recognize King Wen's perception. "Oh, how profound" is not enough to exhaust Heaven; only with "Oh, how profound and unceasing" is there nothing more discerning among explanations of Heaven. "Was it not illustrious" is not enough to exhaust King Wen; only with "Was it not illustrious and pure" is there nothing more discerning among discussions of King Wen. In King Wu's neither neglecting the near nor forgetting the distant, he looked for the Way in what was near and far, and his mind that looked as though it had not yet seen united the near and the far into one. In the Duke of Zhou's continuing from night into day, he looked for the Way in the four undertakings, and his mind that looked as though it had not yet seen united the four undertakings into one. This is how King Wu and the Duke of Zhou received the succession of the Way from King Wen. Nor is it only thus: Confucius was a sage endowed by Heaven, yet he said, "Do I possess knowledge? No, I have no knowledge." Now, to know all things and yet regard oneself as having no knowledge is just like King Wen's seeing all things and yet regarding himself as having seen nothing. Through ten thousand ages there is one Way; among a thousand sages there is one mind. If a scholar wishes to obtain the transmission of the method of the mind so as to continue the succession of this Way, where then should he begin? It is simply to "have, yet seem to lack," and to "be full, yet seem empty." If one learns the learning of Master Yan [Yan Hui], then one will be able to …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
心先聖之心而幾希之理所以自靈於萬物而
卓然於庶民者亦庶乎其在我矣
表
擬輔臣進文武職名
御屏表〔萬曆二年〕
江楫
同考試官教諭馮批因名責實進
屏之本意也子本以忠悃之心發爲麗藻之詞其不凡士耶
同考試官教諭姚批莊重典則冲澹和平此四
===
六之最佳者可錄
考試官教諭鄭批莊嚴得體
考試官學正馮批典實不浮
萬曆二年某月某日具官臣某等謹以文
武職名
御屏上進者
帝王圖理責實爲先臣子效忠達聰尤要方萬
化維新之始正羣工交飭之時願獻愚忱
用裨
punctuated:
心先聖之心，而幾希之理，所以自靈於萬物而卓然於庶民者，亦庶乎其在我矣。

表

擬輔臣進文武職名御屏表〔萬曆二年〕
江楫
同考試官教諭馮批：因名責實，進屏之本意也。子本以忠悃之心，發爲麗藻之詞，其不凡士耶？

translation_en:
…take the minds of the former sages as their own mind, and the subtle principle by which we are more spiritually endowed than the myriad things and stand out above the common people will perhaps also reside within us!

Memorial (Biao)

Draft Memorial of the Grand Secretaries Presenting an Imperial Screen Inscribed with the Names and Titles of Civil and Military Officials [Second Year of Wanli (1574)]
Jiang Ji 
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Feng comments: Demanding reality on the basis of titles is the original intent of presenting the screen. Taking a heart of loyal sincerity as your foundation, you have expressed it in ornate and elegant words—are you not an extraordinary scholar?
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Yao comments: Solemn and classic in form, serene and harmonious in tone; this is the finest of parallel prose (siliu) and worthy of recording.
Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng comments: Dignified and appropriate to the genre.
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng comments: Classical, substantive, and free of superficiality.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
宸鑒臣等誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟虞廷稽古
以亮工乃成屢省周室備官以立政厥若
灼知師師而庶績其凝濟濟而兆民俾乂
蓋用人既精於鑒別故致治自躋於煕隆
世變漸趨官聯彌濫幽明之典悉委諸司
存章癉之權靡關於獨斷屏疏刺史竟綜
覈之罔聞圖列百官惟叙遷之是計即省
臺廊署之邇姓名已不及知矧甸服要荒
之遐閱歷何繇致察堂廉遼隔淹速混淆
===
以故玩愒成風視地方如傳舍甚至榮肥
溺志等職業於弁髦吏治多奸民功莫叙
相襲已成乎積弊更張有待於
明時顧轉移之機在上而不在下且簡稽之
要以實而不以名惟權衡常注於
淵衷庶臧否莫廋於兼照然非出入起居之
際觸目而興思尤恐職銜名次之多掛一
而遺十知人則哲信自帝以其難託物納
忠惟
punctuated: 宸鑒。臣等誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟虞廷稽古以亮工，乃成屢省；周室備官以立政，厥若灼知。師師而庶績其凝，濟濟而兆民俾乂。蓋用人既精於鑒別，故致治自躋於煕隆。世變漸趨，官聯彌濫。幽明之典，悉委諸司存；章癉之權，靡關於獨斷。屏疏刺史，竟綜覈之罔聞；圖列百官，惟叙遷之是計。即省臺廊署之邇，姓名已不及知；矧甸服要荒之遐，閱歷何繇致察？堂廉遼隔，淹速混淆。以故玩愒成風，視地方如傳舍；甚至榮肥溺志，等職業於弁髦。吏治多奸，民功莫叙。相襲已成乎積弊，更張有待於明時。顧轉移之機在上而不在下，且簡稽之要以實而不以名。惟權衡常注於淵衷，庶臧否莫廋於兼照。然非出入起居之際，觸目而興思，尤恐職銜名次之多，掛一而遺十。知人則哲，信自帝以其難；託物納忠，惟…
translation_en:
…the imperial judgment. Your servants, in utmost fear and trepidation, bow our heads to the ground.

We humbly reflect that when the court of Yu examined antiquity to assist in the works, it achieved success through frequent inspection; when the House of Zhou established offices to order governance, it conformed to clear understanding. With officials emulating one another, all achievements were consolidated; in dignified multitude, the millions of people were brought to order. Because the employment of men was refined through discerning judgment, the attainment of good governance naturally ascended to prosperous heights.

As the times gradually changed, official posts became increasingly excessive. The canons of demotion and promotion were entirely delegated to the routine of functionaries; the authority to distinguish good and evil no longer depended on the ruler's sole decision. Regional Inspectors were listed on screens, yet ultimately nothing was heard of their comprehensive verification; the hundred officials were arrayed on charts, yet only the order of their promotions was calculated. Even for those close at hand in the central ministries, censorate, and capital offices, their names are already beyond the ruler's acquaintance; how much more so for those far away in the royal domain and the remote borderlands—by what means can their careers and performances be examined? The hall and its steps are widely separated, and stagnation and rapid advancement are confounded.

For this reason, negligence and idling have become the prevailing wind, and officials regard their localities as mere relay inns; some even drown their ambitions in glory and self-enrichment, treating their professional duties like discarded caps. Official administration is rife with deceit, and merits on behalf of the people go unrecorded. Passed down from one to another, this has become an accumulated abuse; its reform awaits an enlightened era.

Yet the pivot of transformation lies above and not below, and the essence of selection and inspection lies in reality and not in name. Only when the balance of judgment is constantly fixed in the profound imperial mind will good and bad have nowhere to hide beneath Your all-encompassing illumination. However, unless Your Majesty's eyes are struck and thoughts aroused during Your daily movements and repose, it is especially to be feared that amid the multitude of official titles and rosters, taking note of one will mean overlooking ten. To know men is wisdom—truly even the Emperor of old found it difficult; entrusting our loyalty to an object, we only…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
凝神之是冀茲蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
命基宥密
道邁敬承隆尊養於
慈闈
孝思維則勤咨詢於
講幄
聖學懋昭百度惟貞猶厪徹桑之慮四夷率服
不忘集蓼之思儆官邪則
===
踐祚之初即
示羣臣以蕩平皇路嚴武備則防秋之候復
諭諸將以震疊威稜
所無逸以知艱慮恒周乎民瘼
承顯思而敬止德克當乎
天心二百年熙洽之休方隆而未艾億萬載靈
長之慶益引而彌昌臣等繆列贊襄莫圖
報塞惟念人材進退之際實係理道隆汙
之幾雖九六陰陽陳於
punctuated: 凝神之是冀。茲蓋伏遇皇帝陛下：命基宥密，道邁敬承。隆尊養於慈闈，孝思維則；勤咨詢於講幄，聖學懋昭。百度惟貞，猶厪徹桑之慮；四夷率服，不忘集蓼之思。儆官邪，則踐祚之初，即示羣臣以蕩平皇路；嚴武備，則防秋之候，復諭諸將以震疊威稜。所無逸以知艱，慮恒周乎民瘼；承顯思而敬止，德克當乎天心。二百年熙洽之休，方隆而未艾；億萬載靈長之慶，益引而彌昌。臣等繆列贊襄，莫圖報塞，惟念人材進退之際，實係理道隆汙之幾。雖九六陰陽，陳於
translation_en:
… hoping that Your Majesty will fix your mind upon it.

Now we humbly encounter Your Majesty the Emperor, whose Mandate is grounded in quiet profundity, and whose Way excels in reverent succession. Exalting the honor and nourishment of the Empress Dowager's quarters, your filial thoughts serve as a model; diligently consulting at the Classics-Mat lectures, your sagely learning shines brightly. All measures of governance are upright, yet you still harbor the precautionary concern of gathering mulberry root-bark before the rain; the four border peoples all submit, yet you do not forget the bitter toil of gathering smartweed. To warn against official misconduct, at the very beginning of your reign you showed all ministers the broad and level imperial way; to tighten military preparedness, at the season of autumn defense you again instructed the generals to inspire awe with majestic power. Dwelling in "Against Luxurious Ease" so as to know the hardships of life, your concern always encompasses the sufferings of the people; inheriting the illustrious legacy and resting in reverence, your virtue answers fully to the mind of Heaven. The harmonious blessings of two hundred years are now flourishing without end; the enduring felicity of ten thousand myriad years stretches onward ever more prosperously.

Your servants have unworthily been placed in positions to assist in governance, yet have found no way to repay your grace. We reflect only that the advancement and dismissal of men of talent is truly the pivotal factor upon which the rise and decline of good governance depend. Although the yin and yang principles of the eighty-one positives and thirty-six negatives set forth in…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
帝鑑之圖幸蒙
采納而階資浩冗麗於銓曹之籍矣自周知
謹按類以區分爰製屏以
上獻尊卑有統而百司庶府兼載以無遺大小
相維而六服羣辟並收而靡漏為惠疇為
亮采如四肢百體之各效其勞為禦侮為
折衝如四時五行之各宣其氣置之
左右而位序之考詢有據何須取信於簡書
不下
===
堂階而人官之論辨已真無庸致疑於耳目
循資以課績則御其廢御其置庶可興明
作之功隨任以程能則簡厥脩簡厥良或
少助
勵精之政心存許
國敢徒飾乎虛文人可事
君方共期乎實效伏願
舉先選眾
愛急親賢端視聽以廣聰明公是非以定取
punctuated: 《帝鑑》之圖幸蒙采納，而階資浩冗麗於銓曹之籍，奚自周知？謹按類以區分，爰製屏以上獻。尊卑有統，而百司庶府兼載以無遺；大小相維，而六服羣辟並收而靡漏。為惠疇、為亮采，如四肢百體之各效其勞；為禦侮、為折衝，如四時五行之各宣其氣。置之左右，而位序之考詢有據，何須取信於簡書？不下堂階，而人官之論辨已真，無庸致疑於耳目。循資以課績，則御其廢、御其置，庶可興明作之功；隨任以程能，則簡厥脩、簡厥良，或少助勵精之政。心存許國，敢徒飾乎虛文；人可事君，方共期乎實效。伏願舉先選眾，愛急親賢，端視聽以廣聰明，公是非以定取
translation_en: … the illustrations of the Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian) have fortunately met with Your acceptance; yet the ranks and qualifications recorded in the registers of the Ministry of Personnel are so vast and multifarious—how could they all be thoroughly known [note: 矣 appears to be a graphic error for 奚]? We have therefore respectfully classified them by category and fashioned a folding screen to present to the throne. With high and low properly ordered, all the various offices and bureaus are comprehensively recorded without omission; with great and small mutually connected, all the regional officials throughout the six domains are included together without oversight. Whether serving in beneficent governance or assisting in state affairs, they are like the four limbs and hundred parts of the body, each exerting its labor; whether defending against aggression or repelling the enemy, they are like the four seasons and five phases, each diffusing its vital force. Placed beside Your Majesty, there will be a firm basis for examining and inquiring into official ranks and precedence—what need is there to rely on consulting bamboo slips and documents? Without descending the steps of the hall, the evaluation and discernment of men and their offices will already be clear and true—there is no need to harbor doubts about what is heard and seen. By following qualifications to assess merit—directing dismissals and directing appointments—one may hope to rouse achievements of enlightened vigor; by measuring ability according to responsibility—selecting the cultivated and selecting the worthy—this may slightly assist Your Majesty's administration of diligent governance. With hearts set on devoting ourselves to the state, how would we dare merely adorn empty words? Only by presenting men fit to serve the sovereign do we together hope for practical results. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will promote the upright by selecting from the multitude, and make loving and drawing near to the worthy Your urgent priority; rectify Your sight and hearing to broaden Your perspicacity, and make judgments of right and wrong impartial so as to determine whom to accept…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
舍無偏無黨運
帝德於罔愆惟幾惟康鞏
皇圖於孔固臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以文武職名
御屏奉
表隨
進以
聞
