第叄場
策五道
第一問
王命爵
同考試官教諭姚批我
皇上敬
天勤民紹休揚烈子能敷對詳盡末復致交儆意可覌忠藎
同考試官教諭薄批是策能對揚我
皇上昭事懷保有光
punctuated:
舍。無偏無黨，運帝德於罔愆；惟幾惟康，鞏皇圖於孔固。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至。謹以文武職名御屏奉表隨進以聞。

第叄場
策五道
第一問
王命爵
同考試官教諭姚批：我皇上敬天勤民，紹休揚烈，子能敷對詳盡，末復致交儆意，可覌忠藎。
同考試官教諭薄批：是策能對揚我皇上昭事懷保，有光
translation_en:
…and rejection. Without bias and without faction, may you exercise the imperial virtue free from fault; attentive to the subtle signs of change and mindful of stability, may you consolidate the imperial enterprise in great firmness. Your servants are overcome with the utmost awe, earnestly looking up to Heaven and the Sacred Person in trepidation. We reverently present the Imperial Screen inscribed with the names and titles of civil and military officials, accompanying this memorial for Your Majesty's information.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays
First Question
Wang Mingjue 王命爵
Associate Examiner Instructor Yao comments: "Our August Emperor reveres Heaven and labors diligently for the people, continuing the blessings and exalting the glorious achievements of his predecessors. The candidate has been able to set forth his reply in full detail, and at the end further conveys the meaning of mutual admonition; from this one may observe his loyal devotion."
Associate Examiner Instructor Bo comments: "This policy essay succeeds in extolling how our August Emperor brightly serves Heaven and lovingly protects the people, shedding luster upon…"

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
前聖而亹亹規言溢于詞表取之不徒以其文也
考試官敎諭鄭批寓忠愛於揚厲得靖獻義
考試官學正馮批美不忘規宜錄
帝王所以妙感孚之機而盡統理之責者
其道維何曰敬天勤民而已夫人君一身
上而為天之宗子焉其精意流通與天心
相為孚格故必有時憲之實而後可以奉
若而不違下而為民之父母焉其仁愛旁
浹與民命相為聯屬故必有懷保之誠而
===
後可以宰制而無忝此明明在下赫赫在
上其機為至神而維天惠民維辟奉天其
道所當自盡也即是而觀則我
祖
宗之所以敬天勤民與我
皇上之所以丕承光昭者可得而言矣詩曰時
邁其邦昊天其子之則敬以事之子道宜
耳而其禮莫大於郊祀所謂因名山以升
中于天因吉土以享帝于郊者此也書曰
punctuated:
前聖，而亹亹規言溢于詞表。取之，不徒以其文也。
考試官敎諭鄭批：寓忠愛於揚厲，得靖獻義。
考試官學正馮批：美不忘規，宜錄。

帝王所以妙感孚之機而盡統理之責者，其道維何？曰：敬天勤民而已。夫人君一身，上而為天之宗子焉，其精意流通與天心相為孚格，故必有時憲之實，而後可以奉若而不違；下而為民之父母焉，其仁愛旁浹與民命相為聯屬，故必有懷保之誠，而後可以宰制而無忝。此「明明在下，赫赫在上」，其機為至神；而「維天惠民，維辟奉天」，其道所當自盡也。即是而觀，則我祖宗之所以敬天勤民，與我皇上之所以丕承光昭者，可得而言矣。《詩》曰：「時邁其邦，昊天其子之。」則敬以事之，子道宜耳；而其禮莫大於郊祀，所謂「因名山以升中于天，因吉土以享帝于郊」者，此也。《書》曰：
translation_en:
… the former sages, while earnest words of remonstrance overflow beyond the surface of the text. I select it not merely for its literary style.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Zheng comments: It embeds loyalty and affection within praise and exaltation, capturing the principle of serene dedication to the sovereign.
Examiner and Subprefectural Learned Official Feng comments: In praising, he does not forget to offer remonstrance; it deserves to be recorded.

By what Way do emperors and kings master the subtle mechanism of resonant trust and fulfill the responsibility of governing all? It is simply to revere Heaven and be diligent toward the people. Now, in his own person, the ruler above is the eldest son of Heaven; his finest intentions flow forth to mutually correspond and commune with the mind of Heaven, and therefore there must be the reality of timely emulation before he can reverently accord with it without transgression. Below, he is the father and mother of the people; his benevolent love spreads widely to be mutually bound up with the lives of the people, and therefore there must be the sincerity of cherishing and protecting them before he can govern and direct them without disgrace. In this—“brightly discerning below, awe-inspiring on high”—the mechanism is supremely marvelous; and in “it is Heaven that benefits the people, it is the sovereign who serves Heaven,” this is the Way that he ought to fulfill to the utmost himself. Viewed from this perspective, how our Imperial Ancestors revered Heaven and were diligent toward the people, and how His Majesty grandly inherits and gloriously manifests their example, may now be set forth. The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: “Timely he progresses through his states; may vast Heaven treat him as its son.” Thus, to serve it with reverence is simply what is fitting for the way of a son; and among its rites, none is greater than the suburban sacrifice—what is meant by “making use of famous mountains to send up the report of peace to Heaven, and making use of auspicious ground to sacrifice to the Lord in the suburbs” is this. The Book of Documents (Shujing) says: …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
亶聰明作元后元后作民父母則勤以保
之君道宜耳而其要莫大於官人所謂君
以知人爲明臣以任職爲良者此也稽古
如欽若昊天也勅天之命也克謹天戒也
上帝是祗也小心昭事也莫非所以敬天
也命官敷治也璣衡齊政也封山濬川也
子惠困窮也遹求厥寧也莫非所以勤民
也唐虞三代由此其選矣洪惟我
太祖高皇帝膺天眷命表正萬邦當洪武戊申
===
祀
天鍾山之陽精誠昭格乃命儒臣作
存心錄首之以二郊綴之以羣祀而物采度
數之節致祥召異之徵靡不載焉復
勅禮官議郊曰聖帝明王嚴于祭祀內致誠敬
外致儀文大哉
聖謨其敬天也至矣又
詔有司節財用以崇儉蠲租稅以覃恩耕籍之
典躬舉先其倡於農夫種樹之令時申課
punctuated: 「亶聰明，作元后，元后作民父母。」則勤以保之，君道宜耳，而其要莫大於官人，所謂「君以知人爲明，臣以任職爲良」者此也。稽古如「欽若昊天」也，「勅天之命」也，「克謹天戒」也，「上帝是祗」也，「小心昭事」也，莫非所以敬天也；「命官敷治」也，「璣衡齊政」也，「封山濬川」也，「子惠困窮」也，「遹求厥寧」也，莫非所以勤民也。唐、虞、三代，由此其選矣。洪惟我太祖高皇帝，膺天眷命，表正萬邦。當洪武戊申，祀天鍾山之陽，精誠昭格。乃命儒臣作《存心錄》，首之以二郊，綴之以羣祀，而物采度數之節、致祥召異之徵，靡不載焉。復勅禮官議郊，曰：「聖帝明王，嚴于祭祀，內致誠敬，外致儀文。」大哉聖謨，其敬天也至矣！又詔有司節財用以崇儉，蠲租稅以覃恩；耕籍之典躬舉，先其倡於農夫；種樹之令時申，課
translation_en:
… “Truly endowed with intelligence and perspicacity, he becomes the great sovereign; the great sovereign is the father and mother of the people.” Thus, to protect them with diligence is simply what is fitting according to the Way of the Ruler, and nothing is more essential to this than appointing the right men to office—this is what is meant by the saying, “A ruler shows his wisdom by knowing men; a minister shows his worth by fulfilling his office.” When we examine antiquity, such phrases as “reverently accorded with August Heaven,” “respectfully attend to the ordinances of Heaven,” “able to be cautious of the warnings of Heaven,” “held the Supreme Ancestor on High in awe,” and “with cautious care brightly served [God]” all refer to the means of revering Heaven. Such phrases as “appointing officials to spread governance,” “regulating the seven governors with the jade-transverse and sighting-tube,” “raising mounds on the mountains and deepening the rivers,” “treating the distressed and impoverished like one’s own children,” and “seeking out their tranquility” all refer to the means of being diligent toward the people. Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties were exemplary because they followed this path.

Vast indeed was our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu)! Receiving the favored mandate of Heaven, he stood as a standard to rectify the myriad states. In the wushen year of the Hongwu era (1368), he sacrificed to Heaven on the southern slope of Bell Mountain (Zhongshan), his pure sincerity brightly reaching on high. Thereupon he commanded the Confucian officials to compile the Record of Preserving the Mind-and-Heart (Cunxin lu), beginning with the two suburban sacrifices and appending the various lesser sacrifices, wherein the regulations for ritual paraphernalia, colors, and numbers, as well as the portents that bring about auspiciousness or summon anomalies, were all recorded without omission. He further commanded the ritual officials to deliberate on the suburban sacrifices, saying: “Sage emperors and enlightened kings are strict in their sacrifices: inwardly they extend sincerity and reverence; outwardly they extend ritual form and elegance.” Great indeed are the sacred counsels! His reverence for Heaven reached the utmost!

Furthermore, he proclaimed to the authorities to economize on expenditures so as to exalt frugality, and to remit land taxes so as to spread his grace widely. The ceremony of plowing the imperial sacred field he personally performed, taking the lead to encourage the farmers; the ordinances for planting trees he repeatedly enjoined at the proper seasons, assessing…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
其數於計吏恤刑而有施鐻之喻賑饑而
有待哺之矜一哉
聖心其勤民也至矣
成祖文皇帝乗幾務之暇乃采聖賢嘉言編爲
聖學心法以示子孫甞莊誦
御製序云爲治莫大於敬天而敬天章首采書
之堯典而終以心學之說
序又曰聖王之於百姓也恒保之如赤子而
仁政章首舉易之坤卦而終以真德秀之
===
言他如因地震而慎陰陽之調燮當晡奏
而勉大臣以勤勵免北平之差役蠲鳳陽
之田賦孰非所以
敬天勤民者乎我
世宗肅皇帝舉
圜丘之禮乃因甘露降祥遂作
欽天記頌以賜臣工甞莊誦
御製頌云先之以珍佩繼之以申酬功惟歸
祖而復推及於仁民善則稱
punctuated: 其數於計吏；恤刑而有施鐻之喻，賑饑而有待哺之矜。一哉聖心，其勤民也至矣！成祖文皇帝乗幾務之暇，乃采聖賢嘉言，編爲《聖學心法》，以示子孫。甞莊誦御製序，云：「爲治莫大於敬天。」而〈敬天〉章首采《書》之〈堯典〉，而終以心學之說。序又曰：「聖王之於百姓也，恒保之如赤子。」而〈仁政〉章首舉《易》之〈坤〉卦，而終以真德秀之言。他如因地震而慎陰陽之調燮，當晡奏而勉大臣以勤勵，免北平之差役，蠲鳳陽之田賦，孰非所以敬天勤民者乎？我世宗肅皇帝舉圜丘之禮，乃因甘露降祥，遂作《欽天記頌》以賜臣工。甞莊誦御製頌，云：先之以「珍佩」，繼之以「申酬」，功惟歸祖，而復推及於仁民；善則稱
translation_en:
…their numbers from the accounting officials; in showing compassion in punishments, He used the metaphor of setting up a bell-stand, and in relieving famine, He felt pity for those waiting to be fed. Single-minded indeed was the Imperial Mind! His diligence toward the people was supreme.

Emperor Chengzu Wen (the Yongle Emperor), taking advantage of leisure from the myriad affairs of state, gathered the fine words of sages and worthies and compiled them into the Mental Method of Imperial Learning (Shengxue xinfa) to instruct his descendants. I have reverently recited the Imperial Preface, which says: "In governing, nothing is greater than revering Heaven." And the chapter on "Revering Heaven" begins by selecting the "Canon of Yao" from the Book of Documents and ends with the doctrines of the learning of the mind. The Preface also says: "As for a sage-king's relation to the common people, he always protects them like newborn infants." And the chapter on "Benevolent Governance" begins by citing the Kun hexagram from the Book of Changes and ends with the words of Zhen Dexiu 真德秀. As for other measures—such as being cautious about harmonizing yin and yang on account of earthquakes, encouraging the grand ministers to be diligent and devoted during late-afternoon memorials, remitting labor services in Beiping, and granting exemptions from land taxes in Fengyang—which of these was not a means of revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people?

Our Emperor Shizong Su (the Jiajing Emperor) performed the rites at the Circular Mound Altar, and because auspicious sweet dew descended, He thereupon composed the Record and Ode on Revering Heaven (Qintian jisong) to bestow upon His officials. I have reverently recited the Imperial Ode: it begins with "cherishing and wearing at the girdle" and continues with "renewed requital"; merit is attributed solely to the Ancestors, while further extending to benevolence toward the people; goodness is credited to…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
親而又克慎於保祚他如免稅勸農開其源於
衣食發帑施藥軫其念於顛連屢
頒欽恤之典特申貪虐之科孰非所以
敬天勤民者乎我
皇上躬至聖之資撫綦隆之運
紀元一詔首以敬天爲言矣而猶未已也災
異則露禱于
宮庭敬畏則交修於臣下而敬天之念靡少
間焉復于去冬以
===
郊禮爲重精白一心躬祀
上帝飭壇戒具之必先
省牲省蠲之惟謹而外心之敬已豫矣
宿齋宮而儼對越之誠
馨明德而隆將享之典而內心之敬已昭矣
又於輔臣所進
郊禮圖冊
特賜嘉納隆之以溫諭寵之以留覽是我
皇上之聖敬昭升
punctuated:
親，而又克慎於保祚。他如免稅勸農，開其源於衣食；發帑施藥，軫其念於顛連；屢頒欽恤之典，特申貪虐之科，孰非所以敬天勤民者乎？

我皇上躬至聖之資，撫綦隆之運。紀元一詔，首以敬天爲言矣，而猶未已也。災異則露禱于宮庭，敬畏則交修於臣下，而敬天之念靡少間焉。復于去冬，以郊禮爲重，精白一心，躬祀上帝。飭壇戒具之必先，省牲省蠲之惟謹，而外心之敬已豫矣；宿齋宮而儼對越之誠，馨明德而隆將享之典，而內心之敬已昭矣。又於輔臣所進《郊禮圖冊》，特賜嘉納，隆之以溫諭，寵之以留覽。是我皇上之聖敬昭升，
translation_en:
…parents, while also exercising utmost caution in preserving the dynastic fortune. As for other measures—such as remitting taxes and encouraging agriculture to open the sources of food and clothing; disbursing treasury funds and dispensing medicine out of compassionate concern for those in distress; repeatedly promulgating statutes of imperial compassion for prisoners, and specially reiterating the legal penalties for贪婪 (venality) and cruelty—which of these was not a means of revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people?

Our reigning Sovereign possesses the endowments of supreme sageliness and presides over an era of utmost flourishing. In the inaugural edict of his reign period, he first spoke of revering Heaven, and yet he did not stop there. When natural disasters and anomalies occur, he prays in the open air in the palace courtyard; in reverent awe, he engages in mutual cultivation with his officials, so that the thought of revering Heaven is never interrupted for a moment. Furthermore, last winter, holding the Suburban Sacrifice to be of paramount importance, with a pure and single mind he personally sacrificed to the Lord on High. By必ず (invariably) attending first to the preparation of the altar and the readying of the ritual implements, and by exercising utmost care in inspecting the sacrificial victims and the purity of the vessels, the reverence of his outward mind was already prepared in advance. By lodging in the Palace of Abstinence and displaying the solemn sincerity of standing in the presence of the divine, and by offering the fragrance of his illustrious virtue and exalting the rites of presentation and offering, the reverence of his inward mind was already made manifest. Moreover, regarding the Illustrated Album of the Suburban Sacrifice (Jiaoli tuce) presented by the Grand Secretaries, he specially bestowed his approving acceptance, honoring them with warm words of instruction and favoring the work by retaining it for his personal perusal. Thus, our Sovereign's sagely reverence ascends brightly,…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天心克享蓋質之
祖
宗而一揆乎
嗣服以來輒以勤民為訓矣而猶未已也比
地旱乾則賑貸徧於黔黎徐淮水溢則發
帑賙及昏墊而勤民之念不少置焉邇復
加意元元
頒降
聖諭申飭羣工以牧養責之有司而戒其飾譽
===
以自衒以品隲責之銓曹而欲其崇實以
黜浮是即幽明黜陟意也憫小民之失所
而以催科太濫咎之守令酌逋負之分數
而以調停蠲免委之司農是即蠲租大賚
意也且於部臣肅將
綸綍德意特賜頒行昭示臣工徧布宇內是我
皇上之至仁洋溢民心允懷其視
前烈有光乎是以
恩覃四海則含生之類莫不翹首跂足以霑
punctuated: 天心克享，蓋質之祖宗而一揆乎！嗣服以來，輒以勤民為訓矣，而猶未已也。比地旱乾，則賑貸徧於黔黎；徐、淮水溢，則發帑賙及昏墊，而勤民之念不少置焉。邇復加意元元，頒降聖諭，申飭羣工：以牧養責之有司，而戒其飾譽以自衒；以品隲責之銓曹，而欲其崇實以黜浮，是即幽明黜陟意也；憫小民之失所，而以催科太濫咎之守令；酌逋負之分數，而以調停蠲免委之司農，是即蠲租大賚意也。且於部臣肅將綸綍德意，特賜頒行，昭示臣工，徧布宇內。是我皇上之至仁洋溢，民心允懷，其視前烈有光乎！是以恩覃四海，則含生之類莫不翹首跂足以霑
translation_en:
… and is acceptable to the heart of Heaven—surely, when measured against the Imperial Ancestors, it follows the very same principle!

Ever since ascending the throne, His Majesty has repeatedly made diligence toward the people his guiding precept, and yet he does not stop there. When nearby regions suffered drought, relief and loans reached all the common folk; when the waters overflowed in Xu and Huai, funds were issued from the treasury to succor those drowning in distress, and his concern for being diligent toward the people was never set aside even for a moment. Recently, paying further heed to the common people, he promulgated a sacred edict sternly admonishing all officials: he charged the local authorities with shepherding and nourishing the people, warning them against fabricating a fine reputation to boast of themselves; and he charged the Ministry of Personnel with evaluating and ranking officials, desiring that they prize substance and dismiss superficiality—this is precisely the principle of demoting the benighted and promoting the enlightened. Pitying the common folk for losing their livelihoods, he blamed the prefects and magistrates for excessive harshness in pressing for taxes; weighing the proportions of tax arrears, he entrusted the Ministry of Revenue with mediating and granting remissions—this is precisely the principle of remitting taxes and bestowing grand largesse. Moreover, when the ministry officials reverently carried out the gracious intent of the imperial decree, he specially ordered its promulgation, clearly displaying it to all officials and spreading it throughout the realm. Thus the supreme benevolence of our August Emperor overflows, and the hearts of the people are truly cherished—compared to the achievements of his predecessors, does it not shine even brighter? Therefore, as grace extends throughout the Four Seas, all living beings without exception crane their necks and stand on tiptoe to be moistened by…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
庥澤令飭百司而嚮風之臣莫不洗心滌慮以
奉
明威猗歟休哉執事猶欲愚生效忠悃于萬一
則豈所敢知哉雖然竊與有聞焉夫帝天
之命主于民心而愛民者即所以奉天也
我
皇上之
欽崇天道者豈徒以恪恭于豆籩之文哉蓋有
敬天之實焉是故思
===
天心之視聽在民則顧民情之嵒險可畏
政令之布所以宣于民也以代天言不可以
不慎也
紀綱之運所以式乎民也以代天工不可以
不慎也法
天之仁以育萬民也則其恩為雨露焉而天下
以熙以洽也法
天之義以正萬民也則其威為霜雪焉而天下
以震以懾也秉憲宣力者民之庇也則順
punctuated: 庥澤；令飭百司，而嚮風之臣莫不洗心滌慮以奉明威。猗歟休哉！執事猶欲愚生效忠悃于萬一，則豈所敢知哉？雖然，竊與有聞焉。夫帝天之命主于民心，而愛民者即所以奉天也。我皇上之欽崇天道者，豈徒以恪恭于豆籩之文哉？蓋有敬天之實焉。是故思天心之視聽在民，則顧民情之嵒險可畏。政令之布，所以宣于民也，以代天言，不可以不慎也；紀綱之運，所以式乎民也，以代天工，不可以不慎也。法天之仁以育萬民也，則其恩為雨露焉，而天下以熙以洽也；法天之義以正萬民也，則其威為霜雪焉，而天下以震以懾也。秉憲宣力者，民之庇也，則順
translation_en:
… blessings and grace; when orders admonish the hundred offices, the officials who incline toward the ruler's moral influence all without exception cleanse their hearts and purify their thoughts so as to uphold His illustrious majesty. Oh, how glorious! Yet Your Excellency still wishes this ignorant student to offer some ten-thousandth part of loyal sincerity—how could I dare presume to know enough for that? Even so, I have humbly heard something on the matter.

Now, the mandate of Imperial Heaven is governed by the hearts of the people, and to love the people is the very means of serving Heaven. In revering the Way of Heaven, how could Our Majesty merely show respectful diligence in the outward forms of sacrificial vessels? Rather, there is the substance of revering Heaven. Therefore, reflecting that Heaven's seeing and hearing reside in the people, He looks upon the perilousness of popular sentiment as something to be feared. The promulgation of policies and ordinances is that by which announcements are made to the people; as they speak on behalf of Heaven, one cannot but be cautious with them. The operation of laws and institutions is that by which a model is set for the people; as they carry out the work of Heaven, one cannot but be cautious with them. By emulating Heaven's benevolence in nurturing the myriad people, His grace becomes rain and dew, and the realm is thereby made prosperous and harmonious; by emulating Heaven's righteousness in rectifying the myriad people, His majesty becomes frost and snow, and the realm is thereby awed and subdued. Those who uphold the laws and exert their strength are the shelter of the people; thus, in accordance with…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
天之命而彰善行焉比周回遹者民之蠹也則
勅
天之罰而癉惡行焉豐亨日中之時凜若匹夫
之不獲太和徧覆之中隱若下民之其咨
則仁不遺其民者孝不違于天以此事
天不必祝嘏陳詞而大心自降監矣天之生賢
所以弼君而得人者正所以弘化也我
皇上之勤恤民隱者豈徒以兢業于宵旰之間
哉蓋有勤民之道焉是故念
===
元首股肱之分旣明則調元贊化之責當盡
三公所以論道經邦也將何以贊襄
密勿而萬國咸寧乎六卿所以分職率屬也
將何以克倡九牧阜成兆民乎臺諫之臣
耳目乎四方也以主公議使膏澤日流於
民者非其寄歟監司之臣總核乎吏治也
以持風裁使饕餮之不爲民病者非其責
歟典郡邑者以親民爲務果能悃愊無華
而不獵虛聲乎否也專封疆者以衞民爲
punctuated:
天之命，而彰善行焉；比周回遹者，民之蠹也，則勅天之罰，而癉惡行焉。豐亨日中之時，凜若匹夫之不獲；太和徧覆之中，隱若下民之其咨。則仁不遺其民者，孝不違于天。以此事天，不必祝嘏陳詞，而天心自降監矣。

天之生賢，所以弼君，而得人者，正所以弘化也。我皇上之勤恤民隱者，豈徒以兢業于宵旰之間哉？蓋有勤民之道焉。是故念元首股肱之分旣明，則調元贊化之責當盡。三公所以論道經邦也，將何以贊襄密勿，而萬國咸寧乎？六卿所以分職率屬也，將何以克倡九牧，阜成兆民乎？臺諫之臣，耳目乎四方也，以主公議，使膏澤日流於民者，非其寄歟？監司之臣，總核乎吏治也，以持風裁，使饕餮之不爲民病者，非其責歟？典郡邑者，以親民爲務，果能悃愊無華，而不獵虛聲乎否也？專封疆者，以衞民爲…
translation_en:
… the mandate of Heaven, andthus the commending of the good is carried out; those who form cliques and act perversely are pests to the people, so one enforces the punishments of Heaven, and thus the chastising of the wicked is carried out. At a time of abundance and prosperity like the sun at its zenith, one trembles as though a single common man were left unprovided for; amidst universal harmony sheltering all, one grieves as though the lowly people were sighing in distress. Thus, one whose benevolence does not neglect his people is one whose filial piety does not contravene Heaven. Serving Heaven in this manner, one need not offer prayers for blessings or present ritual words, and the mind of Heaven[?] (大心/天心) will naturally look down in inspection.

Heaven gives birth to the worthy in order to assist the ruler, and obtaining the right men is precisely the means to broaden transforming influence. In diligently showing compassion for the hidden sufferings of the people, how could Our Majesty merely be cautious and fearful from before dawn until late at night? Indeed, there is a proper way to be diligent on behalf of the people. Therefore, when one bears in mind that the distinction between the sovereign as the head and the ministers as the limbs is already clear, the responsibility of harmonizing the primordial forces and assisting in transformation must be fulfilled. The Three Dukes are meant to discourse on the Way and govern the state; how shall they assist in confidential deliberations so that all the myriad states enjoy peace? The Six Ministers are meant to divide responsibilities and lead their subordinates; how shall they succeed in leading the Pastors of the Nine Provinces and bringing abundance and maturity to the millions of people? Officials of the Censorate and the Remonstrance Bureaus serve as eyes and ears throughout the four quarters; to uphold public opinion so that the enriching dew of grace flows daily to the people—is this not their trust? Surveillance officials exercise general verification over administrative governance; to maintain strict integrity so that rapacious gluttons do not become a scourge to the people—is this not their responsibility? Those in charge of prefectures and counties take being close to the people as their duty; are they truly able to be sincere and unadorned, without hunting after empty reputation, or not? Those entrusted with the frontiers take defending the people as their…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
功果能干城無忝而足以禦侮者否也服
休服采雅有師師之風百司庶府共效蹇
蹇之義則
大君恭己而成功人臣靖共以恪職以此勤民
雖不必家賜人益而民心自永懷矣然此
非愚生之臆說也
聖祖諭侍臣曰所謂敬天者不獨嚴而有禮當
有其實天以子民之任付於君爲君者欲
求事天必先恤民恤民者事天之實也即
===
如國家命任守令之事若不能福民則是
棄君之命不敬孰大焉是於敬天之中而
寓恤民恤民之內而寓責臣也天人相爲
一道
君臣各任其責此交泰之時治之極也芹曝之
見敢爲執事誦之不識可轉聞于
上否
第二問
江楫
punctuated:
功，果能干城無忝而足以禦侮者否也？服休服采，雅有師師之風；百司庶府，共效蹇蹇之義。則大君恭己而成功，人臣靖共以恪職，以此勤民，雖不必家賜人益，而民心自永懷矣。然此非愚生之臆說也。聖祖諭侍臣曰：「所謂敬天者，不獨嚴而有禮，當有其實。天以子民之任付於君，爲君者欲求事天，必先恤民，恤民者事天之實也。即如國家命任守令之事，若不能福民，則是棄君之命，不敬孰大焉？」是於敬天之中而寓恤民，恤民之內而寓責臣也。天人相爲一道，君臣各任其責，此交泰之時、治之極也。芹曝之見，敢爲執事誦之，不識可轉聞于上否？

第二問
江楫
translation_en:
…their achievement—can they truly serve as bulwarks without shame and suffice to repel foreign aggression, or not? When those serving in close attendance and those handling general affairs possess the refined air of emulating one another, and all the hundred offices and various bureaus jointly devote themselves to the duty of forthright loyalty, then the Great Sovereign will achieve success through reverent self-possession, and his ministers will diligently fulfill their duties in quiet devotion. Laboring for the people in this manner, even without bestowing gifts on every household or enriching every individual, the hearts of the people will naturally cherish the dynasty forever. Yet this is not merely the conjecture of this humble student. The Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu] instructed his attending officials, saying: "What is called revering Heaven does not consist solely in solemnity and ritual; there must be the substance of it. Heaven entrusts the responsibility of caring for the people as children to the ruler. One who acts as ruler and seeks to serve Heaven must first show compassion for the people; showing compassion for the people is the true substance of serving Heaven. For instance, when the state appoints prefects and magistrates to their duties, if they fail to bring welfare to the people, they are abandoning the ruler's mandate—what greater irreverence could there be?" Thus, within the reverence for Heaven is lodged compassion for the people, and within compassion for the people is lodged the holding of ministers to account. Heaven and humanity share a single Way, and ruler and minister each bear their own responsibilities: this is an era of harmonious flourishing and the pinnacle of governance. Humbly offering these modest views, I venture to recite them before Your Excellency, not knowing whether they might be relayed to His Majesty on high or not.

Second Question
Jiang Ji

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭馮批周禮一書本是太平成跡
唯我
朝倣之以收治效子能揚述披納其有志者
同考試官敎諭姚批會典昉乎職掌
國家經世之大經大法也其潤色於
今日千載一時子能知其原委其通達當世之務者乎
考試官敎諭鄭批條悉明備宜錄
考試官學正馮批揚厲殆盡
聖王所以肇丕基而貽謀燕翼也必有以
===
垂宏遠不易之規聖王所以守成業而潤
色鴻猷也必有以盡精微不遺之制創守
兼資述作互麗所以開萬世之太平者此
也所以衍萬世之治統者此也開太平則
政敎休明溥利澤於無疆其諸如天之仁
乎衍治統則繼述盡善廣令聞於不墜其
諸繩祖之孝乎觀此則我
太祖高皇帝
諸司職掌之作
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭馮批：「《周禮》一書，本是太平成跡，唯我朝倣之以收治效。子能揚述披納，其有志者。」
同考試官敎諭姚批：「《會典》昉乎《職掌》，國家經世之大經大法也。其潤色於今日，千載一時。子能知其原委，其通達當世之務者乎！」
考試官敎諭鄭批：「條悉明備，宜錄。」
考試官學正馮批：「揚厲殆盡。」
聖王所以肇丕基而貽謀燕翼也，必有以垂宏遠不易之規；聖王所以守成業而潤色鴻猷也，必有以盡精微不遺之制。創守兼資，述作互麗，所以開萬世之太平者此也，所以衍萬世之治統者此也。開太平，則政敎休明，溥利澤於無疆，其諸如天之仁乎！衍治統，則繼述盡善，廣令聞於不墜，其諸繩祖之孝乎！觀此，則我太祖高皇帝《諸司職掌》之作，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Feng's comment: "The book of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) is originally a vestige of achieved great peace, and only our dynasty has modeled itself upon it to reap the results of good governance. You are able to extol, recount, and present it—truly a man of aspiration."
Associate Examiner Instructor Yao's comment: "The Collected Statutes (Huidian) originated from the Duties of All Offices (Zhizhang); they are the great standards and fundamental laws by which the state orders the world. Their embellishment in the present day is a once-in-a-millennium occasion. Since you are able to understand their origins and development, are you not one who thoroughly comprehends the affairs of the present age?"
Examiner Instructor Zheng's comment: "Itemized thoroughly, clear and complete; it should be selected for inclusion."
Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Feng's comment: "Praised and expounded almost to the fullest."
Whereby the sage kings founded a great enterprise and handed down plans to comfort and shelter their descendants, they necessarily had the means to pass down vast, far-reaching, and unchangeable regulations; whereby the sage kings preserved the accomplished enterprise and embellished the grand plan, they necessarily had the means to exhaust subtle, refined, and all-encompassing institutions. Founding and preserving mutually support one another, and transmitting and creating mutually adorn one another; it is by this that great peace is opened for ten thousand generations, and it is by this that the succession of governance is extended for ten thousand generations. In opening great peace, governance and instruction are auspicious and bright, spreading benefits and blessings without limit—is this not benevolence like that of Heaven? In extending the succession of governance, succeeding and transmitting are perfected, broadening a fine reputation without fail—is this not filial piety that continues the ways of the ancestors? Viewing it from this perspective, then our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao's (Taizu) creation of the Duties of All Offices (Zhusi zhizhang), …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
孝宗敬皇帝
大明會典之修與夫
世宗之敬承
皇上之纘述可得而揚厲其萬一矣嘗聞自古
王者之興或開物而成務或更化而善治
莫非所以奠民生也布之爲制度述之爲
訓辭莫非所以垂後裔也典謨遠不可追
矣考諸方冊其體裁之大經畫之精莫過
於周禮一書設官分職立綱陳紀首重三
===
公繼列六官次而卿大夫士下而府史胥
徒亦皆備載而無遺焉昔人謂爲致太平
之跡非聖人不能作是也維時周公以元
聖之親輔成王冲睿之主君臣道合明聖
相須則所以堯舜其君而文武其政者信
爲一時之間值矣下此漢唐宋掌故之職
非不設會要之書非不編然紀綱未正治
化未光後人相承拘泥紛更適足以弊其
治無異乎不能比隆於成周也洪惟我
punctuated: 孝宗敬皇帝《大明會典》之修，與夫世宗之敬承、皇上之纘述，可得而揚厲其萬一矣。嘗聞自古王者之興，或開物而成務，或更化而善治，莫非所以奠民生也；布之爲制度，述之爲訓辭，莫非所以垂後裔也。典謨遠不可追矣，考諸方冊，其體裁之大、經畫之精，莫過於《周禮》一書。設官分職，立綱陳紀，首重三公，繼列六官，次而卿大夫士，下而府史胥徒，亦皆備載而無遺焉。昔人謂爲「致太平之跡，非聖人不能作」，是也。維時周公以元聖之親，輔成王冲睿之主，君臣道合，明聖相須，則所以堯舜其君而文武其政者，信爲一時之間值矣。下此漢、唐、宋，掌故之職非不設，會要之書非不編，然紀綱未正，治化未光，後人相承，拘泥紛更，適足以弊其治，無異乎不能比隆於成周也。洪惟我
translation_en:
… the compilation of the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Daming huidian) by Emperor Xiaozong the Reverent, together with the reverent continuation by Emperor Shizong and the succession and transmission by His Majesty the reigning Emperor—we may thereby extol even a ten-thousandth part of their glory.

I have heard that since antiquity, when true kings arose, whether by pioneering undertakings and accomplishing great affairs, or by renewing transformation and perfecting governance, none did so for any purpose other than to settle the livelihood of the people; and whether they promulgated these as institutional systems or set them down as instructive injunctions, none did so for any purpose other than to bequeath them to posterity. The Canons and Counsels are distant and can no longer be recovered in detail; yet if we examine the written records, in grandeur of structure and precision of planning, nothing surpasses the single book of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli). In establishing offices and apportioning duties, in setting up the overarching principles and arraying the regulations, it first gives primacy to the Three Dukes, next arrays the Six Ministries, then follows with the ministers, grand masters, and servicemen, and down to the repository keepers, scribes, clerks, and runners—all are comprehensively recorded without omission. People of the past called it "the traces of achieving great peace, which none but a sage could have composed," and rightly so. At that time, the Duke of Zhou, as a close kinsman and supreme sage, assisted King Cheng, a young yet wise ruler. Ruler and minister were united in the Way, wisdom and sagehood complemented one another, so that making his ruler like Yao and Shun and his governance like that of Kings Wen and Wu was truly a rare conjunction of an age.

Coming down to the Han, Tang, and Song dynasties, it was not that offices for institutional precedents were left unestablished, nor that compendia of essential statutes (huiyao) were left uncompiled; yet their overarching principles were not rectified and their transformative governance was not illustrious. When later generations inherited them, they either clung rigidly to the letter or made disorderly alterations, which served only to ruin their governance. Little wonder, then, that they could not match the flourishing splendour of the accomplished Zhou! Humbly reflecting upon our…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝汎掃胡元肇造區夏謂繼亂世者
其道變議禮制度舍成周奚法焉於是倣
乎周禮
創製諸司職掌一書提其綱領則文武竝建六
部之外增院司布列條貫則職守分屬戶
役之末續圖志其中兵柄之分言責之寄
司徒司空之分合雖曰間與周禮不同然
相乎時宜以殫經綸何嘗失周官之美意
耶是書也頒於洪武癸酉至
===
英宗已幾五紀屢議條例之續其亦克遵
彝訓者與至我
孝宗敬皇帝撫運盈成丕承
令緒謂繼治世者其道同宣徽揚烈舍
祖宗奚法焉於是倣乎職掌編摩
大明會典一書以官職制度爲綱全錄職掌附
以頒降之書兩京同制而詹事等衙門則
增入焉以事物名數爲目雜考條例而存
沿革之舊圖式竝紀而制辭等類則詳定
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝汎掃胡元，肇造區夏，謂繼亂世者其道變，議禮制度，舍成周奚法焉？於是倣乎《周禮》，創製《諸司職掌》一書。提其綱領，則文武竝建，六部之外增院、司；布列條貫，則職守分屬，戶役之末續圖志。其中兵柄之分、言責之寄、司徒司空之分合，雖曰間與《周禮》不同，然相乎時宜以殫經綸，何嘗失《周官》之美意耶？是書也，頒於洪武癸酉，至英宗已幾五紀，屢議條例之續，其亦克遵彝訓者與！至我孝宗敬皇帝撫運盈成，丕承令緒，謂繼治世者其道同，宣徽揚烈，舍祖宗奚法焉？於是倣乎《職掌》，編摩《大明會典》一書。以官職制度爲綱，全錄《職掌》，附以頒降之書，兩京同制，而詹事等衙門則增入焉；以事物名數爲目，雜考條例，而存沿革之舊，圖式竝紀，而制辭等類則詳定
translation_en:
… Emperor Gao, our Grand Progenitor (Taizu), swept away the barbarian Yuan and founded our Chinese realm. He held that for one who succeeds an age of disorder, the Way requires change; in deliberating on rites and establishing institutions, what else was there to take as a model if not the flourishing Zhou? Thereupon, in imitation of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), he created and compiled the book Functions of All Offices (Zhusi zhizhang). In setting forth its main principles, civil and military hierarchies were established side by side, and beyond the Six Ministries were added the Censorate and the Offices; in arranging its detailed articles, official duties were divided and assigned to their respective jurisdictions, and maps and registers were appended at the end of the section on households and corvée labor. Within it, the division of military authority, the entrusting of speaking responsibilities, and the separation and merging of the functions of the Minister of Education (situ) and the Minister of Works (sikong)—although these differed at times from the Rites of Zhou, yet in adapting to what was appropriate for the times so as to exhaustively order the state, how did they ever lose the admirable intent of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan)? This book was promulgated in the guiyou year of the Hongwu reign (1393). By the time of Temple Emperor Yingzong, nearly five twelve-year cycles (sixty years) had passed, and there were repeated deliberations on supplementing its regulations and precedents—was he not also one who was able to follow the constant instructions?

Coming down to our Emperor Jing, Temple Emperor Xiaozong, he presided over a fortune of fullness and completion and grandly succeeded to the fine line of succession. He held that for one who succeeds an age of order, the Way remains the same; in proclaiming virtue and extolling meritorious achievements, what else was there to take as a model if not the Ancestors? Thereupon, in imitation of the Functions of All Offices, he had the book Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian) compiled and polished. Taking official posts and institutions as the main headings, it recorded the Functions of All Offices in full and appended books promulgated by imperial decree; the two capitals shared the same system, while offices such as the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent (Zhanshi fu) were added into it. Taking affairs, objects, titles, and figures as the subheadings, it widely examined regulations and precedents while preserving the old records of institutional evolution; diagrams and formats were recorded together, while categories such as imperial edicts and decrees were determined in detail…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
焉其中勳戚領宗人三公不建府鴻臚欽
天之易名雖日間與職掌不同然黼黻治
平遡循意緒何嘗違
祖宗之良法耶是書也成於弘治壬戌至
武宗已更五歲始為刊布於世其亦善成
先德者與由是而觀讀職掌則惇大之治體備
會典之原也讀會典則精明之治具張職
掌之委也
聖子神孫所當世守而恪遵者也嗣我
===
世宗肅皇帝入繼大統加意會典
申命儒臣訂補脫略取令格以續之
命下於嘉靖八年至二十九年而進呈焉其增
定之大者如
郊祇之祀
壇廟之儀閣臣不載於國子監後殿試不次
於有司科舉其餘可類推矣然修會典而
不及職掌者蓋會典一職掌也尊
孝宗之制即所以尊
punctuated: 焉。其中勳戚領宗人，三公不建府，鴻臚、欽天之易名，雖曰間與《職掌》不同，然黼黻治平，遡循意緒，何嘗違祖宗之良法耶？是書也，成於弘治壬戌，至武宗已更五歲，始為刊布於世，其亦善成先德者與！由是而觀，讀《職掌》，則惇大之治體備，《會典》之原也；讀《會典》，則精明之治具張，《職掌》之委也。聖子神孫所當世守而恪遵者也。嗣我世宗肅皇帝入繼大統，加意《會典》，申命儒臣，訂補脫略，取令格以續之。命下於嘉靖八年，至二十九年而進呈焉。其增定之大者，如郊祇之祀、壇廟之儀，閣臣不載於國子監後，殿試不次於有司科舉，其餘可類推矣。然修《會典》而不及《職掌》者，蓋《會典》一《職掌》也，尊孝宗之制，即所以尊
translation_en: … therein. Among these, that meritorious nobles and imperial relatives by marriage head the Court of the Imperial Clan, that the Three Dukes do not establish independent offices, and the renaming of the Court of State Ceremonial and the Directorate of Astronomy—although it is said that at times these differ from the Handbook of Government Posts (Zhizhang), yet in adorning an era of peace and good order and tracing back the thread of their underlying intent, how do they ever depart from the fine laws of the Ancestors? This book was completed in the renxu year of the Hongzhi reign (1502), and by the reign of Emperor Wuzong, after five years had passed, it was first printed and promulgated to the world; was this not also a fine fulfillment of the virtue of his predecessor! Viewed in this light, when one reads the Handbook of Government Posts, the generous and grand substance of governance is complete—it is the source of the Collected Statutes (Huidian); when one reads the Collected Statutes, the precise and clear instruments of governance are spread forth—it is the outflow of the Handbook of Government Posts. They are what sacred sons and divine grandsons ought to guard for generations and reverently observe. Thereafter, our Emperor Shizong Su entered to succeed to the Great统 (Imperial Line) and paid special attention to the Collected Statutes, repeatedly commanding Confucian officials to correct and supplement omissions and to take the ordinances and regulations to continue it. The command was issued in the eighth year of the Jiajing reign (1529), and by the twenty-ninth year (1550) it was presented to the throne. Among the major additions and revisions were such matters as the sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the rituals of the altars and ancestral temples, that Grand Secretaries were no longer recorded after the Directorate of Education, and that the Palace Examination was no longer placed after the civil service examinations conducted by the regular authorities; the rest can be inferred by analogy. Yet the reason for revising the Collected Statutes without touching upon the Handbook of Government Posts is that the Collected Statutes is one and the same as the Handbook of Government Posts; to revere the institutions of Emperor Xiaozong is the very means to revere…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
高祖之制也寧有二心哉肆我
皇上明睿篤生
受命以來庶績其凝羣工恪職
治化之隆真可以軼美成周而匹休
列聖矣乃
朝講之暇注意會典宣賚
綸音重加修輯開編纂之局專總裁之
命上而
世宗晚年之令甲近而
===
皇考御統之典章無不兼收而備錄之以是貽
謀則大經大法昭垂于後
列聖稱作者之聖焉以是揚休則盡倫盡制光
顯乎前
皇上稱述者之明焉而
開創之仁
繼述之孝不於此兩見之哉執事篇終又以
會典之修何者為因革損益之要焉問然
愚也陋非識時務而達
punctuated:
高祖之制也，寧有二心哉！肆我皇上明睿篤生，受命以來，庶績其凝，羣工恪職，治化之隆，真可以軼美成周而匹休列聖矣。乃朝講之暇，注意《會典》，宣賚綸音，重加修輯，開編纂之局，專總裁之命。上而世宗晚年之令甲，近而皇考御統之典章，無不兼收而備錄之。以是貽謀，則大經大法昭垂于後，列聖稱作者之聖焉；以是揚休，則盡倫盡制光顯乎前，皇上稱述者之明焉。而開創之仁、繼述之孝，不於此兩見之哉！

執事篇終，又以《會典》之修，何者為因革損益之要焉問。然愚也陋，非識時務而達
translation_en:
… the institutions of Gaozu! How could there be any divided intent? Now Our Emperor, born with clarity and sagacity, since receiving the Mandate has brought all achievements to completion while the body of officials dutifully fulfills its charges; the flourishing of his governance and transformation can truly surpass the excellence of the accomplished Zhou and match the glory of the Successive Sages. Yet in the leisure from court audiences and lectures, he has turned his attention to the Collected Statutes (Huidian), proclaiming and bestowing his silken words to have it compiled and edited anew, opening a bureau for its compilation and issuing special commands to Directors-General. Going back to the statutory ordinances from the final years of Shizong, and coming down to the institutional canons from the reign of the Imperial Father, there are none that are not comprehensively gathered and fully recorded. By handing down counsels in this way, the great norms and great laws are brightly transmitted to posterity, and the Successive Sages may be acclaimed as sages who create; by extolling their glory in this way, the fulfillment of human relations and the perfection of institutions shine forth before what came earlier, and His Majesty may be acclaimed as an enlightened ruler who transmits. And are not the benevolence of founding and the filiality of continuing and transmitting both manifested herein?

At the end of your question, Sir, you further ask what constitutes the essential points of continuity, change, reduction, and augmentation in the compilation of the Collected Statutes. Yet I am untutored, not one who understands current affairs or comprehends …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
國體者也竊有一得之愚願為
今日獻焉我
朝設官分職本有定員也邇來建議靡一廢
置無常添設一官此以便議請而彼以不
便議罷朝更夕改閭閻之下能不苦其繹
騷乎明職掌而杜紛更之請今日所當講
也歲運太倉本有額數也
京師之冗役殆數萬計裁之未幾而役者如
故甚至日增焉所以坐食而糜費之者何
===
異鼷鼠之盈倉乎汰老弱而終改折之令
意者不容已也
宗藩
帝室之裔所宜優厚者也今則稱繁盛矣窮蹙
者比屋矣常祿既有不給小民難於加賦
不有以處之何以廣
恩於不匱乎限爵限祿之法任官建學之議所
當破格而舉行之者也我
朝任將或出自世胄或起於武科或發身行
punctuated: 國體者也。竊有一得之愚，願為今日獻焉。我朝設官分職，本有定員也。邇來建議靡一，廢置無常，添設一官，此以便議請，而彼以不便議罷，朝更夕改，閭閻之下能不苦其繹騷乎？明職掌而杜紛更之請，今日所當講也。歲運太倉，本有額數也。京師之冗役殆數萬計，裁之未幾而役者如故，甚至日增焉。所以坐食而糜費之者，何異鼷鼠之盈倉乎？汰老弱而終改折之令，意者不容已也。宗藩，帝室之裔，所宜優厚者也。今則稱繁盛矣，窮蹙者比屋矣。常祿既有不給，小民難於加賦，不有以處之，何以廣恩於不匱乎？限爵限祿之法，任官建學之議，所當破格而舉行之者也。我朝任將，或出自世胄，或起於武科，或發身行…
translation_en:
…the principles of governance. Yet in my humble folly I have hit upon one small insight, which I wish to offer up for the present day.

When our Dynasty established offices and divided responsibilities, there was originally a fixed quota of personnel. Recently, however, proposals have been inconsistent, and posts are abolished or created without regularity. When an additional official is appointed, one party requests it on the grounds of convenience, while another proposes its abolition on the grounds of inconvenience. With policies changed from morning to evening, how can the common people in the villages not suffer from the constant disruption? Clarifying official duties and putting an end to requests for disorderly changes is something that ought to be discussed today.

The annual grain transport to the Great Granary Complex originally had a fixed quota. Yet superfluous laborers in the Capital number nearly in the tens of thousands; no sooner are they reduced than those in service return as before, and even increase by the day. How are those who sit idle and wastefully consume grain any different from mice filling up a granary? Culling the old and weak and seeing through the orders for commuting grain tribute to silver is, I suspect, something that cannot be avoided.

The imperial clansmen and princely establishments are the descendants of the Imperial House, whom it is proper to treat with generous favor. Now, however, they have grown exceedingly numerous, and those in dire straits live door to door. Since their regular stipends are already insufficient, and it is difficult to levy additional taxes on the common people, if we do not find a way to manage this, how can we extend imperial grace without exhausting resources? Laws to limit noble ranks and stipends, as well as proposals to appoint them to office and establish schools for them, are measures that ought to be carried out by breaking with convention.

In our Dynasty's appointment of generals, some come from hereditary military families, some rise through the military examinations, and some start their careers from the ranks…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
伍求之未嘗不廣也但邇來各邊有以眞
夷薦起作參遊者矣狼子野心能保其無
他腸乎宜急裁之或曰以夷攻夷豈其然
與問刑條例所以補律之不及者也但刋
行者有數而續增者無已反以啓不諳法
律妄行引擬者之端也削其牽合而定爲
畫一之軌此亦
欽恤之一誼也造作坐派顔料後因改徵料銀
例甚嚴也今造作不興矣而加派如常甚
===
或數溢正額屹然爲民間兩稅矣查節年
之蓄積抵後來之徵輸此非蠲省之一端
耶凡此數事皆有關於
國體有利於民生今日所當講求而釐正之
者或者在此矣但草茅迂腐之見掛其一
而漏其萬啓其端未能竟其說耳方今
聖人在上聰明睿智所以
延納而虛受者卽訪落之規賢哲在下協恭
和衷所以賛襄而弼承者卽夾輔之助然
punctuated: 伍，求之未嘗不廣也。但邇來各邊有以眞夷薦起作參遊者矣。狼子野心，能保其無他腸乎？宜急裁之。或曰：「以夷攻夷」，豈其然與？《問刑條例》，所以補律之不及者也。但刋行者有數，而續增者無已，反以啓不諳法律、妄行引擬者之端也。削其牽合，而定爲畫一之軌，此亦欽恤之一誼也。造作坐派顔料，後因改徵料銀，例甚嚴也。今造作不興矣，而加派如常，甚或數溢正額，屹然爲民間兩稅矣。查節年之蓄積，抵後來之徵輸，此非蠲省之一端耶？凡此數事，皆有關於國體，有利於民生，今日所當講求而釐正之者，或者在此矣。但草茅迂腐之見，掛其一而漏其萬，啓其端未能竟其說耳。方今聖人在上，聰明睿智，所以延納而虛受者，卽訪落之規；賢哲在下，協恭和衷，所以賛襄而弼承者，卽夾輔之助。然
translation_en:
…the ranks; the search for them has never been less than broad. Yet recently along the various frontiers, there have been cases where genuine barbarians have been recommended and raised to serve as Assistant Regional Commanders and Mobile Corps Commanders. With the wild ambitions of wolf cubs, how can one guarantee that they harbor no ulterior motives? This practice should be urgently curtailed. Some say this is "using barbarians to attack barbarians," but how could that really be so?

The Regulations for Trying Penal Cases (Wenxing tiaoli) were meant to supplement what the statutory Code does not cover. Yet while the published regulations are finite in number, the subsequent additions are endless; on the contrary, this opens the door for those unfamiliar with the law to recklessly cite precedents in proposing sentences. Pruning away forced analogies and establishing a uniform standard would also be one expression of imperial compassion in punishment.

As for the pigments and materials requisitioned by quota for imperial construction, these were later commuted into a levy of material-silver under very strict regulations. Today, construction projects are no longer being undertaken, yet the surcharges continue as usual—and in extreme cases the amounts exceed the regular quota, standing firmly as a second regular tax upon the common people. Investigating the accumulated surpluses from past years in order to offset future tax levies—would this not be one way to grant remissions and economize?

All of these several matters have a bearing on the dignity of the state and are beneficial to the livelihood of the people; what ought to be investigated and rectified today perhaps lies right here. Still, the pedantic views of a rustic scholar catch only one part while omitting ten thousand, merely broaching the topics without being able to exhaust their explanation.

Right now, a Sage sits on high,perspicacious and wise; the way he welcomes counsel and receives it with an open mind follows the very model of the royal consultation on taking up the succession [in the ode "Fangluo"]. Worthy and wise ministers serve below in harmonious reverence; the way they assist and support the throne provides the very aid of flanking guardians. Thus…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
則今日會典之修眞千載一時也必能刪
繁補略神化宜民使是書一出而天下之
人皆仰
大聖人之制作超出尋常與周禮並傳於萬世
豈不偉與愚生歷考往昔深感明良相遇
之難而幸見於
今也敢因明問敬爲執事者告幸轉而聞之於
上
第三問
===
傅一元
同考試官敎諭段批邇來守令未崇實政正以
察吏者失其理也子能特詳其故良是
同考試官敎諭李批監司守令之綱責實務要
交修以救時弊誠如子言
考試官敎諭鄭批說尙實政處剴切
考試官學正馮批據言儼然良吏
親民者有爲民之實功而後無負乎民察
吏者責爲民之實效而後無負乎吏夫設
punctuated:
則今日《會典》之修，眞千載一時也。必能刪繁補略，神化宜民，使是書一出，而天下之人皆仰大聖人之制作超出尋常，與《周禮》並傳於萬世，豈不偉與！愚生歷考往昔，深感明良相遇之難，而幸見於今也，敢因明問，敬爲執事者告，幸轉而聞之於上。

第三問

傅一元

同考試官敎諭段批：邇來守令未崇實政，正以察吏者失其理也。子能特詳其故，良是。
同考試官敎諭李批：監司，守令之綱；責實務要，交修以救時弊，誠如子言。
考試官敎諭鄭批：說尙實政處，剴切。
考試官學正馮批：據言儼然良吏。

親民者有爲民之實功，而後無負乎民；察吏者責爲民之實效，而後無負乎吏。夫設
translation_en:
…then today's compilation of the Collected Statutes (Huidian) is truly an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. It will surely be able to prune away prolixity and supply what was omitted, wondrously transforming customs and suiting the needs of the people, so that once this book is issued, all people in the realm will look up to the institutions created by the Great Sage as surpassing the ordinary, to be handed down alongside the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) for ten thousand generations—how magnificent indeed! Having examined the past at length, I, a foolish student, am deeply moved by how difficult it is for an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers to meet, and feel fortunate to witness it in the present day. Prompted by your enlightened question, I venture to respectfully state this for you, the directors of the examination, in the hope that you will in turn transmit it to the attention of the Emperor above.

Third Question

Fu Yiyuan 傅一元

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Duan 段: "Lately, prefects and magistrates have failed to esteem substantive governance, precisely because those who evaluate officials have lost the proper principle of doing so. That you are able to set forth the reasons in particular detail is truly right."
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李: "Surveillance commissioners are the guiding cord for prefects and magistrates; demanding substantive results and attending to essentials, cultivating their duties together to remedy the abuses of the age—it is truly as you say."
Comment by Examiner Instructor Zheng 鄭: "Where it speaks of esteeming substantive governance, it is incisive and to the point."
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng 馮: "Judging from his words, he already bears himself like a good official."

Only when those who are close to the people achieve real accomplishments on the people's behalf do they not fail the people; only when those who evaluate officials demand real results on the people's behalf do they not fail the officials. Now in establishing…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
官分職凡以爲民也而況親民莫若令其
次莫若守守與令有親民之責不思實意
爲民而一切從事于靡文以要譽則民何
賴焉廼有監臨之責者復以名求之以文
法拘之而亦不考其所以爲民者何如則
吏又何賴焉以此爲治何惑乎民生之日
瘁治效之罔臻而無以復隆古之盛哉是
故采實不采名者作新之要術也務實不
務名者醇德之休風也上以此察吏故試
===
一功課一最必其利於民者焉匪是雖善
不錄矣吏以此治民故建一事剔一弊必
其利於民者焉匪是雖可以近名不爲矣
唐虞三代之治不越此何論漢世哉愚嘗
俯仰今昔見吏治之所關重矣昔人有言
六合元元之衆懸命于縣令宅生於刺史
愚讀其言而悵然悲心焉無論六合即此
一郡一邑之民林林總總何可計算可漫
然不加之意哉漢之君曰使民安其田里
punctuated: 官分職，凡以爲民也。而況親民莫若令，其次莫若守。守與令有親民之責，不思實意爲民，而一切從事于靡文以要譽，則民何賴焉？廼有監臨之責者，復以名求之，以文法拘之，而亦不考其所以爲民者何如，則吏又何賴焉？以此爲治，何惑乎民生之日瘁，治效之罔臻，而無以復隆古之盛哉！是故采實不采名者，作新之要術也；務實不務名者，醇德之休風也。上以此察吏，故試一功、課一最，必其利於民者焉，匪是雖善不錄矣；吏以此治民，故建一事、剔一弊，必其利於民者焉，匪是雖可以近名不爲矣。唐虞三代之治不越此，何論漢世哉！愚嘗俯仰今昔，見吏治之所關重矣。昔人有言：「六合元元之衆，懸命于縣令，宅生於刺史。」愚讀其言而悵然悲心焉。無論六合，即此一郡一邑之民，林林總總，何可計算，可漫然不加之意哉！漢之君曰：「使民安其田里，
translation_en: …establishing offices and dividing duties is all done for the sake of the people. How much more so when none is closer to the people than the District Magistrate, and next to him none is closer than the Prefect! If Prefects and District Magistrates bear the responsibility of being close to the people, yet do not think of serving the people with genuine intent, instead devoting themselves entirely to ornate formalities in order to court reputation, then what have the people to rely upon? And when those who bear the responsibility of supervision in turn demand reputation of them, fetter them with legalistic rules, and likewise fail to examine how they actually serve the people, then what have the officials in turn to rely upon? Governing in this manner, what wonder is it that the people's livelihood grows daily more distressed, that effective governance is never achieved, and that there is no way to restore the flourishing state of high antiquity? Therefore, selecting substance rather than selecting reputation is the essential art of renewal; pursuing substance rather than pursuing reputation is the admirable custom of pure virtue. When superiors inspect officials by this standard, in testing a single merit or evaluating a single top rating, it must be something that benefits the people; if it is not so, even though it seems good, it is not recorded. When officials govern the people by this standard, in establishing a single measure or eradicating a single abuse, it must be something that benefits the people; if it is not so, even though it might bring immediate reputation, they do not do it. The governance of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties did not go beyond this—what need is there to speak of the Han era! I have reflected upon the present and the past and seen how weighty are the consequences of official governance. Someone in the past said: "The common masses within the six directions have their lives suspended from the District Magistrate and their livelihoods lodged with the Regional Inspector." Reading these words, I felt a wistful sorrow in my heart. Setting aside the whole realm within the six directions, even the people of a single prefecture or a single district are so multitudinous that they cannot be counted—how could one be heedless and pay them no mind? A ruler of the Han said: "To cause the people to be content in their fields and villages…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
而亡嘆息愁恨者其惟良二千石乎言守
重也又曰郎官出宰百里苟非其人民受
其殃言令重也三代而下惟漢世良吏為
盛然觀班史所傳西漢之吏僅僅六人則
黃霸朱邑王成龔遂文翁召信臣是已范
史所傳東漢之吏僅僅十二人則衛颯任
延王景之秦彭王渙許荊孟嘗劉寵第五
倫童恢劉矩仇覽是已夫是數子獨以循
良稱意其時必有奇樹偉績赫然一時而
===
標異方冊也及考其所述不過曰謹身率
先興敎化也廉平不苛尚仁恕也為民興
利巡阡陌也夫此數事一庸眾人可按法
而治亡他奇也若夫斤斤自號如投巫鄴
水一郡震驚有西門豹者銍筩發奸人稱
神明有趙廣漢者魯恭宰中牟蝗不入境
馴雉應而豎子興仁因以三異徵奇廉范
治成都聽民夜作厲禁削而百姓歡呼至
以五袴詠德非不卓然見奇也而循吏之
punctuated: 而亡嘆息愁恨者，其惟良二千石乎！」言守重也。又曰：「郎官出宰百里，苟非其人，民受其殃。」言令重也。三代而下，惟漢世良吏為盛。然觀班史所傳，西漢之吏僅僅六人，則黃霸、朱邑、王成、龔遂、文翁、召信臣是已；范史所傳，東漢之吏僅僅十二人，則衛颯、任延、王景之、秦彭、王渙、許荊、孟嘗、劉寵、第五倫、童恢、劉矩、仇覽是已。夫是數子獨以循良稱，意其時必有奇樹偉績，赫然一時，而標異方冊也。及考其所述，不過曰謹身率先，興敎化也；廉平不苛，尚仁恕也；為民興利，巡阡陌也。夫此數事，一庸眾人可按法而治，亡他奇也。若夫斤斤自號，如投巫鄴水，一郡震驚，有西門豹者；銍筩發奸，人稱神明，有趙廣漢者；魯恭宰中牟，蝗不入境，馴雉應而豎子興仁，因以「三異」徵奇；廉范治成都，聽民夜作，厲禁削而百姓歡呼，至以「五袴」詠德，非不卓然見奇也，而循吏之…
translation_en:
…and free from sighing, sorrow, and resentment—is that not the work solely of our good two-thousand-bushel officials [Commandery Governors]!’ This speaks to the importance of the Governor. Another [emperor] said: ‘Court Gentlemen go out to govern regions of a hundred li [districts]; if they are not the right men, the common people suffer calamity from them.’ This speaks to the importance of the District Magistrate.

From the Three Dynasties downward, good officials flourished most of all in the Han era. Yet when we examine those recorded in Ban [Gu]’s History [Book of Han (Hanshu)], the upright officials of the Western Han numbered a mere six men: namely, Huang Ba 黃霸, Zhu Yi 朱邑, Wang Cheng 王成, Gong Sui 龔遂, Wen Weng 文翁, and Shao Xinchen 召信臣. And among those recorded in Fan [Ye]’s History [Book of the Later Han (Hou Hanshu)], the upright officials of the Eastern Han numbered a mere twelve men: namely, Wei Sa 衛颯, Ren Yan 任延, Wang Jing 王景 [with a superfluous 之 in text?], Qin Peng 秦彭, Wang Huan 王渙, Xu Jing 許荊, Meng Chang 孟嘗, Liu Chong 劉寵, Diwu Lun 第五倫, Tong Hui 童恢, Liu Ju 劉矩, and Qiu Lan 仇覽.

Now, since these several gentlemen alone were acclaimed as dutiful and good officials, one might suppose that in their day they must have achieved extraordinary feats and grand accomplishments, dazzling their generation and standing out as marvels in the historical records. Yet when we examine what is recounted of them, it says nothing more than that they were circumspect in their own conduct and led by example in promoting moral teaching and transformation; that they were incorruptible, fair-minded, and not harsh, prizing benevolence and reciprocity; and that they promoted what was beneficial to the people, inspecting the field paths and dykes. Now, these few matters are things that even an ordinary, mediocre person could manage by following the regulations; there is nothing else extraordinary about them.

As for those who made a calculating display to win a name for themselves—such as Ximen Bao 西門豹, who cast the shamans into the waters of Ye 鄴, shocking the entire commandery; or Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢, who used a bamboo receptacle for secret denunciations to expose villainy, so that people acclaimed him as divine in discernment; or Lu Gong 魯恭, who governed Zhongmou 中牟, where locusts did not enter the borders, pheasants grew tame in response, and a young boy was moved to benevolence, thereby manifesting marvels through the ‘Three Wonders’; or Lian Fan 廉范, who governed Chengdu 成都 and permitted the people to work by night, abolishing strict prohibitions [against night fires] so that the common folk cheered and even sang of his virtue with the song of the ‘Five Pairs of Trousers’—it is not that these were notoutstanding displays of the extraordinary, and yet the biographies of dutiful officials…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
傳乃不在此而在彼者豈非以武健材明
終遠道德齊禮之化而表奇釣譽非鳴琴
不下堂之治歟彼吏之所謂循者服道德
明世務居官如家視民如子所居民富所
去見思有悶悶之政無赫赫之名誠專于
敦本務實而非世所稱一切辦給之能可
同日語也通乎此而吏治之得失兩漢之
所由盛者彰彰明矣我
國家加惠元元慎重守令而責成以學校農
===
桑戶口田野詞訟盜賊之六事法最詳也
皇上卽位之初宣諭嚴切又大計羣吏賞卓異
以榮之而治其尤不職者數人德意勤矣
然而澤不下究民或愁嘆而治效罔臻誠
有如執事所憂者何哉蓋今天下之吏有
如傷銘座保百姓如嬰兒者矣而視民命
同草菅以赤子之生死而佐其喜怒者不
盡無也有却硯選錢不以毫毛自玷者矣
而以狠牧羊剝民膏髓而不顧者不盡無
punctuated:
傳，乃不在此而在彼者，豈非以武健材明終遠道德齊禮之化，而表奇釣譽非鳴琴不下堂之治歟？彼吏之所謂循者，服道德、明世務，居官如家，視民如子，所居民富，所去見思，有悶悶之政，無赫赫之名，誠專于敦本務實，而非世所稱一切辦給之能可同日語也。通乎此，而吏治之得失、兩漢之所由盛者，彰彰明矣。

我國家加惠元元，慎重守令，而責成以學校、農桑、戶口、田野、詞訟、盜賊之六事，法最詳也。皇上卽位之初，宣諭嚴切，又大計羣吏，賞卓異以榮之，而治其尤不職者數人，德意勤矣。然而澤不下究，民或愁嘆，而治效罔臻，誠有如執事所憂者，何哉？蓋今天下之吏，有「如傷」銘座、保百姓如嬰兒者矣；而視民命同草菅，以赤子之生死而佐其喜怒者，不盡無也。有却硯選錢、不以毫毛自玷者矣；而以狠牧羊，剝民膏髓而不顧者，不盡無…
translation_en:
… biographies [of Upright Officials] do not lie with these men, but rather with those others—is this not because stern vigor and clever talent ultimately remain far removed from transformation through moral virtue and ritual order, and because displaying marvels and fishing for fame are not the governance of strumming the zither without descending from the hall? Those whom we call upright among officials adhere to moral virtue and understand worldly affairs; they treat their offices like their own homes and regard the common people like their own children. Where they reside, the people prosper; when they depart, they are fondly remembered. Their governance is quiet and unassuming, and they possess no blazing reputation. Truly, they concentrate on honoring the fundamentals and attending to practical realities, and cannot be spoken of in the same breath as what the world calls the ability to manage everything with expedient efficiency. Once one comprehends this, the successes and failures of official governance, as well as the reasons why the Two Han dynasties flourished, become abundantly clear.

Our Dynasty bestows favor upon the common people, exercises great care in selecting Prefects and Magistrates, and holds them accountable for the Six Matters—schools, agriculture and sericulture, household registration, cultivated land, litigation, and banditry—so the regulations are most detailed. At the very beginning of His Majesty's reign, he issued stern and earnest proclamations; moreover, at the Great Reckoning of all officials, he rewarded those of outstanding merit to honor them and punished several who were particularly derelict in their duties. His benevolent intentions have been diligent indeed! Yet blessings do not reach down to the lowest levels, the people at times sigh in distress, and effective governance is not achieved, truly just as Your Reverence has worried—why is this? It is because among the officials of the empire today, there are indeed those who inscribe "as if tending the wounded" upon their seats and protect the common people as though they were infants; yet those who regard the lives of the people as mere grass and weeds, using the life and death of the Sovereign's innocent children to indulge their own moods of pleasure and anger, are not entirely absent. There are indeed those who refuse inkstones and select a single coin, not sullying themselves by so much as a hair's breadth; yet those who herd sheep like wolves [reading 狼 for 狠], stripping away the fat and marrow of the people without a second thought, are not entirely absent…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
也甚則依阿淟涊託之乎通變詞伺儇媮
託之乎才幹匿智閟鑠託之乎藏用冥行
喜功託之乎勇敢苟可以收名而不必獲
實不去也苟可以獲實而不必收名不居
也爲下者習王成之故智且以僞增戶口
而希賞爲上者執張敞之偏見反以力行
敎化而致譏方今之患大率坐此執事欲
崇實政而黜虛文甚盛心也愚請先言其
弊可乎今之爲吏者其弊有二而今之察
===
吏者其弊亦有二尚苛刻急功利吏之弊
也狥毀譽拘繩墨察吏之弊也夫水之深
也魚鼈生焉激而躍之則鱗介之族無弗
駭矣山之茂也鳥獸歸焉剪其椔翳張之
罝畢則羽毛之族無弗駭矣今吏道率務
精采獵能聲察見及淵魚而操下若濕薪
民且囂然喪其樂生之心而元氣日以耗
矣此苛刻之不可尚也夫急轡御者非千
里之節也急刀刃者非磔解之神也今則
punctuated: 也。甚則依阿淟涊，託之乎通變；詞伺儇媮，託之乎才幹；匿智閟鑠，託之乎藏用；冥行喜功，託之乎勇敢。苟可以收名而不必獲實，不去也；苟可以獲實而不必收名，不居也。爲下者習王成之故智，且以僞增戶口而希賞；爲上者執張敞之偏見，反以力行敎化而致譏。方今之患，大率坐此。執事欲崇實政而黜虛文，甚盛心也。愚請先言其弊，可乎？今之爲吏者，其弊有二；而今之察吏者，其弊亦有二。尚苛刻、急功利，吏之弊也；狥毀譽、拘繩墨，察吏之弊也。夫水之深也，魚鼈生焉，激而躍之，則鱗介之族無弗駭矣；山之茂也，鳥獸歸焉，剪其椔翳，張之罝畢，則羽毛之族無弗駭矣。今吏道率務精采，獵能聲，察見及淵魚，而操下若濕薪，民且囂然喪其樂生之心，而元氣日以耗矣。此苛刻之不可尚也。夫急轡御者，非千里之節也；急刀刃者，非磔解之神也。今則
translation_en:
… In extreme cases, those who are obsequious and corrupt excuse it as adaptability; those who spy [?詞伺 for 窺伺] and are glib and opportunistic excuse it as administrative talent; those who conceal their wits and hide their brilliance excuse it as keeping their utility in reserve; and those who act recklessly and crave exploits excuse it as courage. If a course of action can win them reputation without necessarily achieving real results, they will not abandon it; if it can achieve real results without necessarily winning them reputation, they will not occupy themselves with it. Subordinates practice the old trick of Wang Cheng 王成, even falsifying population increases in hopes of reward; superiors cling to the biased view of Zhang Chang 張敞, conversely drawing ridicule upon those who strive to carry out moral transformation. The ills of the present day largely stem from this. Your Honor wishes to exalt substantive governance and dismiss empty formalism—this is a most noble intention. May this humble candidate ask to speak first of the abuses?

Among those who serve as officials today, there are two abuses; and among those who evaluate officials today, there are likewise two abuses. Valuing harshness and rushing after immediate utility and profit are the abuses of officials; yielding to praise and blame and clinging rigidly to rules and regulations are the abuses of those who evaluate officials.

Now, when waters are deep, fish and turtles thrive therein; if one churns the water and makes it leap, none of the scaly and shelled creatures will fail to be startled. When mountains are lush, birds and beasts flock to them; if one clears away their deadwood and undergrowth and spreads nets and snares across them, none of the feathered and furred creatures will fail to be startled. Today, the way of officialdom generally strives for flashy brilliance and hunts for a reputation for competence. Their scrutiny reaches the fish in the depths, and they bind their subordinates like bundled wet firewood. The people become clamorous and lose their joy in living, while the vital energy of the state is daily depleted. This is why harshness must not be valued.

Now, driving with a taut rein is not the pace for a thousand-li journey; hacking hastily with a blade is not the marvelous skill of dismembering an ox. Today, however, …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
專事炫飾建白易置功不可成者倖其成
法不當變者輕於變政令未布而案牘日
煩且曰吾能興民利除民害是誰欺乎此
功利之不可急也夫人有得燕石者或言
之曰此玉也則信而藏之人有鬻朴者驟
而聞之曰此璞也則慕而求之故燕石之
亂目朴之亂耳誠亦有之彼佞合者不倡
而和乘人而中其懽所憎則堯舜可非也
所喜則桀紂可譽也甚或計禮數而持短
===
長據好尚以定賢否不幾於失真矣乎此
毀譽之不可徇也夫考牧事者視牛羊之
贏詘而已矣不必煩爲之驅也課農業者
視其所入之多寡而已矣不必力自已出
也今以一守令而大吏十數人制于其上
四方之兵甲錢穀營建徵發守令所得相
宜而從事者而今弗敢也一方之均賦平
刑恤煢達滯守令所得控制而罷行者而
今弗敢也以其有所顧忌而掣肘也此繩
punctuated: 專事炫飾，建白易置，功不可成者倖其成，法不當變者輕於變。政令未布，而案牘日煩，且曰：「吾能興民利、除民害。」是誰欺乎？此功利之不可急也。夫人有得燕石者，或言之曰：「此玉也。」則信而藏之。人有鬻朴者，驟而聞之曰：「此璞也。」則慕而求之。故燕石之亂目、朴之亂耳，誠亦有之。彼佞合者，不倡而和，乘人而中其懽；所憎則堯、舜可非也，所喜則桀、紂可譽也。甚或計禮數而持短長，據好尚以定賢否，不幾於失真矣乎？此毀譽之不可徇也。夫考牧事者，視牛羊之贏詘而已矣，不必煩爲之驅也；課農業者，視其所入之多寡而已矣，不必力自已出也。今以一守令，而大吏十數人制于其上。四方之兵甲、錢穀、營建、徵發，守令所得相宜而從事者，而今弗敢也；一方之均賦、平刑、恤煢、達滯，守令所得控制而罷行者，而今弗敢也，以其有所顧忌而掣肘也。此繩…
translation_en:
…focus exclusively on ostentatious display, proposing changes and replacements: where achievements cannot be brought to fruition, they hope by chance to succeed; where laws ought not to be altered, they lightly alter them. Before policies and ordinances are even promulgated, official documents grow daily more burdensome, and yet they say: "I am able to promote the people's welfare and eliminate the people's harms." Whom are they deceiving? This is why quick results and immediate profit must not be hastily pursued.

Now, suppose someone obtains a stone from Yan, and someone else says of it, "This is jade"—so he believes it and treasures it away. Or suppose someone is selling dried rat meat [pu 朴], and another, suddenly hearing the sound of the word, thinks, "This is uncarved jade [pu 璞]"—so he admires it and seeks to buy it. Thus, that stones of Yan confuse the eye and rat meat confuses the ear is truly something that happens. Those who flatter and curry favor echo others without taking the lead, seizing upon people's inclinations to hit upon what delights them. Toward those they hate, even Yao and Shun can be condemned; toward those they favor, even Jie and Zhou can be praised. Worse still, some calculate courtesies and protocols tofind fault or merit, or rely on personal preferences to determine who is worthy and who is unworthy—does this not come close to losing the truth entirely? This is why slander and praise must not be blindly followed.

Now, one who evaluates herding merely looks at whether the cattle and sheep are thriving or depleted; he need not trouble himself to drive them around. One who assesses farming merely looks at the abundance or scarcity of the harvest; the physical labor need not come from himself. Today, over a single prefect or magistrate, there are a dozen or more high officials controlling him from above. Matters of military armor, money and grain, construction, and levies across the region are things that prefects and magistrates ought to be able to handle as appropriate to the circumstances—yet nowadays they do not dare to do so. Equalizing taxes, meting out fair punishments, relieving the solitary and destitute, and clearing up backlogs within a locality are things that prefects and magistrates ought to be able to manage, whether to discontinue or put into practice—yet nowadays they do not dare to do so, because they have apprehensions and their hands are tied. This is why rigid rules and regulations…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
墨之不可拘也誠使爲監司者而知此精
其藻鑑不以毀譽亂是非握其權衡不以
文法撓治體非無舉也舉必當賢非無刺
也刺必當罪奬恬淡而抑浮兢喜平易而
惡深文不以巧慧最老成不以險詐上忠
厚禮節闊略而孚至誠簿書不煩而持體
要利苟可興不必請而後行弊苟可革不
必議而後罷夫上以名求下故可以名應
上以實求下不可不以實應所謂實者無
===
他卽於
國家六事之責而加之意焉耳以實心興學
校使學校日興如古之感化蜀民文風比
齊魯者而後可也以實心勸農桑使農桑
日繁如古之勸農而嘉禾無螟犯者而後
可也以實心稽戶口使戶口日增如古之
爲令而鄰縣民歸者而後可也以實心闢
田野使田野日闢如古之歲增漑田三萬
頃者而後可也以實心弭盜賊使盜賊日
punctuated: 墨之不可拘也。誠使爲監司者而知此，精其藻鑑，不以毀譽亂是非；握其權衡，不以文法撓治體。非無舉也，舉必當賢；非無刺也，刺必當罪。奬恬淡而抑浮兢，喜平易而惡深文，不以巧慧最老成，不以險詐上忠厚。禮節闊略而孚至誠，簿書不煩而持體要。利苟可興，不必請而後行；弊苟可革，不必議而後罷。夫上以名求，下故可以名應；上以實求，下不可不以實應。所謂實者，無他，卽於國家六事之責而加之意焉耳。以實心興學校，使學校日興，如古之感化蜀民，文風比齊魯者，而後可也；以實心勸農桑，使農桑日繁，如古之勸農，而嘉禾無螟犯者，而後可也；以實心稽戶口，使戶口日增，如古之爲令，而鄰縣民歸者，而後可也；以實心闢田野，使田野日闢，如古之歲增漑田三萬頃者，而後可也；以實心弭盜賊，使盜賊日
translation_en: … strict rules cannot be rigidly adhered to. If those who serve as Regional Inspectors and Surveillance Commissioners truly understand this, they will refine their discernment and not let slander or flattery confound right and wrong; they will hold firm the scales of judgment and not let legalistic technicalities disrupt the substance of governance. It is not that there are no recommendations, but recommendations must match true worth; it is not that there are no impeachments, but impeachments must match actual offenses. They will encourage quiet modesty and curb superficial competition, favor plain fairness and detest harsh legalism, not rank cleverness above seasoned maturity, nor place treacherous deceit above loyal honesty. They will relax ceremonial formalities to inspire utmost sincerity, and avoid burdensome paperwork to uphold the essential principles. If a benefit can be promoted, it need not wait for a petition before being carried out; if an abuse can be eliminated, it need not wait for deliberation before being abolished. Now, when superiors seek only reputation, subordinates can respond with mere reputation; when superiors seek reality, subordinates cannot but respond with reality. What is called reality is nothing other than paying earnest attention to the state's six administrative duties. Only when one promotes schools with a sincere heart, causing schools to flourish daily—like those in antiquity who transformed the people of Shu until their literary culture equaled that of Qi and Lu—will it suffice. Only when one encourages agriculture and sericulture with a sincere heart, causing agriculture and sericulture to prosper daily—like those in antiquity who encouraged farming so that fine grain suffered no pest damage—will it suffice. Only when one audits households and population with a sincere heart, causing the registered population to increase daily—like those in antiquity who served as magistrates and drew people from neighboring counties to give allegiance—will it suffice. Only when one opens up farmlands with a sincere heart, causing farmlands to expand daily—like those in antiquity who annually increased irrigated fields by thirty thousand qing—will it suffice. Only when one suppresses bandits and thieves with a sincere heart, causing bandits and thieves daily…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
以屛息如古之化刀劒爲牛犢者而後可
也以實心理詞訟使詞訟日以清簡如古
之治獄八年無重囚者而後可也無因循
以廢章程無紛更以乖俗尚無紛端而寡
究無滯往而鮮功吏以此治民故澤不壅
而常流上以此察吏故情不隔而常達悃
愊者不病于難知粉飾者不至於倖售政
何以不若古人而治何以不臻實效哉由
是而績用有叙者則增秩以觀其成久任
===
亦可行也由是而賢能異等者則殊擢以
示其勸超遷亦可行也此則銓曹之責也
若夫端揆肅紀微機在相臣建極維風本
原在
主上愚生并有望焉
第四問
毛志尹
同考試官敎諭曾批泉貨流通全在法
制一定而官民通用子能言之而終之以利害真偽之辨甚中肯綮
punctuated:
以屛息，如古之化刀劒爲牛犢者，而後可也；以實心理詞訟，使詞訟日以清簡，如古之治獄八年無重囚者，而後可也。無因循以廢章程，無紛更以乖俗尚，無紛端而寡究，無滯往而鮮功。吏以此治民，故澤不壅而常流；上以此察吏，故情不隔而常達。悃愊者不病于難知，粉飾者不至於倖售，政何以不若古人，而治何以不臻實效哉？由是而績用有叙者，則增秩以觀其成，久任亦可行也；由是而賢能異等者，則殊擢以示其勸，超遷亦可行也。此則銓曹之責也。若夫端揆肅紀，微機在相臣；建極維風，本原在主上，愚生并有望焉。

第四問

毛志尹
同考試官敎諭曾批：泉貨流通，全在法制一定而官民通用。子能言之，而終之以利害真偽之辨，甚中肯綮。
translation_en:
… subside day by day, like the ancient who turned swords and blades into oxen and calves—only then will it do; and with a sincere heart manage litigation so that lawsuits become clearer and simpler day by day, like the ancient who adjudicated cases for eight years without a single capital prisoner—only then will it do. Let there be no perfunctory routine that neglects established regulations, no capricious changes that go against local customs, no multiplication of initiatives with little follow-through, and no clinging to the past with meager results. When officials govern the people by these means, beneficence is not blocked and constantly flows; when superiors evaluate officials by these means, true conditions are not cut off and are constantly communicated. The sincere and unpretentious will not suffer from being hard to recognize, and those who merely window-dress will not succeed by lucky chance. Why then would governance not equal that of the ancients, and why would order not achieve genuine efficacy? From this, for those whose achievements are in due order, their rank may be increased while observing their completion of the work, and long tenure can also be practiced; for those whose worth and ability are of an extraordinary grade, they may be specially promoted to show encouragement, and supernumerary advancement can also be practiced. This, then, is the responsibility of the Ministry of Personnel. As for rectifying the norms of governance and enforcing discipline, the subtle hinge lies with the grand secretaries; as for establishing the supreme standard and upholding mores, the fundamental source lies with the Sovereign above—for both of which this foolish student likewise harbors hope.

Fourth Question

Mao Zhiyin 毛志尹
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zeng 曾: The circulation of coinage depends entirely on the regulations being fixed and its use being common to both officials and the people. You are able to articulate this, and conclude with a distinction between benefit and harm, genuine and counterfeit, which hits the crucial point very well.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批錢乃足用之大者導利於
上下王者所以成天地之能也此作得旨
考試官教諭鄭批鑄錢因革敷對詳明
考試官學正馮批條達無遺
嘗謂天地有自然之利導利以前民用者
裁成輔相之功也斯人有無窮之欲定制
以防民偽者整齊嚴肅之法也何則造化
陶鎔乎萬物一洪鑪大冶也食貨之所資
不出於山林川澤然必導利於下而後可
===
以收生養之功王者範圍乎萬民一神工
大陶也法令之所出莫妙乎變通鼓舞然
必定制於上而後可以息爭奪之欲故曰
天生五材民並用之惟君出令而民從之
成天地之能操統御之柄寧非人君之所
有事哉執事以錢法下詢承學請詳言之
今夫造化生物莫非福澤乎民而體重用
神者必歸於五金五金之利利也取五金
之一而鑄錢尤利之大也利大則民趨而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：錢乃足用之大者，導利於上下，王者所以成天地之能也。此作得旨。
考試官教諭鄭批：鑄錢因革，敷對詳明。
考試官學正馮批：條達無遺。

嘗謂天地有自然之利，導利以前民用者，裁成輔相之功也；斯人有無窮之欲，定制以防民偽者，整齊嚴肅之法也。何則？造化陶鎔乎萬物，一洪鑪大冶也，食貨之所資，不出於山林川澤，然必導利於下，而後可以收生養之功；王者範圍乎萬民，一神工大陶也，法令之所出，莫妙乎變通鼓舞，然必定制於上，而後可以息爭奪之欲。故曰：「天生五材，民並用之。」惟君出令，而民從之。成天地之能，操統御之柄，寧非人君之所有事哉？執事以錢法下詢，承學請詳言之。

今夫造化生物，莫非福澤乎民，而體重用神者，必歸於五金。五金之利，利也；取五金之一而鑄錢，尤利之大也。利大則民趨，而
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen: Coinage is a major means of ensuring sufficiency of resources; channeling its benefit between those above and those below is whereby a true king completes the capabilities of Heaven and Earth. This composition grasps the essential meaning.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Zheng: On the continuities and changes in minting coins, the exposition in response is detailed and clear.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Feng: Well-ordered, fluent, and comprehensive.

I have heard it said that Heaven and Earth possess natural resources, and that channeling those benefits to advance the people's use is the achievement of regulating and assisting nature; meanwhile, humans possess boundless desires, and establishing fixed institutions to guard against popular deceit is the method of bringing order and strictness. Why is this so? The creative forces of nature mold and smelt all things like a vast furnace and great foundry. The resources for food and commodities come from nowhere else than mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes, yet one must channel their benefits to those below before one can reap the achievements of nourishing life. A true king encompasses the myriad people like a divine craftsman and great potter. In the issuing of laws and ordinances, nothing is more marvelous than adapting to change and inspiring action, yet one must establish fixed regulations from above before one can quell the desires of contention and seizure. Thus it is said: "Heaven produces the five materials, and the people use them all." Only the ruler issues commands, and the people follow them. Completing the capabilities of Heaven and Earth and wielding the handle of governance—is this not the proper business of the sovereign? Since Your Excellency has inquired of us below regarding monetary policy, this humble student begs leave to speak of it in detail.

Now, when the creative forces bring forth things, there is none that does not bestow blessings upon the people, yet those whose substance is weighty and whose utility is marvelous must be attributed to the five metals. The benefit of the five metals is indeed a benefit; taking one of the five metals and minting coins from it is an even greater benefit. When the benefit is great, the people rush toward it, and…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
亂由玆啓矣棄利則民困而國由玆病矣
皆非也王者興利於民而持阿於己作法
於始而嚴禁於終於是權在上而不在下
民旣足而國亦裕故錢不可不鑄也鑄中
錢而不鑄大小錢則利鑄於上而不鑄於
下則利此萬世不易之定論也稽古禹湯
伐二山之銅太公立九府之法固以開財
之源而盡人之能矣司市行布阜商外府
泉府掌布待用是官有所入而民有所出
===
矣法善而心公泉流而布布是以上下交
相利而致殷富之治有由然也後世不知
法此而煩其令者若文帝弛盜鑄之禁吳
王專私鑄之利武帝下更鑄之令元帝罷
鑄錢之官孫權聽民鑄大錢王安石縱民
日銷錢若是乎變更之不同識者亦紛紛
議之矣大抵亂則無紀私則不公以言乎
虧國困民則均焉中惟漢武帝禁革輕小
更鑄五銖錢得圜法遺意而便於用此五
punctuated: 亂由玆啓矣；棄利則民困，而國由玆病矣。皆非也。王者興利於民而持阿於己，作法於始而嚴禁於終，於是權在上而不在下，民旣足而國亦裕。故錢不可不鑄也。鑄中錢而不鑄大小錢則利，鑄於上而不鑄於下則利，此萬世不易之定論也。稽古禹、湯伐二山之銅，太公立九府之法，固以開財之源而盡人之能矣。司市行布阜商，外府、泉府掌布待用，是官有所入而民有所出矣。法善而心公，泉流而布布，是以上下交相利，而致殷富之治有由然也。後世不知法此而煩其令者，若文帝弛盜鑄之禁，吳王專私鑄之利，武帝下更鑄之令，元帝罷鑄錢之官，孫權聽民鑄大錢，王安石縱民日銷錢，若是乎變更之不同，識者亦紛紛議之矣。大抵亂則無紀，私則不公，以言乎虧國困民則均焉。中惟漢武帝禁革輕小，更鑄五銖錢，得圜法遺意而便於用，此五
translation_en:
… disorder begins from this; yet if one abandons that profit, the people suffer hardship and the state grows weak from this. Both approaches are wrong. A true king generates profit for the people while holding the handle of authority [?] himself, establishing regulations at the outset and strictly enforcing prohibitions to the end. Thus, authority resides above and not below; the people have sufficiency and the state is likewise prosperous. Therefore, coins must not fail to be minted. It is beneficial to mint medium-sized coins and not large or small ones; it is beneficial for minting to be done by those above and not by those below. This is a settled conclusion unchanged for ten thousand generations.

Examining antiquity, Yu 禹 and Tang 湯 mined copper from the two mountains, and the Grand Duke (Taigong 太公) established the Nine Repositories (Jiufu 九府) currency regulations, certainly in order to open the sources of wealth and bring human capabilities to the fullest. Under the Zhou, the Supervisor of Markets (Sishi 司市) circulated cloth-money (bu 布) to enrich merchants, while the Outer Treasury (Waifu 外府) and Currency Office (Quanfu 泉府) managed the coinage awaiting expenditure; thus the officials had revenues and the people had expenditures. Because the laws were good and intentions public-spirited, money flowed like a spring (quan 泉) and spread like cloth (bu 布). Consequently, superior and inferior mutually benefitted one another, and there was good reason why they achieved an administration of abundant wealth.

In later ages, there were those who did not know to take this as their model and instead complicated their ordinances: for instance, Emperor Wen 文帝 of Han relaxed the prohibition against illicit minting; the King of Wu 吳王 monopolized the profits of private minting; Emperor Wu 武帝 issued orders to recoin currency; Emperor Yuan 元帝 abolished the offices in charge of minting; Sun Quan 孫權 permitted the people to mint large coins; and Wang Anshi 王安石 allowed the people to melt down coins daily. With changes as varied as these, men of discernment have also debated them in great profusion. In general, disorder leads to a lack of discipline, and private interest leads to a lack of fairness; in terms of harming the state and distressing the people, they were all the same. Among them, only Emperor Wu of Han prohibited and abolished light and small coins, minting instead the five-zhu (wuzhu 五銖) coin, which captured the bequeathed intent of the ancient round-currency system (huanfa 圜法) and was convenient for use.
