title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
銖所以行於數代也後有不知鑒此而煩
其式者或半兩榆莢或八銖四銖其名互
更乃始變也或赤仄當千或鵝眼荇葉其
體各異乃再變也若是乎輕重之不齊小
民亦洶洶苦之矣大抵大則病銅小則病
物以言乎虧國困民則均焉中惟唐高祖
斟酌低昻置造開元錢倣五銖遺法而增
文郭此開元所以行於後世也若夫用鹿
皮藻幣以代錢者意在抑大賈其實遺大
===
害錢遂阻格而不行乃漢之弊也令富家
合券號飛錢者意在便輕裝其實滋詐偽
民遂窮乏而無策乃唐之繆也求其商確
時事動中機宜者吾有取於賈誼劉秩孔
顗三子焉漢文帝放民鑄錢亦厚下之心
也誼上七福之說如黥罪不積偽錢不蓄
鑄者反耕挾銅平貨等議皆通達國體之
見終之以制吾棄財與匈奴逐爭其民其
意更深遠矣張九齡縱民自鑄亦散財之
punctuated: 銖所以行於數代也。後有不知鑒此而煩其式者，或半兩、榆莢，或八銖、四銖，其名互更，乃始變也；或赤仄、當千，或鵝眼、荇葉，其體各異，乃再變也。若是乎輕重之不齊，小民亦洶洶苦之矣。大抵大則病銅，小則病物，以言乎虧國困民則均焉。中惟唐高祖斟酌低昻，置造開元錢，倣五銖遺法而增文郭，此開元所以行於後世也。若夫用鹿皮、藻幣以代錢者，意在抑大賈，其實遺大害，錢遂阻格而不行，乃漢之弊也；令富家合券號「飛錢」者，意在便輕裝，其實滋詐偽，民遂窮乏而無策，乃唐之繆也。求其商確時事、動中機宜者，吾有取於賈誼、劉秩、孔顗三子焉。漢文帝放民鑄錢，亦厚下之心也，誼上「七福」之說，如黥罪不積、偽錢不蓄、鑄者反耕、挾銅平貨等議，皆通達國體之見，終之以「制吾棄財，與匈奴逐爭其民」，其意更深遠矣。張九齡縱民自鑄，亦散財之
translation_en: … [five-]zhu coins circulated through several dynasties. Later, those who did not know to take this as a mirror and complicated the specifications—whether banliang or "elm-pod" (yujia) coins, or eight-zhu or four-zhu coins, with names repeatedly altered—marked the first change; whether red-rimmed (chize) or "worth-a-thousand" (dangqian) coins, or "goose-eye" (eyan) or "water-fringe" (xingye) coins, each differing in form—marked the second change. With weights so uneven, the common people were thrown into turmoil and suffered bitterly from it. Broadly speaking, when coins are too large, it harms the copper supply; when too small, it harms the value of goods. In terms of damaging the state and distressing the people, the result is the same. Among them, only Emperor Gaozu of Tang weighed the balance of heavy and light and instituted the Kaiyuan coin, imitating the bequeathed method of the five-zhu coin while adding inscriptions and rims; this is why the Kaiyuan coin circulated in later generations. As for using white deerskin and ornate currency [?] (zaobi) to replace coins, the intention was to curb great merchants, yet in reality it left behind great harm, so that coins were obstructed and failed to circulate—this was the abuse of the Han. Ordering wealthy households to match tallies called "flying cash" (feiqian) was intended to facilitate light travel, yet in reality it bred fraud and forgery, so that the people became impoverished and had no recourse—this was the error of the Tang. If we seek those who deliberated on contemporary affairs and consistently hit the mark of what was opportune, I find merit in the three masters Jia Yi 賈誼, Liu Zhi 劉秩, and Kong Yi 孔顗. When Emperor Wen of Han allowed the people to mint coins, it too came from a desire to be generous to those below. Jia Yi submitted his discourse on the "Seven Blessings," with arguments such as that the crime of facial tattooing would not accumulate, counterfeit coins would not be hoarded, minters would return to farming, and holding copper would stabilize goods—all views thoroughly conversant with the principles of statecraft—and concluded with "controlling our discarded wealth to compete with the Xiongnu for their people," whose meaning was even more profound and far-reaching. When Zhang Jiuling 張九齡 permitted the people to mint on their own, it too came from a desire to disperse wealth…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
意也秩有四美之規如銅不布下而盜鑄
無因公錢不破錢貨日增等條皆洞察時
艱之言繫之以人不犯刑於中其識更卓
越矣若顒在南齊推原盜鑄之禍由於人
主惜銅愛工發爲議論惟銅擅於官而不
惜則體質厚而肉好適均工出於上而不
愛則製作精而輪郭周正此則息盜鑄之
原夫亦救弊之見也然就三子而論之誼
秩欲操公鑄之柄而銖兩不定何以得中
===
正之制顒欲杜私鑄之奸而小患不計寔
以開大錢之端卒之美利不歸於初漢功
費竟寢於南齊難免君子之遺論焉洪惟
我
太祖高皇帝建極之前即創大中通寶混一之
後再鑄洪武通寶以垂法而利民
列聖相承各鑄通寶而冠以年號取五銖開元
而較量之偉然中正之規若今永樂宣德
弘治嘉靖隆慶等寶謂非可流布於萬世
punctuated:
意也。秩有四美之規，如銅不布下而盜鑄無因，公錢不破、錢貨日增等條，皆洞察時艱之言；繫之以人不犯刑於中，其識更卓越矣。若顒在南齊，推原盜鑄之禍，由於人主惜銅愛工，發爲議論：惟銅擅於官而不惜，則體質厚而肉好適均；工出於上而不愛，則製作精而輪郭周正。此則息盜鑄之原，夫亦救弊之見也。然就三子而論之：誼、秩欲操公鑄之柄，而銖兩不定，何以得中正之制？顒欲杜私鑄之奸，而小患不計，寔以開大錢之端。卒之美利不歸於初漢，功費竟寢於南齊，難免君子之遺論焉。

洪惟我太祖高皇帝，建極之前，即創大中通寶；混一之後，再鑄洪武通寶，以垂法而利民。列聖相承，各鑄通寶而冠以年號，取五銖、開元而較量之，偉然中正之規。若今永樂、宣德、弘治、嘉靖、隆慶等寶，謂非可流布於萬世
translation_en:
… intention. Liu Zhi 劉秩 offered his counsel of the "four merits," containing points such as that if copper is not distributed below, there will be no means for illicit minting, and that official coins will not be melted down while currency daily increases. These were all words that penetrated the difficulties of the times; and when he tied them together with the point that the people would not violate the penal laws in the process, his insight was all the more outstanding. As for Kong Yong 孔顒 [Kong Yi 孔顗] in the Southern Qi [note: historically Liu Song], he traced the disaster of illicit minting to the ruler begrudging copper and sparing labor, and set forth his argument: only when copper is monopolized by the state and not begrudged will the substance of the coin be thick and its body and center hole be properly proportioned; only when labor is supplied from above and not spared will the workmanship be fine and the outer and inner rims squarely aligned. This gets to the source of stopping illicit minting, and is indeed a view aimed at remedying abuses. Yet if we discuss the three men together: Jia Yi 賈誼 and Liu Zhi wished to hold the handle of official minting, but without fixing the weight in zhu and liang, how could one attain a balanced and proper standard? Kong Yong wished to stop the villainy of private minting, yet by disregarding minor troubles he actually opened the way for oversized coins. In the end, the fine benefits did not accrue to the early Han, and the labor and expense were ultimately shelved in the Southern Qi; thus they could hardly escape the lingering criticisms of gentlemen.

Thinking with awe upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), even before establishing the imperial throne he created the Dazhong tongbao 大中通寶 coin, and after unifying the realm he further minted the Hongwu tongbao 洪武通寶 coin to hand down a model and benefit the people. The successive sacred emperors inherited this practice, each minting circulating treasure coins headed by their reign titles. If one takes the Wuzhu 五銖 and Kaiyuan 開元 coins and compares them with these, ours are truly a magnificent, balanced, and proper standard. Such coins of the present dynasty as those of the Yongle, Xuande, Hongzhi, Jiajing, and Longqing reigns—how could one say they are not fit to be circulated for ten thousand generations…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
者乎奈何歷年以來鑄錢限於地而未徧
及乎寓內錢法行於北而未通行乎江南
間有用錢之地則又行於市肆而不達於
窮鄉用於民間而不通於官府少得疏通
則規利之徒四出磨滓淄染逞制於僞造
翦鑿鎔液津利於舊錢甚至伐山匿澤貽
患且無窮矣凡若此者蓋由上不操其柄
而利源未開下不遵其令而弊竇未塞欲
國富而民足也不能不待於今日矣惟我
===
皇上親賢圖治節用愛人惓惓以經
國用厚民生爲念邇者順天地之宜體財用
之大而鑄錢之令下焉是故銅有定價責
有專官開廣局於適中頒定式於各省始
也官發銀以鑄錢終也官收錢以抵銀且
約以十文市不二價而洪武永樂等寶與
歷代古錢兼行制無用之貨以通有用之
財何其盡善而盡美耶但天下之事利與
害每相因者也夫以銀權錢謂之母以其
punctuated: 者乎？奈何歷年以來，鑄錢限於地，而未徧及乎寓內；錢法行於北，而未通行乎江南。間有用錢之地，則又行於市肆，而不達於窮鄉；用於民間，而不通於官府。少得疏通，則規利之徒四出，磨滓淄染，逞制於僞造；翦鑿鎔液，津利於舊錢。甚至伐山匿澤，貽患且無窮矣。凡若此者，蓋由上不操其柄，而利源未開；下不遵其令，而弊竇未塞。欲國富而民足也，不能不待於今日矣。惟我皇上親賢圖治，節用愛人，惓惓以經國用、厚民生爲念。邇者，順天地之宜，體財用之大，而鑄錢之令下焉。是故銅有定價，責有專官，開廣局於適中，頒定式於各省。始也，官發銀以鑄錢；終也，官收錢以抵銀。且約以十文，市不二價，而洪武、永樂等寶與歷代古錢兼行。制無用之貨，以通有用之財，何其盡善而盡美耶！但天下之事，利與害每相因者也。夫以銀權錢，謂之「母」，以其…
translation_en:
… [could not be circulated for ten thousand generations]? Why is it that over the past years, the minting of coins has been restricted to certain localities and has not extended throughout the empire; and the monetary laws have operated in the north, yet have not circulated generally south of the Yangtze? Where there occasionally are places that use coins, they circulate in the urban markets without reaching isolated villages, and are used among the people without being accepted by government offices. As soon as they achieve a slight circulation, profit-seeking scoundrels emerge everywhere: grinding dross and dyeing it black to run rampant in counterfeiting, or clipping and melting down old coins to extract profit from them. It even goes so far that they strip the mountains and hide in the marshes, leaving behind endless troubles. All of this stems from the fact that those above do not hold firm control of the authority, so the sources of benefit have not been opened; while those below do not obey the ordinances, so the avenues of abuse have not been stopped up. If we wish for the state to be wealthy and the people well-supplied, it cannot but await the present day.

Now Our Majesty draws close to the worthy and plans for good governance, economizes on expenditures and cherishes the people, remaining earnestly mindful of regulating state finances and enriching the people's livelihood. Recently, in accordance with the appropriateness of Heaven and Earth and in recognition of the great importance of financial resources, the order to mint coins has been handed down. Therefore, copper has a fixed price, responsibility is vested in specialized officials, expansive mints are opened in centrally located places, and standard models are promulgated to the various provinces. In the beginning, the government issues silver to mint coins; in the end, the government collects coins in lieu of silver. Moreover, the rate is set at ten cash, with no dual pricing in the markets, and the Hongwu, Yongle, and other reign-period coins circulate alongside the ancient coins of past dynasties. Turning useless material into a medium that circulates useful wealth—how utterly perfect and admirable this is!

However, in the affairs of the world, benefit and harm always arise from one another. Now, using silver to weigh the value of coins is called the "mother" [currency], because its…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
銀貴於錢也今則假銀充斥市價相欺乃
恬不爲異寧無害於錢法乎嚴禁之可也
錢出於銅謂之利以其銅賤於錢也今則
銅價增高奸商坐索使鑄者傷本寧無害
於錢法乎折衷之可也真與偽每難辨者
也洪武永樂等錢銅美工精與新錢同體
矣惟古錢文制未備不可不辨也去其低
磽之甚定以十分之則不可行乎開元太
平等錢肉好適均與制錢同用矣若官府
===
止收新錢民將生疑阻焉新舊兼收以抵
差銀不可行乎果能此道將見蒙山盡獻
瑞之銅嚴道悉燒爐之野匪頒好用淵泉
斯流仰事俯育飛蚨貫索權歸於上而利
通於民參贊之功豈小補哉若行之旣久
而有阻撓私鑄者出焉則惟堅執吾之律
令申飭吾之法紀以救正之爾古人置上
林三官而滿山盜息得一第五倫而長安
姦除謂非得人行法之驗耶抑愚生猶有
punctuated: 銀貴於錢也。今則假銀充斥，市價相欺，乃恬不爲異，寧無害於錢法乎？嚴禁之可也。錢出於銅，謂之利，以其銅賤於錢也。今則銅價增高，奸商坐索，使鑄者傷本，寧無害於錢法乎？折衷之可也。真與偽每難辨者也。洪武、永樂等錢，銅美工精，與新錢同體矣；惟古錢文制未備，不可不辨也。去其低磽之甚，定以十分之則，不可行乎？開元、太平等錢，肉好適均，與制錢同用矣；若官府止收新錢，民將生疑阻焉。新舊兼收以抵差銀，不可行乎？果能此道，將見蒙山盡獻瑞之銅，嚴道悉燒爐之野；匪頒好用，淵泉斯流；仰事俯育，飛蚨貫索。權歸於上而利通於民，參贊之功豈小補哉！若行之旣久，而有阻撓私鑄者出焉，則惟堅執吾之律令，申飭吾之法紀以救正之爾。古人置上林三官而滿山盜息，得一第五倫而長安姦除，謂非得人行法之驗耶？抑愚生猶有
translation_en: … silver is more valuable than cash. Nowadays, however, counterfeit silver floods the market and merchants cheat one another over prices, yet people take this calmly and do not consider it strange. Could this fail to harm the monetary system? Strictly prohibiting it would be proper. Cash is produced from copper and is called "profit" because the copper is cheaper than the minted cash. Nowadays, however, the price of copper has risen high, and unscrupulous merchants sit back and demand extortionate prices, causing those who mint to suffer losses on their capital. Could this fail to harm the monetary system? Striking a fair balance in the price would be proper. The genuine and the counterfeit are often difficult to distinguish. Coins of the Hongwu and Yongle eras have fine copper and exquisite workmanship, sharing the same standard as the newly minted cash; only with ancient coins, whose inscriptions and forms are not uniform, must distinctions be made. If we eliminate those that are extremely debased and thin, and establish a ten-grade standard of valuation, would that not be workable? Coins such as those of the Kaiyuan and Taiping eras have well-proportioned rims and holes, and can be used alongside the standard imperial cash; if government offices accept only the new cash, the people will develop doubts and resistance. If both old and new are accepted together to offset labor-service silver payments, would that not be workable? If this way can truly be followed, we shall see Mount Meng offering up all its auspicious copper and Yandao becoming entirely a countryside of smelting furnaces; through imperial bestowal and the love of bounty, wealth will flow like a deep spring; for serving parents above and nurturing families below, "flying water-beetles" [coins] will be strung on cords. Monetary authority will revert to the ruler above while benefits circulate among the people below—how could this achievement in assisting the transformative work of Heaven and Earth be merely a minor supplement! If, after this has been practiced for a long time, there emerge those who obstruct the currency or engage in illicit minting, we need only firmly uphold our statutes and ordinances and strictly enforce our laws and discipline to rectify them. The ancients established the Three Offices of the Shanglin Park and bandits throughout the mountains ceased; they obtained a single Diwu Lun and illicit practices in Chang'an were eradicated. Can this be said not to be the proven effect of obtaining the right men to enforce the law? Yet your foolish student still has…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
說焉甞聞國裕則用奢民富則俗壞有識
之士是以懷卭山之憂抱近鹽之懼也使
在上者不思天地生財止有此數而躬行
節儉在下者不思一夫所獲難食十人而
終嵗憂勤則雖造化爲爐萬物爲銅點沙
爲金變礫爲玉亦豈能供無窮之欲哉此
亦管子守財御人以平天下之意也謹對
第五問
陳良材
===
同考試官教諭郭批弭盗江省要務是作區畫
周詳長慮却顧而以覈實之說終之有用之才也
同考試官教諭諸批敷陳時事不激不迂且利
病舉若指掌匪徒空言之施者錄之以采
考試官教諭鄭批通達時宜具見經濟
考試官學正馮批籌畫切中肯綮
執事發策以弭盗之略下詢承學甚盛心
也顧章縫之識未足以達當世之務視之
董賈後矣然承問而不能陳其槩焉恥也
punctuated:
說焉。甞聞國裕則用奢，民富則俗壞，有識之士是以懷卭山之憂、抱近鹽之懼也。使在上者不思天地生財止有此數而躬行節儉，在下者不思一夫所獲難食十人而終嵗憂勤，則雖造化爲爐、萬物爲銅，點沙爲金、變礫爲玉，亦豈能供無窮之欲哉？此亦《管子》守財御人以平天下之意也。謹對。

第五問
陳良材
同考試官教諭郭批：弭盗江省要務，是作區畫周詳，長慮却顧，而以覈實之說終之，有用之才也。
同考試官教諭諸批：敷陳時事，不激不迂，且利病舉若指掌，匪徒空言之施者，錄之以采。
考試官教諭鄭批：通達時宜，具見經濟。
考試官學正馮批：籌畫切中肯綮。

執事發策，以弭盗之略下詢承學，甚盛心也。顧章縫之識，未足以達當世之務，視之董、賈後矣；然承問而不能陳其槩焉，恥也，
translation_en:
… something to add. I have heard that when the state is affluent, expenditure becomes extravagant, and when the people are wealthy, customs deteriorate. That is why men of insight harbor the worry of Mount Qiong and embrace the fear of living near salt marshes. If those above do not reflect on the fact that the wealth produced by Heaven and Earth is limited to a fixed amount and personally practice frugality, and if those below do not reflect on the fact that what one man harvests can hardly feed ten people and remain anxious and diligent throughout the year, then even if the Creator were the furnace and the myriad things were copper, turning sand into gold and transforming gravel into jade, how could it ever supply boundless desires? This too is the meaning in the Book of Master Guan (Guanzi) of guarding wealth and governing the people in order to pacify the world. I respectfully reply.

Fifth Question
Chen Liangcai 陳良cai
Associate Examiner, Instructor Guo 郭 comments: Suppressing banditry is a vital task for Jiangxi Province. This essay lays out plans thoroughly and in detail, looking ahead and considering behind, and concludes with the doctrine of verifying realities—a man of useful talent.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu 諸 comments: He sets forth current affairs without being either extreme or pedantic, and points out advantages and disadvantages as clearly as pointing to his own palm. Not one who merely offers empty words, I record this for adoption.
Examiner, Instructor Zheng 鄭 comments: Thoroughly conversant with what is appropriate to the times, fully demonstrating statesmanship.
Examiner, Director of Studies Feng 馮 comments: His planning hits right on the crucial points.

Your Excellency has issued a policy question, inquiring of us junior scholars below about strategies for suppressing banditry; this is a most magnanimous intention. Yet the knowledge of a scholar in ceremonial dress and cap is insufficient to comprehend the affairs of the present age, falling far behind Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 and Jia Yi 賈誼. Nevertheless, to receive your question and be unable to set forth the general outline of an answer would be a disgrace; …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
敢以計安桑梓者僭言之夫古稱極治莫
過于唐虞而寇賊奸宄之防猶不免焉問
禮之制有司徒以訓五典有司救以誅讓
邪惡矣至野廬司寤之禁不少廢也江右
連吳楚而接閩越天下稱奧區焉
明興以來畫謨建置設險預防如三營之並
建兩鎮之分峙而虔中復設參戎焉將領
非乏也為衛者三為所十一有客兵之召
募有精常之操備兵非益寡也邇來綏輯
===
日加地方敕寧無疇昔桶岡姚源之變閩
廣流突之虞亦旣躋元元于衽席矣而執
事者猶以為慮焉豈非欲警衣袽之戒而
期計安於萬全也耶顧今之為盜者四曰
饑寒曰奸民曰嘯聚曰羈縻饑寒之盜窮
困迫身冀活溝壑甘心於弁髦就戮而莫
之悔也奸民之盜深根蟠結陰為逋藪以
至里閈效尤安其黨而莫之恤也嘯聚之
盜潜匿谿洞流入鄰境防弛則陰肆毒螫
punctuated: 敢以計安桑梓者僭言之。夫古稱極治，莫過于唐、虞，而寇賊奸宄之防猶不免焉。問禮之制，有司徒以訓五典，有司救以誅讓邪惡矣，至野廬、司寤之禁，不少廢也。江右連吳、楚而接閩、越，天下稱奧區焉。明興以來，畫謨建置，設險預防，如三營之並建，兩鎮之分峙，而虔中復設參戎焉，將領非乏也；為衛者三，為所十一，有客兵之召募，有精常之操備，兵非益寡也。邇來綏輯日加，地方敕寧，無疇昔桶岡、姚源之變，閩、廣流突之虞，亦旣躋元元于衽席矣，而執事者猶以為慮焉，豈非欲警衣袽之戒，而期計安於萬全也耶？顧今之為盜者四：曰饑寒，曰奸民，曰嘯聚，曰羈縻。饑寒之盜，窮困迫身，冀活溝壑，甘心於弁髦，就戮而莫之悔也；奸民之盜，深根蟠結，陰為逋藪，以至里閈效尤，安其黨而莫之恤也；嘯聚之盜，潜匿谿洞，流入鄰境，防弛則陰肆毒螫，
translation_en:
I venture to speak presumptuously from the perspective of planning for the security of my native homeland. Now, in antiquity, the era praised as the pinnacle of good governance was none other than that of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], yet even then, precautions against bandits, robbers, and traitorous villains could not be dispensed with. Under the institutions of the Rites of Zhou [? 問禮 for 周禮], there was the Minister of Education (situ) to instruct in the Five Teachings, and the Mediator (sijiu) to reprove and punish the wicked and evil; yet even down to the prohibitions enforced by the Keeper of Country Lodges (yelu) and the Night Watchman (siwu), none were neglected in the slightest. Jiangxi [Jiangyou] links Wu and Chu and borders Min [Fujian] and Yue [Guangdong/Zhejiang], and is known throughout the empire as a deep, strategic interior region. Since the rise of the Ming, plans have been drawn up and institutions established, setting up defenses at strategic points to guard against danger in advance. For instance, the Three Training Divisions were jointly established, the Two Garrisons stand poised separately, and within Qianzhou [Ganzhou] an Assistant Regional Commander (canrong) was additionally installed—so commanders and officers are by no means lacking. There are three Guards (wei) and eleven Battalions (suo), along with recruited guest troops and the regular training of elite and standing forces—so soldiers have by no means grown fewer. Recently, pacification and ordering have increased daily, and the region is tranquil and secure [? 敕寧 for 敕寧/謐寧]; there are no longer the uprisings of Tonggang and Yaoyuan of former days, nor the threat of roving raids from Fujian and Guangdong. This has indeed already raised the common people onto peaceful mats; yet you, sir, still regard it as a matter of concern. Is it not because you wish to heed the warning from the Classic of Changes about "having rags ready to caulk leaks," and hope to plan for security with complete perfection?

However, among those who become bandits today, there are four kinds: those driven by hunger and cold, those who are villainous commoners, those who band together at a whistle, and those held under loose rein (jimi). Bandits driven by hunger and cold are pressed by extreme destitution; hoping to survive the ditches and ravines, they willingly cast off the laws like a useless cap and go to their execution without regret. Bandits who are villainous commoners have deep roots intertwined together, secretly serving as dens for fugitives, to the point where their village neighbors imitate their bad example, comfortably sheltering their faction without any compunction. Bandits who band together at a whistle hide secretly in mountain streams and caverns and flow across into neighboring jurisdictions; when defenses relax, they secretly unleash their poisonous stings, …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
勢迫則蛇伏鼠竄也羈縻之盜始雖盤據
巢穴繼則俛首聽命而向背之機又視我
所以御之何如也而今所掃除綏懷不過
此數耳何也寧新接壤楚之瀏陽平江重
巖複嶺深箐密林延袤三百餘里揭竿之
徒向嘯聚焉如華林始禍已明鑑矣邇畫
策掃蕩殲其渠醜議分憲臣以彈壓之又
增兵立營宜林莽之間一清矣而窺伺者
復竊發焉迨旬日始平其故何哉蓋山谷
===
之民多為盜藪非一窮治之能令其不萌
蘖耶黃鄉連跨粵之平遠龍川層巒疊峯
巢洞險阻離邑三百餘里負固之徒每怙
終焉如葉酋梗化已見汧矣邇密計誅戮
收其餘黨
請設縣治以控御之仍區畫疆界宜新附之衆
帖服矣而奸宄者復攜貳焉至撫之後定
其故何哉蓋頑悍之民陽示效順非一孚
結之能保其無生心乎鄱湖環遶豫章三
punctuated: 勢迫則蛇伏鼠竄也。羈縻之盜，始雖盤據巢穴，繼則俛首聽命，而向背之機，又視我所以御之何如也。而今所掃除綏懷，不過此數耳。何也？寧、新接壤楚之瀏陽、平江，重巖複嶺，深箐密林，延袤三百餘里，揭竿之徒，向嘯聚焉，如華林始禍，已明鑑矣。邇畫策掃蕩，殲其渠醜，議分憲臣以彈壓之，又增兵立營，宜林莽之間一清矣；而窺伺者復竊發焉，迨旬日始平，其故何哉？蓋山谷之民，多為盜藪，非一窮治之，能令其不萌蘖耶？黃鄉連跨粵之平遠、龍川，層巒疊峯，巢洞險阻，離邑三百餘里，負固之徒，每怙終焉，如葉酋梗化，已見汧矣。邇密計誅戮，收其餘黨，請設縣治以控御之，仍區畫疆界，宜新附之衆帖服矣；而奸宄者復攜貳焉，至撫之後定，其故何哉？蓋頑悍之民，陽示效順，非一孚結之，能保其無生心乎？鄱湖環遶豫章三
translation_en:
… and when pressed by circumstances, they lie low like snakes and scurry away like rats. As for bandits held under loose rein, although at first they entrench themselves in their lairs, subsequently they bow their heads and obey commands; yet the pivot of their allegiance or rebellion again depends on how we manage them. And those whom we presently sweep away or pacify are nothing more than these few sorts. Why is this?

Ningzhou 寧州 and Xinchang 新昌 border Liuyang 瀏陽 and Pingjiang 平江 in Huguang 楚, where layered crags and doubled ridges, deep bamboo groves and dense forests stretch for more than three hundred li. Those who raise bamboo poles in revolt have in the past gathered there with whistling calls; how the disaster at Hualin 華林 began is already a clear mirror for us. Recently, plans were laid to sweep them out and annihilate their ugly chieftains; it was proposed to detail a Surveillance Official to suppress them, and troops were also increased and camps established, so the forested wilds ought to have been completely cleared. Yet those watching for an opportunity again secretly broke out, and it took ten days before they were pacified. What is the reason for this? It is because the people of the mountain valleys mostly serve as dens for bandits; without investigating and dealing with them thoroughly, can one keep them from sprouting anew?

Huangxiang 黃鄉 spans across Pingyuan 平遠 and Longchuan 龍川 in Guangdong 粵, with tiered peaks and overlapping summits, where lairs and caves are precipitous and remote, more than three hundred li from the county seat. Those who rely on natural fastnesses constantly persist in their wrongdoing to the end; how the chieftain Ye 葉 obstructed transformation has already been seen in the past [?]. Recently, secret plans were made to execute them and take in their remaining followers; permission was requested to establish a county seat to control them, and boundaries were further demarcated, so the newly submitted multitudes ought to have been docile and submissive. Yet villains and traitors again grew disaffected, and only after they were pacified did things settle down. What is the reason for this? It is because stubborn and fierce people outwardly make a show of obedience; without thoroughly winning their trust and binding them to us, can one guarantee that they will not harbor rebellious intentions?

Poyang Lake 鄱湖 encircles three prefectures of Yuzhang 豫章…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
郡洪濤無際矣爲潢池弄兵者虞也設備
於康山焉協以巡司邏以戎卒邇復增兵
議艘而覈之郡倅制至備也而所以洗其
湖中之穢者毋亦積窩之是求乎九江控
扼江藩門户上游稱雄矣爲萑苻不逞者
防也設備於彭蠡焉險要隸分哨守聯絡
邇復置卒增餉而統之於江防守加密也
而所以清其江上之氛者毋亦詰察之是
嚴乎愚以寧新之寇如虺蛇之在山林不
===
急以驅之則有噬螫之凶故必燻灼之剪
除之不使復入於窟穴也而猶未也爲之
搜藏匿之奸俾奔突者無所容爲之重購
賞之令俾獻功者許其黨爲之開自新之
路使脅從者不加誅如是則山谷以寧也
矧敢自蹙於網羅哉黃鄉之黨如鹿豕之
在圈檻不寬以處之則有奔逸之患故必
馴習之飽飼之使常狎人而依附也而猶
未也緩其租稅而不使之困焉聯以信義
punctuated: 郡，洪濤無際矣，爲潢池弄兵者虞也。設備於康山焉，協以巡司，邏以戎卒，邇復增兵議艘，而覈之郡倅，制至備也；而所以洗其湖中之穢者，毋亦積窩之是求乎？九江控扼江藩門户，上游稱雄矣，爲萑苻不逞者防也。設備於彭蠡焉，險要隸分，哨守聯絡，邇復置卒增餉，而統之於江防，守加密也；而所以清其江上之氛者，毋亦詰察之是嚴乎？愚以寧、新之寇，如虺蛇之在山林，不急以驅之，則有噬螫之凶，故必燻灼之、剪除之，不使復入於窟穴也。而猶未也，爲之搜藏匿之奸，俾奔突者無所容；爲之重購賞之令，俾獻功者許其黨；爲之開自新之路，使脅從者不加誅。如是，則山谷以寧也，矧敢自蹙於網羅哉？黃鄉之黨，如鹿豕之在圈檻，不寬以處之，則有奔逸之患，故必馴習之、飽飼之，使常狎人而依附也。而猶未也，緩其租稅而不使之困焉，聯以信義
translation_en:
…prefectures, its vast waves are boundless, which creates a source of worry regarding those who would play with weapons in the marshes. Defenses have been established at Kangshan, assisted by Police Offices and patrolled by military soldiers; recently, troops were further increased and vessels deliberated upon, all verified and supervised by the Assistant Prefect—the institutional arrangements are thorough indeed. Yet as for the means to wash away the filth within the lake, should we not seek out the long-standing harborers of brigands? Jiujiang controls and commands the gateway to the Jiangxi region, renowned as a strategic stronghold on the upper reaches; defenses are maintained there against lawless bandits in the reed marshes. Preparations have been set up at Pengli, with strategic points assigned to separate jurisdictions and patrols linked in coordination; recently, soldiers were further stationed and rations increased, all placed under the unified command of the River Defense, making the guard ever more tight. Yet as for the means to clear away the miasma upon the river, should we not strictly enforce interrogation and inspection?

In my humble view, the bandits of Ningzhou and Xinchang are like vipers and serpents in the mountain forests: if one does not urgently drive them out, there will be the danger of their biting and stinging. Therefore, one must smoke and burn them out, and clip and eradicate them, so as not to let them re-enter their dens and lairs. And even that is not all: for their sake, search out the villains who harbor and hide them, so that those who flee headlong have nowhere to be sheltered; issue orders for heavy rewards and bounties, so that those who offer meritorious service are permitted to turn in their accomplices; and open a path for self-renewal, so that those who followed under coercion are spared punishment. If this is done, the mountains and valleys will be tranquil—how much less would they dare throw themselves into our nets and snares? The partisans of Huangxiang are like deer and swine in pens and cages: if one does not treat them with leniency, there will be the trouble of their bolting and escaping. Therefore, one must tame and accustom them, and feed them to fullness, so that they constantly grow familiar with people and remain attached. And even that is not all: relax their taxes and levies so as not to drive them into distress, bind them with good faith and righteousness…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
而不使之携焉導之知方使悉心嚮化焉
如是雖異類可格也其有不樂爲赤子乎
鄱湖之寇雜艇商舟其形難窺也乗可掠
之機則如鳥飛飇舉忽在左右矣兹欲廣
爲緝捕之方非計也蓋濱湖豪猾隂爲窩
户以誘奸慝無爲盜之形而享爲盜之利
誠詰而罪之以絶其根而黨與其解散矣
九江之寇多出上流其跡難測也因乎迅
濤之下則如飄風馳駛倏入江關矣兹欲
===
多爲捉影之略非算也蓋洞庭巨寇剽掠
既畢多易舟楫外假商賈之名以愚哨邏
之卒謀而擒之以遏其來而江漢其澄清
矣然是四者皆自今日之所急者陳之也
而經久之計則尚有可言焉夫天下之勢
必如血脉之周流而後可以無壅閼守封
疆者必緩急同患焉而後可以相保今甸
服幸賴寧謐間有不逞者不過一二無聊
輩矣非有負嵎莫櫻勢也列壤者誠共驅
punctuated: 而不使之携焉，導之知方，使悉心嚮化焉。如是，雖異類可格也，其有不樂爲赤子乎？鄱湖之寇，雜艇商舟，其形難窺也；乗可掠之機，則如鳥飛飇舉，忽在左右矣。兹欲廣爲緝捕之方，非計也。蓋濱湖豪猾，隂爲窩户，以誘奸慝，無爲盜之形，而享爲盜之利。誠詰而罪之，以絶其根，而黨與其解散矣。九江之寇，多出上流，其跡難測也；因乎迅濤之下，則如飄風馳駛，倏入江關矣。兹欲多爲捉影之略，非算也。蓋洞庭巨寇，剽掠既畢，多易舟楫，外假商賈之名，以愚哨邏之卒。謀而擒之，以遏其來，而江漢其澄清矣。然是四者，皆自今日之所急者陳之也，而經久之計則尚有可言焉。夫天下之勢，必如血脉之周流，而後可以無壅閼；守封疆者，必緩急同患焉，而後可以相保。今甸服幸賴寧謐，間有不逞者，不過一二無聊輩矣，非有負嵎莫櫻勢也。列壤者誠共驅…
translation_en:
…so as not to let them become alienated, and guide them to know righteous principles so that they wholeheartedly turn toward civilization. If this is done, even those of a different kind can be won over—how could they not rejoice in being the Emperor's infant children?

As for the bandits of Poyang Lake (Pohu 鄱湖), they mingle their skiffs among merchant vessels, making their forms difficult to detect; when they seize an opportunity to plunder, they rise like flying birds or a sudden gale, appearing instantly on all sides. Now, to broadly deploy methods of pursuit and arrest is not a sound plan. For powerful and cunning locals along the lakeshore secretly act as harboring households to lure in wicked elements; they bear no outward appearance of being bandits, yet they enjoy the profits of banditry. If we truly investigate and punish them so as to cut off the root, their confederates will surely disperse.

As for the bandits of Jiujiang 九江, they mostly emerge from the upper reaches of the river, making their tracks difficult to fathom; riding down upon the swift currents, they race like a whirlwind and dart suddenly into the river passes. Now, to multiply schemes that merely chase after shadows is not a sound calculation. For once the great bandits of Dongting 洞庭 have finished plundering, they mostly change their boats and outwardly borrow the name of merchants to deceive the patrolling soldiers. If we lay plans to capture them so as to block their coming, the Yangtze and Han (Jiang Han 江漢) region will surely be made clear and tranquil.

Yet these four matters are all set forth with respect to what is urgent today, whereas concerning a long-term plan there is still more that can be said. Now, the condition of the realm must be like the circulation of blood and pulse throughout the body before it can be free of blockage and obstruction; those who guard the frontiers and territories must share one another's distress in times of urgency before they can mutually preserve one another. Today, the royal domain is fortunately peaceful and tranquil; if occasionally there are unruly elements, they are no more than one or two desperate fellows, not possessing the posture of a tiger backed against a mountain crag that none dare confront. If those who govern adjacent territories truly join together to drive them…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
之不終朝可撲滅矣乃勢分秦越苟幸寇
之不入吾界斯已矣幸鄰壤者足以當之
可矣而不知萬一潰流其境是自撤其藩
籬而示以可乘之隙也愚以為此當今之
通弊也則鄰封一體之義其可岐乎昔李
崇之守兗州也村置樓鼓互為捄援竇儼
之立義營也令村自相保盜無所入此保
甲意也今之保甲要皆飾文具而無其實
耳誠使聯比其居什伍其人責之相防相
===
保則守望相助者倣於古而盜自息矣保
甲之所當申飭者此其一也李抱真之守
懷州也徧籍人戶而簡教之歲終大校以
示賞責故兵為諸道最今江右衞所之卒
疲弱大半所恃者客兵土著耳然客兵雖
募徒備一時而精常乏兵非素練者固有
聞鼙鼓而心悸見旌旗而目眩者矣愚以
為當無事之時誠稽其役占嚴其挑選簡
壯勇者而練習之擇知兵以為之長如古
punctuated: 之，不終朝可撲滅矣。乃勢分秦越，苟幸寇之不入吾界斯已矣，幸鄰壤者足以當之可矣。而不知萬一潰流其境，是自撤其藩籬，而示以可乘之隙也。愚以為此當今之通弊也，則鄰封一體之義，其可岐乎？昔李崇之守兗州也，村置樓鼓，互為捄援；竇儼之立義營也，令村自相保，盜無所入。此保甲意也。今之保甲，要皆飾文具而無其實耳。誠使聯比其居，什伍其人，責之相防相保，則守望相助者倣於古，而盜自息矣。保甲之所當申飭者，此其一也。李抱真之守懷州也，徧籍人戶而簡教之，歲終大校以示賞責，故兵為諸道最。今江右衞所之卒，疲弱大半，所恃者客兵、土著耳。然客兵雖募，徒備一時，而精常乏。兵非素練者，固有聞鼙鼓而心悸，見旌旗而目眩者矣。愚以為當無事之時，誠稽其役占，嚴其挑選，簡壯勇者而練習之，擇知兵以為之長，如古
translation_en: … them out, they could be extinguished before a single morning is out. Yet nowadays authorities treat one another with the indifference of Qin and Yue: they are content merely to consider themselves fortunate if bandits do not enter their own borders, and fortunate if neighboring jurisdictions are able to withstand them. They do not realize that if by any chance the bandits break through and spill over into those territories, they are in effect tearing down their own protective fences and exposing a vulnerability that can be exploited. I believe this is a universal failing of the present day; how, then, can the principle that neighboring jurisdictions form a single body be divided? In the past, when Li Chong 李崇 governed Yanzhou 兗州, he set up watchtowers and drums in every village for mutual rescue and aid; when Dou Yan 竇儼 established righteous camps (yiying 義營), he ordered villages to guarantee one another's security, leaving bandits nowhere to enter. This is the very spirit of the mutual-security system (baojia 保甲). The mutual-security system of today, in essence, merely dresses up bureaucratic formalities without any real substance. If we truly link households together in close association, organize the people into squads of five and ten, and hold them responsible for mutual defense and mutual guarantee, then mutual aid in keeping watch will follow the ancient model, and banditry will subside of its own accord. That the mutual-security system ought to be strictly reinforced is one point. When Li Baozhen 李抱真 governed Huaizhou 懷州, he registered all households and selected men for training, holding a grand review at the end of the year to dispense rewards and punishments; thus his troops were the finest among all circuits (dao 道). Today, more than half the soldiers in the Guards and Battalions (weisuo 衞所) of Jiangxi (Jiangyou 江右) are exhausted and weak, and what we rely upon are merely guest troops and local militia. Yet although guest troops are recruited, they merely serve as a stopgap for the moment and often lack elite vigor. Among troops who are not regularly trained, there are naturally those whose hearts palpitate at the sound of war drums and whose eyes grow dizzy at the sight of banners and flags. I believe that in times of peace, if we truly audit their improper diversion to private labor, strictly enforce their selection, choose the strong and brave to drill and train them, and select men well-versed in military affairs to serve as their commanders—following the ancient…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
所謂以一教十以十教百以百教千之說
行之則平時有投石超距之勇而臨敵自
收搴旗斬馘之勛矣而練兵之所當行者
此其一也今之將領固皆禦侮計也然無
事則相率以逍遙寇至則虛張以恐喝少
有得則冒功以邀賞其積習使然也於封
疆何賴焉愚以爲執綏在於奮勇而致勇
莫先於倡誠使慎恩威明賞罰謹號令責
功實嚴之紀律以示其法齊之禮義以示
===
其軌而兵識將意將知士情雖以摧勍敵
如狄青之崑崙岳飛之洞庭者可踵也而
將領之當重非其一乎昔歐陽脩言禦盜
四事而歸於用良吏以撫疲民則守令者
其本也誠使今之守令懼民之未樂生也
則奠其居豐其產寬其力而貽之逸薄其
征而俾之富以赤子視之而治其心焉懼
民之有邪心也則陶其性遏其淫事至而
爲之備患生而爲之防以一體懷之而淑
punctuated: 所謂「以一教十，以十教百，以百教千」之說行之，則平時有投石超距之勇，而臨敵自收搴旗斬馘之勛矣。而練兵之所當行者，此其一也。今之將領，固皆禦侮計也。然無事則相率以逍遙，寇至則虛張以恐喝，少有得則冒功以邀賞，其積習使然也，於封疆何賴焉？愚以爲執綏在於奮勇，而致勇莫先於倡。誠使慎恩威、明賞罰、謹號令、責功實，嚴之紀律以示其法，齊之禮義以示其軌，而兵識將意，將知士情，雖以摧勍敵如狄青之崑崙、岳飛之洞庭者，可踵也。而將領之當重，非其一乎？昔歐陽脩言禦盜四事，而歸於用良吏以撫疲民，則守令者，其本也。誠使今之守令，懼民之未樂生也，則奠其居、豐其產，寬其力而貽之逸，薄其征而俾之富，以赤子視之，而治其心焉；懼民之有邪心也，則陶其性、遏其淫，事至而爲之備，患生而爲之防，以一體懷之，而淑
translation_en:
…put into practice the ancient saying of “using one to teach ten, ten to teach a hundred, and a hundred to teach a thousand,” then in peacetime they will possess the bravery to hurl stones and leap over obstacles, and when facing the enemy they will naturally reap the merit of capturing standards and severing heads. This is one imperative that ought to be carried out in training troops.

Today’s commanders and officers are indeed all appointed as a measure to fend off aggression. Yet when there is no trouble, they follow one another in leisurely idleness; when bandits arrive, they make blustering displays of intimidation; and when they achieve a slight gain, they falsely claim merit to seek rewards. Their entrenched habits make them so—what reliance can the borderlands place in them? In my humble opinion, holding the mounting-strap of command lies in rousing bravery, and in inducing bravery nothing comes before leading by example. If indeed they are prudent with grace and authority, clear in rewards and punishments, careful with commands and orders, and demanding of substantive achievement—enforcing strict discipline to show them the law, and ordering them with ritual and righteousness to show them the proper path—so that the soldiers understand the commander’s intent and the commander knows the troops’ feelings, then even crushing formidable enemies like Di Qing 狄青 at Kunlun Pass or Yue Fei 岳飛 at Dongting Lake can be emulated. Is not the importance that ought to be placed on commanders and officers another such imperative?

In the past, Ouyang Xiu 歐陽脩 spoke of four matters for defending against bandits, and concluded by returning to the employment of good officials to soothe the exhausted people; thus, Prefects and Magistrates are the root of the matter. If indeed today’s Prefects and Magistrates, fearing that the people do not yet rejoice in their livelihoods, settle their dwellings, enrich their property, spare their labor to leave them in ease, and lighten their exactions to make them prosperous—regarding them as newborn infants and thereby governing their hearts; and fearing that the people harbor perverse inclinations, mold their natures, curb their excesses, make preparations when affairs arise, and set up defenses when troubles emerge—cherishing them as one body and thereby making virtuous…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
其行焉其困於饑寒而羣然以逞者則戢
而安之如龔遂之治渤海賈琮之刺交州
者矣其有終難化服而毋使滋蔓也則陰
以圖之如虞詡之三科以募張綱之單騎
詣壘者矣又必假之以事權而毋繩以文
墨需之以歲月而勿急其近功則理繩之
化可弘烹鮮之治不擾循良著而民生阜
矣盜何自而起哉雖然所以核將領而察
守令者又豈無其道乎今之分藩者非不
===
有守臣乎握符者非不有憲臣乎所以協
叅驗之法而司振勵之權也誠於將領之
勇略者觀望者虛張首功者摧鋒敵愾者
稽其功罪不以訾譽眩於守令之悃愊者
夸毗者治行異等者功善無聞者第其上
下不以愛憎奪而又精其鑑于臺臣總其
綱于撫臣而
照臨之于
朝廷則紀綱齊一法度精明如絲之有緒而
punctuated: 其行焉。其困於饑寒而羣然以逞者，則戢而安之，如龔遂之治渤海、賈琮之刺交州者矣；其有終難化服而毋使滋蔓也，則陰以圖之，如虞詡之三科以募、張綱之單騎詣壘者矣。又必假之以事權而毋繩以文墨，需之以歲月而勿急其近功，則理繩之化可弘，烹鮮之治不擾，循良著而民生阜矣，盜何自而起哉？雖然，所以核將領而察守令者，又豈無其道乎？今之分藩者，非不有守臣乎？握符者，非不有憲臣乎？所以協叅驗之法而司振勵之權也。誠於將領之勇略者、觀望者、虛張首功者、摧鋒敵愾者，稽其功罪，不以訾譽眩；於守令之悃愊者、夸毗者、治行異等者、功善無聞者，第其上下，不以愛憎奪。而又精其鑑于臺臣，總其綱于撫臣，而照臨之于朝廷，則紀綱齊一，法度精明，如絲之有緒而
translation_en:
…their conduct. As for those who, distressed by hunger and cold, band together to work their will, they will pacify and settle them, just as Gong Sui 龔遂 governed Bohai 渤海 and Jia Cong 賈琮 served as Regional Inspector of Jiaozhou 交州. As for those who ultimately prove impossible to transform and submit, so as not to let them spread, they will secretly devise ways to deal with them, just as Yu Xu 虞詡 recruited men of three categories and Zhang Gang 張綱 rode alone to the rebels' ramparts. Furthermore, one must grant them discretionary authority and not bind them with bureaucratic red tape, allow them months and years and not press them for immediate results. Then the transformation of untangling knots can be broadened, the governance of cooking a small fish without over-stirring will remain unperturbed, upright and benevolent officials will become manifest, and the people's livelihood will be abundant. From where, then, could banditry arise?

Even so, how could there be no proper way to evaluate commanders and scrutinize prefects and magistrates? Among those who today share the provincial administration, are there not Circuit Administration Officials? Among those who hold tallies of authority, are there not Surveillance Officials? They are the ones who harmonize the methods of cross-examination and verification, and who wield the power to rouse and encourage. Truly, with regard to commanders—whether they are brave and strategic, hesitant and watchful, falsely inflating their tallies of enemy heads, or breaking the enemy's vanguard in shared hatred of the foe—one should examine their merits and offenses without being confused by slander or praise. And with regard to prefects and magistrates—whether they are sincere and unpretentious, sycophantic and obsequious, of exceptional administrative performance, or unheard of in merit and goodness—one should rank them high or low without being swayed by personal fondness or animosity. Moreover, let the Censorate officials sharpen their discernment, let the Grand Coordinator gather the overarching control, and let the Imperial Court shine its supervision from above; then discipline and order will be uniform, laws and regulations will be clear and precise, like silk threads having their lead end and…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
不棼如網之有綱而不紊蕩平之風在是
矣方今北虜款邊南服安堵有櫜弓臥鼓
之安無揭竿持籌之警康衢擊壤愚生何
幸躬逢之測蠡之見惓惓爲江右計治安
亦希賈誼積薪喻也敢述所聞以復明問
執事者其可否焉
punctuated: 不棼，如網之有綱而不紊，蕩平之風在是矣。方今北虜款邊，南服安堵，有櫜弓臥鼓之安，無揭竿持籌之警。康衢擊壤，愚生何幸躬逢之！測蠡之見，惓惓爲江右計治安，亦希賈誼積薪喻也。敢述所聞以復明問，執事者其可否焉。
translation_en: … become tangled, and like a net that has a headrope and does not fall into disorder. The ethos of great peace and order lies right here. At present, the northern caitiffs have submitted at the frontiers and the southern regions are secure inside their walls; there is the peace of cased bows and resting war-drums, without the alarms of rebels raising bamboo poles or planners reckoning military tallies. Beating the earth on the grand thoroughfares in celebration of peace—how fortunate is this ignorant student to witness it in person! With a shallow view like measuring the sea with a calabash, I am earnestly concerned with planning for the public order and security of Jiangxi (Jiangyou), hoping also to emulate Jia Yi's metaphor of piling up firewood. I venture to recount what I have heard in reply to your illustrious question; may the examiners judge its merits.

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
萬曆四年丙子例大比士巡
按江西御史張簡實監臨之
日皇皇焉以弗克仰塞
上意是懼稽覈
典制申飭諸司及爾多士視昔
益虔毖焉旣竣事卿獲藉諸
===
大夫以免於蔽賢之罪宜序
諸末簡於是進諸士告之曰
是舉也我
皇上籲俊第二科也諸所舉皆長
育膠庠亦知江右所以稱盛
於海內乎夫人才關氣運鍾
地靈而振作則係于敎化我
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序
萬曆四年丙子，例大比士。巡按江西御史張簡實監臨之，日皇皇焉以弗克仰塞上意是懼，稽覈典制，申飭諸司及爾多士，視昔益虔毖焉。旣竣事，卿獲藉諸大夫以免於蔽賢之罪，宜序諸末簡。於是進諸士告之曰：是舉也，我皇上籲俊第二科也。諸所舉皆長育膠庠，亦知江右所以稱盛於海內乎？夫人才關氣運，鍾地靈，而振作則係于敎化。我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination
In the fourth year of the Wanli reign, bingzi (1576), by precedent the great triennial recruitment of scholars was held. Regional Inspector (xun'an yushi) of Jiangxi Zhang Jian 張簡 actually served as Supervising Official for it. Day by day he was filled with anxious concern lest he prove unable to look up and fulfill His Majesty's intentions; he examined and verified the statutory regulations, and issued strict admonitions to the various officials and to you assembled scholars, with even greater reverence and caution than in the past. Once the affair was concluded, I [Qing 卿, reading for Jian 簡?] was able to rely on the various grandees to escape the offense of obscuring worthy men, and it is fitting that I should write a postface at the end of the bamboo slips. Thereupon I brought forward the scholars and addressed them, saying: "This recruitment is the second examination calling forth men of eminence under our August Emperor. All those who have been selected were raised and nurtured in the local schools; do you also know why Jiangxi (Jiangyou) is acclaimed as flourishing throughout the realm? Now, human talent is bound up with the cycle of cosmic vitality and concentrates the numinous energy of the land, yet its rousing and stimulation depend upon transformative education. When our…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
高皇帝混一區夏首平偽漢
如隆興路時庶務未暇
謁孔子廟使士生於其間者相與
明帝王聖賢之道淑諸身心
以俟用肆肇設賢科而進士
第一人首出茲土夫固有以
發其祥矣我
===
成祖入正大統選文學臣七人直
內閣叅
機務其出茲土者又五人歷永
樂宣德間應鄉薦者至二百
餘人由此取進士幾半天下
迨景泰丙子裁解額定江西
九十五名甲他省如羅倫謝
punctuated: 高皇帝混一區夏，首平偽漢，如隆興路時，庶務未暇，謁孔子廟，使士生於其間者相與明帝王聖賢之道，淑諸身心以俟用。肆肇設賢科，而進士第一人首出茲土，夫固有以發其祥矣。我成祖入正大統，選文學臣七人直內閣、叅機務，其出茲土者又五人。歷永樂、宣德間，應鄉薦者至二百餘人，由此取進士幾半天下。迨景泰丙子，裁解額，定江西九十五名，甲他省，如羅倫、謝
translation_en: … High Emperor [Taizu] unified the Chinese realm, he first pacified the spurious Han regime. When he went to Longxing Route, before he even had leisure for the myriad affairs of state, he visited the Temple of Confucius, causing the scholars born in this region to join together in illuminating the Way of the sage-kings and worthies, cultivating it in their persons and minds while awaiting employment. Thus, when the recruitment examinations for the worthy were first established, the very first top-ranked metropolitan graduate (jinshi) came from this land; truly there was already something that initiated its auspicious flourishing! When our Emperor Chengzu [the Yongle Emperor] entered to rectify the Great Succession, he selected seven literary officials to serve on duty in the Grand Secretariat and participate in confidential state affairs, and five of them again came from this land. Through the Yongle (1403–1424) and Xuande (1426–1435) reigns, those recommended through the Provincial Examination reached more than two hundred men, and those who thereby obtained the metropolitan graduate degree made up nearly half the realm. By the bingzi year of the Jingtai reign (1456), when provincial quotas were reduced and fixed, Jiangxi was set at ninety-five men, ranking first among all the other provinces. Men such as Luo Lun 羅倫 and Xie …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
一夔俱由是科奉
制對相繼
擢冠多士嗣
列聖敎化漸濡旣博且厚以科目
進者鉅儒名臣後先相望不
徒隨時就功名而已今
聖天子握
===
乾符踐
紫極
講學
勤政無間寒暑孳孳以進賢興
理爲急
光紹
二祖鴻業卽遐方殊族尚靡然嚮
punctuated: 一夔，俱由是科奉制對，相繼擢冠多士。嗣列聖敎化漸濡，旣博且厚，以科目進者，鉅儒名臣後先相望，不徒隨時就功名而已。今聖天子握乾符，踐紫極，講學勤政，無間寒暑，孳孳以進賢興理爲急，光紹二祖鴻業，卽遐方殊族尚靡然嚮
translation_en: … [Xie] Yikui 謝一夔 both passed this examination to present their palace examination replies to the Emperor's decree, and in succession were selected as the very first among the multitude of scholars. Thereafter, as the moral transformation of the successive Sacred Emperors gradually imbued the realm, becoming both broad and deep, great Confucians and renowned ministers who advanced through the examination system followed closely upon one another in unbroken succession, not merely accommodating the times to achieve personal功名 (merit and fame). Now, our Sacred Son of Heaven holds the talisman of Heaven and ascends the Purple Throne; he expounds upon learning and labours diligently at governance without pause through winter and summer, tirelessly making the advancement of the worthy and the promotion of order his urgent priority. Gloriously continuing the grand enterprise of the Two Ancestors [Taizu and Chengzu], even distant regions and foreign peoples are swept along in admiration of…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
風矧兹土素稱多賢涵濡
大化而有得者乎卿嘗傾注之思
欲一挹其餘芳而不可得乃
今應御史聘而來竊縱觀山
水之秀麗又幸而獲從事校
諸生業見其闡明義旨根極
理要于古今治亂之迹邪正
===
是非之辯利害休戚之故決
策懇晢咸彬彬哉文質不悖
於道若陟匡廬而窮其巔凌
彭蠡而遡其源庶幾哉無忝
文獻之稱不足以應
明詔矣乎雖然是曷敢知卿等選
才
punctuated: 風，矧兹土素稱多賢，涵濡大化而有得者乎？卿嘗傾注之，思欲一挹其餘芳而不可得。乃今應御史聘而來，竊縱觀山水之秀麗，又幸而獲從事校諸生業，見其闡明義旨，根極理要，于古今治亂之迹、邪正是非之辯、利害休戚之故，決策懇晢，咸彬彬哉，文質不悖於道。若陟匡廬而窮其巔，凌彭蠡而遡其源，庶幾哉無忝文獻之稱，不足以應明詔矣乎？雖然，是曷敢知？卿等選才
translation_en: …to his transforming influence, how much more so in this land, which has long been renowned for its abundance of worthies, who have been steeped in the Great Transformation and have attained true understanding? I [Qing] once directed my admiring thoughts toward it, longing to draw even once upon its lingering fragrance, yet could not do so. Now, having come in response to the Censor's invitation, I have privately gazed at length upon the beauty of its mountains and waters, and have moreover had the good fortune to take part in evaluating the examination papers of the students. I saw how they elucidated the meanings and principles, probing to the very root of essential truths; and how, regarding the traces of order and disorder in antiquity and the present, the distinctions between heterodoxy and orthodoxy, right and wrong, and the causes of benefit and harm, joy and sorrow, their policy essays were earnest and clear—all so refined and accomplished, their form and substance alike in harmony with the Way! It was like ascending Mount Kuanglu (Mount Lu) to reach its highest peak, or crossing Lake Pengli (Poyang Lake) to trace its source. Coming so close to perfection, they bring no shame to the land's reputation for letters and learning—are they not worthy to answer the illustrious imperial decree? Even so, how could we presume to know this for certain? In selecting talent for…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
盛世惟言是徵將以措之行也諸
生以言爲贄將以成其信也
故求玉于崑岡不乏瓌寶則
崑岡增重求驥于冀野不乏
逸足則冀野增重江右爲東
南奧區今之崑岡冀野也
上固以連城千里求諸生脫不副
===
其所舉其自待之謂何即無
論先哲安
社稷覆生民赫然在人耳目者若
倫在翰院疏正綱常天下之
士聞之爭自刮磨舊習爲之
一變陳獻章以青天白日稱
之是爲前丙子榜重而
punctuated: 盛世惟言是徵，將以措之行也；諸生以言爲贄，將以成其信也。故求玉于崑岡，不乏瓌寶，則崑岡增重；求驥于冀野，不乏逸足，則冀野增重。江右爲東南奧區，今之崑岡、冀野也。上固以連城、千里求諸生，脫不副其所舉，其自待之謂何？即無論先哲安社稷、覆生民，赫然在人耳目者，若倫在翰院，疏正綱常，天下之士聞之，爭自刮磨，舊習爲之一變，陳獻章以「青天白日」稱之，是爲前丙子榜重，而
translation_en: … in a flourishing age is verified only through words, with the intention of putting them into action; the candidates present their words as a pledge, with the intention of fulfilling their trustworthiness. Therefore, when one seeks jade on Mount Kun and there is no lack of extraordinary treasures, Mount Kun gains in esteem; when one seeks fine steeds in the wilds of Ji and there is no lack of fleet-footed horses, the wilds of Ji gain in esteem. Jiangxi is a rich heartland of the southeast—the Mount Kun and the wilds of Ji of today. His Majesty indeed seeks among the candidates those worth a string of cities or capable of running a thousand li; if by chance they do not live up to their selection, what would that say of the expectations they hold for themselves? Even leaving aside the former worthies who brought peace to the altars of state and sheltered the common people, whose achievements stand illustriously before people's eyes and ears—take Someone Like Luo Lun 羅倫 [Lun 倫], who while in the Hanlin Academy submitted a memorial to rectify the cardinal principles of human relations. When scholars across the realm heard of it, they vied to polish and refine themselves, and old habits were transformed at a stroke. Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章 praised him as "the blue sky and bright sun." This added weight to the previous bingzi (1456) examination list, and …

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
昭代增額至意亦不負矣方諸生
跧伏草野孰不扼腕高談慷
慨自許以行誼爲知檢以勳
庸爲易策以仁義道德爲體
要與今之贄言無異忍居倫
輩下乎記有之五人曰茂十
人曰選百人曰俊千人曰英
===
倍英曰賢萬人曰傑萬傑曰
聖今九十五人者拔自數千
人中行且偕計吏上公車駸
駸乎嚮用有階感
殊遇思奮不自今日始耶昔周成
王緝熈聖學而藹藹吉士思
媚天子詩人取喻于梧桐鳳
punctuated: 昭代增額至意亦不負矣。方諸生跧伏草野，孰不扼腕高談，慷慨自許，以行誼爲知檢，以勳庸爲易策，以仁義道德爲體要，與今之贄言無異，忍居倫輩下乎？《記》有之：「五人曰茂，十人曰選，百人曰俊，千人曰英，倍英曰賢，萬人曰傑，萬傑曰聖。」今九十五人者，拔自數千人中，行且偕計吏上公車，駸駸乎嚮用有階。感殊遇思奮，不自今日始耶？昔周成王緝熈聖學，而藹藹吉士，思媚天子，詩人取喻于梧桐鳳
translation_en:
… the profound intention of our Illustrious Dynasty in increasing the quota was likewise not betrayed. When the students were still huddled in obscurity in the countryside, who among them did not clasp his wrist in high-minded discourse and passionately pledge himself, taking moral conduct and righteousness as knowing how to exercise self-restraint, taking meritorious achievements as easy to plan, and taking benevolence, righteousness, the Way, and virtue as the essential substance—no different from the words they have presented today as their pledge—so how could they bear to rank below Lun [Luo Lun 羅倫] and his peers?

It is found in the Record (Baihutong 白虎通): "One who surpasses five men is called 'flourishing' (mao); ten men, 'selected' (xuan); a hundred men, 'outstanding' (jun); a thousand men, 'preeminent' (ying); twice a preeminent man, 'worthy' (xian); ten thousand men, 'heroic' (jie); and ten thousand heroic men, 'sage' (sheng)." Now these ninety-five men have been selected from among several thousand; soon they will accompany the fiscal attendants and board the official carriages to the capital, galloping steadily onward with a stepping-stone toward employment. Moved by this extraordinary favor and resolving to rouse themselves—does this not begin today?

In antiquity, King Cheng of Zhou (Zhou Chengwang 周成王) continuously illuminated his sagely learning, and the many fine gentlemen (jishi) longed to show devotion to the Son of Heaven; the poet of the Odes drew a metaphor from the parasol tree (wutong) and the phoenix…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
凰之相感
皇上秉
冲睿
御經筵與二三賢碩講明治緒譬
之梧桐生于朝陽正諸生一
鳴之時也誠心切思媚以周
之吉士自待明正始之道端
===
向往之的不計夷險砥志礪
行上之寅亮天工次之弼成
世敎下之康濟生民務求底
績毋棄實以釣名則由茂俊
躋賢聖皆自一念致之而匡
廬名山彭蠡巨匯且因以生
色固不止高風直氣如倫輩
punctuated: 凰之相感。皇上秉冲睿，御經筵，與二三賢碩講明治緒，譬之梧桐生于朝陽，正諸生一鳴之時也。誠心切思媚，以周之吉士自待，明正始之道，端向往之的，不計夷險，砥志礪行，上之寅亮天工，次之弼成世敎，下之康濟生民，務求底績，毋棄實以釣名；則由茂俊躋賢聖，皆自一念致之，而匡廬名山、彭蠡巨匯且因以生色，固不止高風直氣如倫輩
translation_en: … and the phoenix responding to one another. His Majesty, endowed with youthful sagacity, presides over the Classics Colloquium, discussing and clarifying the threads of governance with a few worthy and eminent ministers. Likened to the wutong tree growing toward the morning sun, this is precisely the time for the candidates to sing out as the phoenix does. If you truly take to heart that earnest desire to serve the sovereign with devotion, hold yourselves to the standard of the fine officers of the Zhou, clarify the Way of rectifying beginnings, and set straight the target of your aspirations; if, without regard for smooth or perilous paths, you temper your resolve and whet your conduct—at the highest level reverently assisting in the work of Heaven, next aiding in the perfection of the moral instruction of the age, and at the fundamental level bringing peace and relief to the common people—striving always to achieve real results and never abandoning substance to fish for fame; then ascending from men of outstanding talent to the ranks of worthies and sages will all be brought about by this single thought. Even the famed mountains of Kuanglu (Mount Lu) and the vast waters of Pengli (Poyang Lake) will thereby gain luster, and your achievements will surely not stop merely at the lofty integrity and upright spirit of your predecessors…

title: 萬曆四年江西鄉試錄
text:
爾矣繼是尚論江右多賢歸
重今丙子榜豈惟嗣徽先哲
不佞亦有光焉
河南南陽府泌陽縣儒學敎
諭鄭卿謹序
punctuated:
爾矣。繼是尚論江右多賢，歸重今丙子榜，豈惟嗣徽先哲，不佞亦有光焉。
河南南陽府泌陽縣儒學敎諭鄭卿謹序。
translation_en:
…alone. Hereafter, when commentators appraise the past and remark that Jiangxi has produced an abundance of worthies, placing special weight on the roster of this Bingzi year (1576), you will not only carry on the fine legacy of the former sages, but I, though unworthy, shall also share in the glory.

Respectfully written as a postface by Zheng Qing 鄭卿, Instructor of the Confucian School of Biyang County, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan.
